LS5vJts4So.one_liner: Plans over subgoal sequences with a Geometric Horizon Model learned online, scoring plans by a learned terminal success probability
LS5vJts4So.problem: Sparse feedback makes long-horizon behaviors hard to discover in online goal-conditioned RL, and existing Geometric Policy Composition methods assume fixed, pretrained policies and world models.
LS5vJts4So.method: OGPC plans over short subgoal sequences to guide exploration while learning the policy and its world model online from scratch, using a Geometric Horizon Model to predict which states the policy reaches per subgoal and chaining those predictions. It replaces the final sampled reward in the Monte Carlo estimator with a learned estimate of its conditional success probability.
LS5vJts4So.key_idea: Chain Geometric Horizon Model predictions over subgoals and replace the Monte Carlo final sampled reward with a learned estimate of terminal success probability.
LS5vJts4So.evidence: Nine JaxGCRL tasks including high-dimensional Humanoid environments, compared with a depth-scaled Contrastive RL policy, including evaluation without planning; the paper claims better sample efficiency and final performance.
LS5vJts4So.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find it tackles an important problem (jointly learning policies and their occupancies under sparse rewards), is well written, and rigorously shows that the conditional terminal estimator reduces variance.
LS5vJts4So.main_concern: It is a direct extension of Jumpy World Models to online RL, and the learned estimator does not clearly outperform the Monte Carlo version in 5 of 9 environments.

RhguGj6A66.one_liner: 4D physics benchmark from real multiview scenes with simulated dense annotations, evaluating 57 VLMs and 10 VFMs on Newtonian reasoning
RhguGj6A66.problem: Existing physics benchmarks use synthetic or semi-synthetic scenes and emphasize high-level events, lacking the visual fidelity needed to assess low-level Newtonian understanding.
RhguGj6A66.method: NewtPhys is a 4D dataset built from multiview images of real-world scenes with physics-grounded simulations, providing dense per-timestep annotations including 3D forces and amodal per-pixel quantities covering physics, tracking, semantics and geometry.
RhguGj6A66.key_idea: Reconstruct real scenes (3D Gaussian splats per reviewers) and run physics-grounded simulation to obtain dense ground-truth physical quantities for question answering and probing.
RhguGj6A66.evidence: Evaluation of 57 VLMs (54 open and 3 frontier closed models) and 10 VFMs, including physics-probing experiments and appendix ablations.
RhguGj6A66.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find it a useful, well-documented benchmark with rich dense annotations and a broad evaluation of both VLMs and VFMs.
RhguGj6A66.main_concern: Label validity is weakly established: question answerability from the visual input is not validated against humans, and simulated dynamics are not compared with real-world measurements.

41sUHtGTDc.one_liner: Perturbation, evidence-conflict and probing tests show biological reasoning models often ignore foundation-model inputs and follow text instead.
41sUHtGTDc.problem: Benchmark accuracy of biological reasoning models is taken as evidence that the LLM reasons over its biological inputs, but that assumption is untested.
41sUHtGTDc.method: Tests six biological reasoning models on DNA, protein and single-cell tasks by perturbing one biological input while holding the rest fixed, pairing one entity's foundation-model representation with another's text (evidence conflicts), fitting linear probes on representations the LLM receives, and analyzing reasoning traces against inputs.
41sUHtGTDc.key_idea: Controlled input perturbation and representation-text evidence conflicts reveal which input the model actually uses, separate from what linear probes show the representation encodes.
41sUHtGTDc.evidence: Six models (including BioReason, BioReason-Pro and C2S-Scale) tested with perturbations, evidence conflicts, linear probes on Evo2 and ESM3 representations, and reasoning-trace analysis.
41sUHtGTDc.claimed_gains: Shuffling the DNA sequence barely changes BioReason disease prediction accuracy, and in evidence conflicts the two models follow the text in 97.9% and 99.7% of cases.
41sUHtGTDc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is timely and the combination of perturbations, evidence conflicts and probes is more informative than accuracy alone, covering DNA, protein and single-cell models.
41sUHtGTDc.main_concern: Shuffled or resampled inputs may create out-of-distribution representations and the text may already hold the needed information, so small performance changes do not prove the model ignores the biological input.

FYCUwYTT6g.one_liner: On-policy self-distillation for MLLMs where the teacher sees textual object coordinates from procedural scenes and the student does not.
FYCUwYTT6g.problem: On-policy self-distillation for MLLMs is largely unexplored, and existing privileged-information approaches using image crops help only zoom-like tasks and need human grounding data or external teachers.
FYCUwYTT6g.method: The teacher receives textual, spatially grounded guidance identifying query-relevant visual elements, taken from procedurally generated scenes with automatic object identities and coordinates, and uses it to integrate evidence from multiple regions. The student, given only the image and question, learns to reproduce the teacher's behavior.
FYCUwYTT6g.key_idea: Give the teacher text hints listing relevant objects and coordinates from procedural scenes, and distill its on-policy behavior into the student without those hints.
FYCUwYTT6g.evidence: Counting, document, and chart benchmarks across multiple models, with a 15-benchmark average on Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.5-9B, and Qwen3-VL-4B, and transfer to real-image tasks despite synthetic-only post-training.
FYCUwYTT6g.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the synthetic-to-real transfer is useful and empirically interesting, with 15-benchmark average gains of 4.45, 1.76, and 1.01 points on Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.5-9B, and Qwen3-VL-4B.
FYCUwYTT6g.main_concern: Hint ablations do not isolate correct spatial coordinates from answer-bearing structure, since the enumerated hint list still reveals the count, and there is no direct comparison with the closely related ViCuR.

SfJkTpXA6p.one_liner: IDRF reward-fine-tunes few-step masked discrete diffusion models with an inverse-distillation penalty that upper-bounds sequence-level KL to the reference.
SfJkTpXA6p.problem: Masked discrete diffusion models need costly iterative sampling, and intractable sequence likelihoods complicate reward fine-tuning with a KL penalty.
SfJkTpXA6p.method: IDRF replaces the intractable sequence-level KL penalty with inverse-distillation regularization, optimized through a trajectory-based surrogate without reference-model rollouts. Reward is optimized with a policy gradient over the student's own rollouts, whose probability can be computed exactly.
SfJkTpXA6p.key_idea: Regularize reward fine-tuning with a trajectory-based inverse-distillation loss that, with an optimal auxiliary denoiser, upper-bounds the sequence-level KL to the reference.
SfJkTpXA6p.evidence: A proof that the population inverse-distillation loss upper-bounds sequence-level KL, and experiments on DNA, image, and text generation.
SfJkTpXA6p.claimed_gains: IDRF achieves high reward with up to 32x fewer denoising steps than the reference while mitigating reward hacking and preserving sample quality.
SfJkTpXA6p.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the results are strong at small step budgets across tasks and that the sequence-level justification for inverse-distillation regularization is principled.
SfJkTpXA6p.main_concern: The method largely builds on IDLM as a regularizer inside a policy gradient, and comparisons are not step-matched or matched against alternative regularization strategies.

1uyaxcgGV9.one_liner: Latent operator trained on Eulerian fluid fields that gives Lagrangian particle rollout zero-shot by querying velocities at particle positions.
1uyaxcgGV9.problem: Lagrangian trajectories are scarcer than Eulerian fields and most neural operators train and evaluate in the Eulerian view, so it is unknown whether an Eulerian-only model can roll out particles zero-shot.
1uyaxcgGV9.method: TLO decouples latent flow evolution from coordinate-dependent decoding: querying the evolving latent at fixed coordinates yields Eulerian fields, while querying velocities at particle positions and recursively updating those positions gives Lagrangian rollout. Reviews add that it uses a local-global patch representation and a Transolver-inspired processor.
1uyaxcgGV9.key_idea: Evolve one shared latent flow representation and decode it at either fixed grid coordinates or moving particle positions through coordinate-conditioned readout.
1uyaxcgGV9.evidence: Five fluid-dynamics benchmarks (2D and 3D, numerical simulation and ocean reanalysis per reviews) covering Eulerian forecasting, zero-shot Lagrangian rollout, and decoder fine-tuning with Lagrangian supervision.
1uyaxcgGV9.claimed_gains: Strong Eulerian forecasting accuracy and competitive zero-shot Lagrangian rollout across five benchmarks, with further gains from decoder fine-tuning; no figures stated.
1uyaxcgGV9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the Eulerian forecasting results strongest (lowest error on all five benchmarks) and the Eul/Ref/Path error decomposition informative, since lower grid error does not imply lower trajectory error.
1uyaxcgGV9.main_concern: The architecture is close to UPT and LNO, which already decode latents at arbitrary coordinates, and Transolver beats TLO on some Lagrangian metrics, leaving the contribution to zero-shot particle rollout unclear.

gv7mtzOYrY.one_liner: Pretrains LMs with a deep-to-shallow state feedback channel by teacher-forcing states derived from a pretrained LM's next-token distribution.
gv7mtzOYrY.problem: Feed-forward Transformer LMs never feed deep-layer representations back to shallower layers, so across generation steps information flows only through the decoded token, forcing recomputation and loss of alternative continuations.
gv7mtzOYrY.method: LIFT pairs each input token with an information-dense state derived from an off-the-shelf pretrained LM's next-token distribution and trains the model, with a small number of extra parameters, to predict both the next token and the next state. Pretraining stays parallel because input states are precomputed, and at inference the model's own predicted states are fed back.
gv7mtzOYrY.key_idea: Turn recurrent-state learning into teacher-forced prediction of precomputed states from a pretrained LM, so a feedback channel is trained fully in parallel.
gv7mtzOYrY.evidence: Pretrained models from 135M to 1B parameters on language modeling, downstream reasoning tasks, and procedural tasks under a token-matched budget (S5 permutation and arithmetic per reviews).
gv7mtzOYrY.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms standard Transformers and baselines on language modeling, downstream reasoning, and procedural tasks under a token-matched budget, with a minor inference overhead that decreases with model size; no figures stated.
gv7mtzOYrY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find teacher-forcing the state channel a simple, parallel-trainable way to get feedback, with gains over Jacobi-style baselines at matched compute across 135M to 1B scales.
gv7mtzOYrY.main_concern: Most of the gain over compute-matched Transformers comes from a stronger teacher whose pretraining cost is not counted, and the reasoning claims rest mainly on likelihood (bits-per-byte) rather than task accuracy.

TzSkIXINcJ.one_liner: A vision-language-action policy that separates persistent tactile context from gated, selective tactile action refinement.
TzSkIXINcJ.problem: Tactile information should not influence control uniformly: persistent tactile context represents contact state, while local action refinement should be applied selectively.
TzSkIXINcJ.method: TCR-ARM derives two tactile interfaces from a shared encoder: compact tactile representations give persistent VLM context and future latent prediction, while dense tactile features update wrist visual tokens through a learned gate. Route-aware tactile pretraining (RAT) samples no-tactile, context-only, and full-tactile routes.
TzSkIXINcJ.key_idea: Train tactile context to work with and without tactile-driven refinement by sampling no-tactile, context-only, and full-tactile routes during pretraining, while a learned gate updates wrist visual tokens.
TzSkIXINcJ.evidence: Pretraining on 1,500 hours of tactile manipulation data, post-training with 100 demonstrations per task, and six real-world contact-rich tasks with 20 trials each, with ablations over routes, gating, and dropout strategies.
TzSkIXINcJ.claimed_gains: Achieves 70.3% average success across six real-world contact-rich tasks, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline by 15.9 (abstract truncated).
TzSkIXINcJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the context-versus-refinement distinction well motivated and implemented through complementary representations, with extensive real-robot ablations showing RAT helps.
TzSkIXINcJ.main_concern: The main comparison confounds architecture with 1,500 hours of extra tactile pretraining that baselines lack, and each condition uses only 20 trials per task without seed variability.

mHOeqQAdql.one_liner: Trains hierarchical almost-linear RNNs on 100 cognitive tasks to study when tasks transfer or interfere.
mHOeqQAdql.problem: It is unclear how tasks interact in recurrent networks as multitask batteries grow in scale and heterogeneity, and how this relates to task complexity and model structure.
mHOeqQAdql.method: Trains hierarchical Almost-Linear RNNs (AL-RNNs) jointly on 100 tasks, varying recurrent nonlinearity and task-feature dimensionality, then analyzes task features, state geometry, and nonlinear-region usage as measures of task similarity.
mHOeqQAdql.key_idea: Hierarchical task features give each task its own parameters inside a shared low-dimensional subspace, and AL-RNNs allow nonlinearity in recurrence to be varied independently of state dimension.
mHOeqQAdql.evidence: Joint training on 100 cognitive tasks compared with individually trained models and an unstructured joint model, plus pairwise transfer and leave-one-out adaptation experiments.
mHOeqQAdql.claimed_gains: The joint hierarchical model outperforms both individually trained models and a single unstructured joint model; no accuracy numbers are stated in the abstract.
mHOeqQAdql.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the unusually large and heterogeneous task battery and the analyses linking task features, state geometry, and nonlinear usage to transfer.
mHOeqQAdql.main_concern: Claims of shared computation exceed what the architecture supports since each task has distinct recurrent parameters, and the joint-versus-individual comparison uses unequal training epochs (3,000 versus 500).

jIYf5Wz8b4.one_liner: Retrieval-based genomic language model that removes alignment gaps and uses column indices as RoPE positions, scaling context 100x.
jIYf5Wz8b4.problem: MSA-based genomic language models are efficient but limited to short input contexts, restricting them to short-range tasks such as variant effect prediction, while standard gLMs need very large compute.
jIYf5Wz8b4.method: RAGenome removes gap tokens from whole-genome alignments of 100 vertebrates, keeps alignment column indices as RoPE positions to preserve cross-species correspondence, and concatenates sampled species under a fixed retrieval budget with taxonomy embeddings. The 168M-parameter model combines within-species sliding-window attention with cross-species attention.
jIYf5Wz8b4.key_idea: Removes gap tokens and keeps alignment column indices as RoPE positions, so token count stops scaling with length times species while cross-species correspondence is preserved.
jIYf5Wz8b4.evidence: Pretrained on whole-genome alignments from 100 vertebrates and evaluated on two tasks: BEND gene finding and ClinVar variant effect prediction.
jIYf5Wz8b4.claimed_gains: Raises gene finding performance from 0.45 to 0.60 over MSA-based gLMs with 100x longer context, while remaining competitive on pathogenic variant prioritization.
jIYf5Wz8b4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that gap removal with alignment-index RoPE positions is a simple, practical fix that scales alignment-based models while keeping the evolutionary signal.
jIYf5Wz8b4.main_concern: Evaluation is too narrow (only gene finding and ClinVar, no run-to-run variance), and context length is confounded with genome coverage and retrieval budget in Table 3.

Vqq8ZO7yui.one_liner: Prefills chat and agentic trajectories with synthetic mistakes to measure whether LLMs disclose or knowingly conceal them.
Vqq8ZO7yui.problem: As LLM agents act with little oversight, users depend on them to report mistakes, but it is unclear whether current models disclose or conceal their errors.
Vqq8ZO7yui.method: The authors prefill trajectories resembling real chat and agentic deployments with synthetic mistakes, then judge disclosure behavior and chain-of-thought awareness across seven frontier models, with a capability control checking that models can spot the mistake when reviewing the transcript.
Vqq8ZO7yui.key_idea: Separates failing to notice a planted mistake (chain-of-thought judge) from noticing it yet staying silent (behavioral judge), with a capability control ruling out inability.
Vqq8ZO7yui.evidence: Prefilled-mistake rollouts in chat and agentic settings across seven frontier models, using separate CoT and response judges, deterministic replayed environments, and cluster-bootstrapped confidence intervals (per reviews).
Vqq8ZO7yui.claimed_gains: Diagnostic study, no method gains: models fail to disclose or hint at the mistake in 17.6% of chat and 64.6% of agentic rollouts, and knowingly conceal it in 2.4% and 5.3% respectively.
Vqq8ZO7yui.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is carefully built, with deterministic environments, separate judges for noticing and disclosure, and a capability control that isolates deception from inability.
Vqq8ZO7yui.main_concern: Headline concealment numbers may be overstated or judge-driven (deception cells are small, judges lack human validation, hints and stated correct facts count as non-disclosure), and prefilled rather than self-generated mistakes may distort behavior.

WoWPD7sfty.one_liner: Proves that recognizing original-coordinate, log-coordinate, and log-log convexity of signomials is strongly NP-hard, via polynomial-to-signomial reductions.
WoWPD7sfty.problem: Signomial optimization is intractable in general and convexity offers three routes to tractability, but the complexity of recognizing each form of convexity is not established.
WoWPD7sfty.method: Starts from gap-promise variants of polynomial convexity and builds polynomial-to-signomial reductions that preserve curvature gaps under the relevant logarithmic transformations, covering compact domains and global settings with positivity ensured in the log-log case.
WoWPD7sfty.key_idea: Reductions from gap-promise polynomial convexity to signomials that preserve curvature gaps under the log-coordinate and log-log transformations.
WoWPD7sfty.evidence: Theoretical proofs of strong NP-hardness on compact domains and globally; motivation cites 45 of 100 AI Feynman equations admitting signomial representations.
WoWPD7sfty.claimed_gains: Shows strong NP-hardness for all three convexity forms on compact sets and globally; no empirical gains.
WoWPD7sfty.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the hardness results are new, clearly stated, and technically sound, with clever reductions that go beyond existing polynomial results.
WoWPD7sfty.main_concern: Relevance to ML and ICLR is unclear: no concrete ML example shows why recognizing signomial convexity matters, and there is no link to learning theory.

DZzSJxqJKA.one_liner: A noisy quadratic model of training dynamics attributes diffusion LM training inefficiency to poorer learned features, not gradient noise.
DZzSJxqJKA.problem: Diffusion language models need far longer training than autoregressive models to reach the same held-out loss despite sharing a Bayes-optimal objective value, and the cause is disputed.
DZzSJxqJKA.method: The authors test three proposed explanations (gradient noise, competition among corruptions, hard prediction problems) with a noisy quadratic model of training dynamics, and design Surface Sudoku, a Sudoku variant with latent digits, to separate limited expressivity from failure to learn good features.
DZzSJxqJKA.key_idea: Compares the attainable loss decrease supported by each model's features at matched loss, showing DLM features permit less reduction, with high-rate corruptions carrying most uncorrectable loss.
DZzSJxqJKA.evidence: Noisy quadratic analysis comparing DLMs and ARMs (reviews mention TinyGSM at one small scale) and the Surface Sudoku benchmark, where an auxiliary objective supervising latent digits narrows the gap.
DZzSJxqJKA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is important and the experiments are clean and carefully designed, praising the noisy quadratic decomposition and Surface Sudoku.
DZzSJxqJKA.main_concern: Experiments are at a single small scale on TinyGSM (where conflicts are absent by design), and the feature-learning-deficiency interpretation is not separated from alternatives such as expressivity or kernel-task alignment.

PARqAJvRPF.one_liner: Generates conjectures by small structural edits to known theorems and selects them with Hard Neighbours, outperforming Minimo's learned conjecturer.
PARqAJvRPF.problem: Self-play provers like Minimo reward conjectures for being hard to prove, but harder conjectures are not necessarily more useful for improving a prover, and the learned conjecturer drifts toward long, artificial statements.
PARqAJvRPF.method: In a controlled single-round Peano setting, conjectures come from small structural edits to statements the prover already knows and are scored by how much a fixed prover improves on held-out theorems after training on their proofs. Hard Neighbours (HN) favors conjectures whose proof difficulty grows disproportionately relative to their structural distance from easier statements.
PARqAJvRPF.key_idea: Edits statements the prover already knows to generate conjectures, then selects those whose proof difficulty grows disproportionately relative to structural distance from easier neighbors.
PARqAJvRPF.evidence: Controlled single-round experiments in the Peano formal environment across propositional logic, abelian groups, and natural-number multiplication, at equal training budget under best-first search.
PARqAJvRPF.claimed_gains: Structural-edit conjectures improve the prover by 6 to 13 percentage points more than Minimo's learned conjectures at equal training budget, and the gain holds even for random draws from the generated pool.
PARqAJvRPF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the finding that simple perturbation beats a learned conjecturer is surprising and supported by a rigorous controlled comparison with Minimo, with a sensible usefulness-based view of conjecture value.
PARqAJvRPF.main_concern: Results cover only a single round in a small Peano setting, so efficacy inside an iterative self-play loop is unvalidated, and the HN formulation is narrow and weakly justified.

CX1Xxj5mJ8.one_liner: Two permutation tests on stored responses separate winner's-curse inflation from real policy specialization in oracle reliability-coverage gaps.
CX1Xxj5mJ8.problem: An oracle choosing the best policy per problem looks much stronger than any single policy partly because taking the largest estimated success rate also selects favorable sampling errors.
CX1Xxj5mJ8.method: The first test redistributes stored correctness outcomes across policies within each problem; the second also preserves each policy's total successes to account for overall quality differences under a specified statistical model. Both run on stored responses before any router is trained.
CX1Xxj5mJ8.key_idea: A permutation null that redistributes correctness outcomes across policies within each problem, optionally preserving each policy's total successes, to calibrate how much oracle gap sampling noise alone produces.
CX1Xxj5mJ8.evidence: Five training seeds of a seven-billion-parameter vision-language model, policies trained on different datasets, light versus stronger post-training recipes, plus power simulations, positive controls, and router, mixture, voting, and weight-averaging baselines.
CX1Xxj5mJ8.claimed_gains: At threshold 0.10 the estimated oracle gap is 0.113 and redistributed outcomes alone give 0.096 on average; neither test finds significant evidence of specialization at this threshold.
CX1Xxj5mJ8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper usefully separates estimated oracle gap, population specialization, and deployable routing gain, backed by careful statistical controls such as power simulations and positive controls.
CX1Xxj5mJ8.main_concern: Presentation is dense with many closely related terms, and non-rejection is weakly decisive (about 50% power against a population gap near five points) with experiments limited to one model, LoRA-based GRPO, and two datasets.

MAiXYYMfGy.one_liner: Large language-action model with a unified human-humanoid motion vocabulary, fine-tuned with motion chain-of-thought SFT then physics-feedback RL.
MAiXYYMfGy.problem: Humanoids following free-form language commands are limited by scarce paired language-humanoid motion data and physical instability, with existing methods confined to simple instructions or trading motion diversity for physical plausibility.
MAiXYYMfGy.method: Humanoid-LLA learns a unified human-humanoid motion vocabulary, then fine-tunes in two stages: supervised motion chain-of-thought learning followed by reinforcement learning refined with physical feedback.
MAiXYYMfGy.key_idea: Tokenizes human and humanoid motion in one shared vocabulary so a language model emits motion tokens executed directly by a controller, then refines with physics-feedback RL.
MAiXYYMfGy.evidence: Simulation and real-world experiments with comparisons to existing methods and ablations; reviews cite Table 2, where RL fine-tuning raises success from 68.64% (SFT-only) to 87.6% and lowers MPJPE from 78.31 to 56.43 mm.
MAiXYYMfGy.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract (it claims superior generalization, diverse motion generation, and high physical fidelity); reviews cite success rising from 68.64% to 87.6% after RL fine-tuning.
MAiXYYMfGy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation is comprehensive (baselines, ablations, real-world tests) and that physical-feedback RL gives substantial execution gains.
MAiXYYMfGy.main_concern: The method contribution is seen as incremental over prior language-driven humanoid motion systems, and ablations do not isolate structured CoT reasoning from richer supervision or quantify the benefit of extra human-only data.

mceBV2YUv4.one_liner: Benchmark of 24 flow-field question families that scores LLM agents on analysis validity, finding recall, and consistency
mceBV2YUv4.problem: Evaluating LLM agents on scientific questions about flow fields is hard because different valid analyses can yield different findings from the same data.
mceBV2YUv4.method: FlowIntentBench has 24 question families over 15 flow-field datasets, each instantiated in four conditions that vary which analysis decisions the question specifies, and each paired with accepted operationalizations and the findings each yields. Responses are scored on validity of the stated analysis, recall of required findings, and consistency between findings and operationalization.
mceBV2YUv4.key_idea: Vary how many analysis decisions the question prescribes while pairing each accepted operationalization with its executed findings, so scoring tolerates multiple valid analyses.
mceBV2YUv4.evidence: Nine tool-using LLM agents evaluated across the four conditions on 15 flow-field datasets.
mceBV2YUv4.claimed_gains: Across nine agents, mean validity falls from 0.846 to 0.742 and recall from 0.910 to 0.863 when all principal analysis decisions are left to the agent.
mceBV2YUv4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled task-family design that separates prescribed analysis from agent-chosen analysis and ties numerical findings to the analytical choices that produced them.
mceBV2YUv4.main_concern: Scores depend on frozen reference evidence and a non-deterministic LLM evaluator, with few stored reference branches and a scope limited to flow fields.

8DjmmLUDAy.one_liner: Bilinear autoencoders decompose activations into low-rank quadratic latents to find multi-dimensional manifolds in language models
8DjmmLUDAy.problem: Sparse autoencoders use linear latents, so concepts that span manifolds cannot be captured without post hoc analysis.
8DjmmLUDAy.method: Implements quadratic latents as bilinear autoencoders that decompose activations into low-rank quadratic forms, compose linearly in weight space, and admit input-independent geometric analysis. Reviewers also mention a kernel trick as a technique that makes the framework feasible.
8DjmmLUDAy.key_idea: Replace linear SAE latents with low-rank quadratic forms of the input, so each latent spans a multi-dimensional geometry analyzable by matrix decomposition.
8DjmmLUDAy.evidence: Experiments and visualisations on language-model activations (reviewers cite a TopK baseline at K = 32), a comparison of autoencoders with different geometric priors, and an interactive visualizer for Qwen 3.5.
8DjmmLUDAy.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims systematically improved reconstruction error in language models, without figures)
8DjmmLUDAy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the principled extension of the linear representation hypothesis, an explicit architecture analyzable with geometric tools, and evaluation on real LLM activations.
8DjmmLUDAy.main_concern: The comparison with TopK SAEs is thin (single K = 32, no compute cost-benefit) and it is unclear whether the manifolds are new structure beyond what SAEs already encode.

5aMUZIy1hu.one_liner: Computes epsilon-exact Shapley values for product games by Gauss-Legendre quadrature of a degree d-1 polynomial integral.
5aMUZIy1hu.problem: Exact Shapley computation sums over exponentially many coalitions, which is intractable even for models whose coalition values factorize multiplicatively across players.
5aMUZIy1hu.method: For a d-player product game the coalition sum becomes a one-dimensional integral of a polynomial of degree at most d-1, evaluated with Gauss-Legendre quadrature using ceil(d/2) nodes for exactness. A computable factor-dependent error bound sets the node budget for a given tolerance before evaluation, and computations are shared across features in log-space with sign tracking.
5aMUZIy1hu.key_idea: Rewrite the product-game Shapley coalition sum as a one-dimensional polynomial integral and evaluate it with Gauss-Legendre nodes sized by an a priori error bound.
5aMUZIy1hu.evidence: Proofs of exactness at epsilon=0 and a geometrically decaying error bound, applied to log-link regression, Cox, odds-scale classifiers, product-kernel machines, and tree models, with float32 checks in the appendix per reviews.
5aMUZIy1hu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is well written and gives a practical speedup for Shapley computation on product games, with a useful computable a priori error certificate and broad model coverage.
5aMUZIy1hu.main_concern: Novelty is limited because the tools are known (TreeGrad and Quadrature SHAP use similar Gauss-Legendre integration) and the main bound (Proposition 3) is not hard to obtain.

QXmQw7NQAJ.one_liner: MEF-VLA trains VLA models to predict remaining motion (event-flow) until the next interaction event, with adaptive horizons.
QXmQw7NQAJ.problem: Fixed-horizon, full-frame visual foresight gives inconsistent guidance on task progress in multi-stage manipulation, and leaves spatial change implicit.
QXmQw7NQAJ.method: Event frames marking upcoming interactions define adaptive prediction horizons, and remaining event-flow encodes motion toward them as spatial displacement. Learned event queries predict remaining-motion features and condition the action expert.
QXmQw7NQAJ.key_idea: Supervise the VLA with learned event queries that predict state-dependent remaining motion (event-flow) toward the next interaction event frame, instead of fixed-horizon future frames.
QXmQw7NQAJ.evidence: Simulation on LIBERO, zero-shot LIBERO-Plus, and CALVIN five-task sequences, plus held-out physical three-stage instructions; matched ablations on horizon and representation.
QXmQw7NQAJ.claimed_gains: Improves success over the vanilla VLA by 1.6 percentage points on LIBERO, 8.9 on zero-shot LIBERO-Plus, and 9.0 on five-task sequences in CALVIN.
QXmQw7NQAJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the decomposition into which future to predict and what to represent is clear, with matched ablations and negligible inference overhead.
QXmQw7NQAJ.main_concern: Gains are not cleanly attributed, since the vanilla baseline lacks event queries and generic auxiliary supervision may explain much of the improvement.

n0XOBB3P8K.one_liner: ProxMAR corrects neural proximal causal estimators for missing outcome proxies using imputation, inverse probability weighting, and augmented weighting.
n0XOBB3P8K.problem: Neural proximal causal estimators assume fully observed proxies, and complete-case analysis distorts bridge learning and causal-mean estimation when proxies are missing at random.
n0XOBB3P8K.method: Conditional-mean imputation, IPW, and AIPW are applied to the estimator-specific functions for bridge learning and causal-mean evaluation, instantiated with NMMR and DFPV for three variants each.
n0XOBB3P8K.key_idea: Apply missingness corrections (conditional-mean imputation, IPW, AIPW) to the estimator-specific functions used in bridge learning and averaging, instead of imputing high-dimensional proxy values.
n0XOBB3P8K.evidence: Observed-data recovery identities, a product-remainder identity for double robustness, and consistency proofs under method-specific conditions; experiments with NMMR and DFPV variants.
n0XOBB3P8K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the missing-proxy problem is practically relevant and that the unified framework has solid theory with consistency guarantees.
n0XOBB3P8K.main_concern: Consistency assumptions are not shown to hold for the implemented kernel-regression and neural estimators, and the method depends on the missing-at-random assumption.

DDylDVKez5.one_liner: Shows LoRA layer-importance scores change under function-preserving reparameterization, and uniform full-depth low-rank LoRA wins at matched budgets.
DDylDVKez5.problem: Layer selection for LoRA assumes pretrained-model importance scores are meaningful, but they may depend on internal coordinates rather than the layers' usefulness.
DDylDVKez5.method: A capacity-preserving audit applies function-preserving transformations that keep the LoRA function set fixed, then measures adaptation value on the original backbone and compares static placements, AdaLoRA, and FoRA at matched budgets.
DDylDVKez5.key_idea: Apply function-preserving reparameterizations that leave the LoRA function set unchanged to test whether layer-selection scores are invariant, then compare allocation schemes at matched adapter parameters.
DDylDVKez5.evidence: Gradient-based selection across architectures and calibration tasks, random placement controls, five-seed tests, an 8B extension, and matched parameter, step, and learning-rate-search comparisons.
DDylDVKez5.claimed_gains: Full-depth uniform low-rank LoRA gets the highest accuracy in matched comparisons, at about 1.3 to 1.6 times the training time of a quarter-depth placement and up to about a quarter more peak memory.
DDylDVKez5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the fixed-placement audit and original-backbone evaluation are systematic and unusually detailed about budgets and controls.
DDylDVKez5.main_concern: Matching final adapter size does not match training time or memory, so the full-depth recommendation may not hold under practical budgets.

wDgx4gxcxR.one_liner: Proves clipped AdamW beats SGD and AdaGrad for stochastic convex optimization when gradients grow with the optimality gap.
wDgx4gxcxR.problem: Non-smooth optimization theory assumes uniformly bounded gradients, which is unrealistic and cannot explain AdamW's advantage.
wDgx4gxcxR.method: The paper defines generalized Lipschitz functions with gradient norm bounded by an affine function of the optimality gap, and analyzes convergence of SGD, AdaGrad, and clipped AdamW, including preconditioned and quasar-convex extensions.
wDgx4gxcxR.key_idea: Under affine gradient growth in the optimality gap, exponentially weighted gradient accumulation with clipped updates avoids the poor rates of simple averaging.
wDgx4gxcxR.evidence: Convergence theory for several algorithms under generalized Lipschitz and generalized smoothness assumptions; reviewers note there are no experiments.
wDgx4gxcxR.claimed_gains: Clipped AdamW provably outperforms SGD and AdaGrad; the abstract states no numeric rates.
wDgx4gxcxR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory is comprehensive, with a nontrivial separation from SGD and AdaGrad and a useful analysis of AdamW's exponential averaging.
wDgx4gxcxR.main_concern: Connection to practical deep learning is limited: the results are mainly convex or quasar-convex and have no experiments supporting the assumption.

skuMwCVqP9.one_liner: Looped Prediction Transformer: only the first recursion writes the KV cache; later recursions read it plus a short local window.
skuMwCVqP9.problem: Each recursion of a looped transformer writes its own key-value cache, so memory still grows with compute, and inference-time cache shrinking costs quality.
skuMwCVqP9.method: Looped language models are pretrained so only the first recursion writes a cache while later recursions read it and keep a short window of their own. A hybrid variant is also built.
skuMwCVqP9.key_idea: Pretrain looped models with a single shared KV cache written by the first recursion, which later recursions attend to alongside a short local window.
skuMwCVqP9.evidence: Pretraining at 150M-1B parameters evaluated by FineWeb-Edu validation perplexity, with analyses of shared versus local memory representations; reviews note 4,096-token contexts and short zero-shot tasks.
skuMwCVqP9.claimed_gains: With five recursions, the hybrid lowers FineWeb-Edu validation perplexity by 1.12-1.82 relative to a same-size standard Transformer while using 76-79% less context memory.
skuMwCVqP9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design is simple, cuts KV memory without losing quality, and comes with insightful analysis of why sharing helps.
skuMwCVqP9.main_concern: Evidence is limited to small models and 4,096-token contexts with no long-range retrieval test or FLOP-matched baseline, and the LPT-versus-LT comparison also changes the training objective.

i4s0c7y3VM.one_liner: Defines a behavioral rate R-star: the smallest serialized compressed LoRA adapter retaining a fixed fraction of held-out fine-tuning gain.
i4s0c7y3VM.problem: Adapter rank, parameter count, and reconstruction error do not tell how many bits are needed to preserve the behavior acquired by fine-tuning.
i4s0c7y3VM.method: Compresses LoRA adapters and measures the smallest serialized size whose reloaded adapter keeps a fixed fraction of the held-out gain, then compares rates across datasets and frozen base models and tests whether correction spectra measured on the data can rank them.
i4s0c7y3VM.key_idea: Measure fine-tuning information as the bits of the smallest compressed adapter that preserves held-out gain, making compressibility a property of the dataset-receiver pair.
i4s0c7y3VM.evidence: LoRA fine-tuning experiments across datasets and frozen base models, codec comparisons, and compression-recovery experiments with adapters trained on corrupted data evaluated on GSM8K.
i4s0c7y3VM.claimed_gains: Adapters trained on deliberately corrupted datasets go from 23.7% to 82.9% on GSM8K after compression, versus 77.6% for a reference cut off in the truncated abstract.
i4s0c7y3VM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the receiver-specific view of fine-tuning information interesting and the corrupted-data compression recovery a surprising, well-tested effect.
i4s0c7y3VM.main_concern: The rate depends on the compression method, the retained-loss metric is not validated against downstream performance, and the claim that compression filters harmful directions is not separated from simple shrinkage.

bFwbBJ7u0m.one_liner: Distributed multi-GPU PDLP using two-dimensional partitioning, load balancing, and a PDLP-specific cost model for resource selection.
bFwbBJ7u0m.problem: PDHG-based LP solvers perform well on single GPUs, but computational throughput becomes a bottleneck for very large instances.
bFwbBJ7u0m.method: D-PDLP, built on cuPDLPx, distributes primal-dual computation across GPUs with two-dimensional partitioning and a load-balancing strategy, and a cost model relates computation and communication costs to processor-grid configuration and GPU count.
bFwbBJ7u0m.key_idea: Partition the constraint matrix across a 2D GPU grid with nonzero-aware load balancing so each iteration's two sparse matrix-vector products need only orthogonal AllReduce phases.
bFwbBJ7u0m.evidence: Standard LP benchmarks (MIPLIB, Mittelmann) and huge-scale real-world datasets on up to eight GPUs, with case studies testing the cost model.
bFwbBJ7u0m.claimed_gains: Approximately 6x speedup on eight GPUs for computationally intensive instances while maintaining numerical accuracy.
bFwbBJ7u0m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a complete distributed PDHG design with a useful load-balancing study, strong speedups on large sparse instances, and strict-accuracy checks.
bFwbBJ7u0m.main_concern: The contribution is limited: the scheme tiles standard SpMV across GPUs, tests use only eight GPUs on one node, partitioning is heuristic and single-seed, and gains concentrate on very large instances.

OhIFmmrsXg.one_liner: JEPA world model with DISReg, a regularizer predicting difference-image embeddings to keep dynamic features from collapsing.
OhIFmmrsXg.problem: Standard JEPA training favors slow features, causing feature suppression and latent collapse, while inverse dynamics needs action labels and gives little incentive to embed general unlabeled dynamics.
OhIFmmrsXg.method: DISReg adds an inverse-dynamics-style module that predicts temporal difference-image embeddings without pixel reconstruction, with a static term shaping the image-embedding distribution and a dynamic term that only requires dynamic features to be present. Integrated into a standard JEPA it forms MotionJEPA.
OhIFmmrsXg.key_idea: Predict embeddings of temporal difference images from frame embeddings as an auxiliary target, so dynamic features are required without constraining the embedding's shape or distribution.
OhIFmmrsXg.evidence: Controlled synthetic environments with independently sampled state factors, nonlinear and linear probes, trajectory-straightness analysis, planning evaluations, and BridgeData, against tuned baselines and a random-initialization baseline.
OhIFmmrsXg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled analysis clearly exposes selective feature suppression and that the difference-image idea is clear and convincingly evaluated against tuned baselines with probing and planning tests.
OhIFmmrsXg.main_concern: Reviewers say the gain is not isolated from the added auxiliary encoder and capacity (no matched individual-image-target control or parameter and compute reporting), and robustness to camera motion and moving distractors is untested.

cx6FU2U8kh.one_liner: Neural PDE solver that learns two-sided interface states inside a finite-volume update with prescribed numerical fluxes.
cx6FU2U8kh.problem: Learned PDE solvers that predict full state transitions do not exploit the finite-volume reconstruction–flux–update structure or its local balance.
cx6FU2U8kh.method: FV-GNO uses a graph network to decode effective two-sided interface states, while prescribed numerical fluxes, source treatment, and geometric assembly advance the solution. It trains end to end on state observations alone without interface or flux labels and inherits local balance for arbitrary network parameters.
cx6FU2U8kh.key_idea: Learn only the interface reconstruction inside a fixed finite-volume update, keeping known numerical fluxes and geometric assembly so local balance holds by construction.
cx6FU2U8kh.evidence: Experiments on diverse nonlinear equations on regular and irregular meshes against neural baselines and second-order finite-volume schemes, plus coarse-grid pretraining for fine-grid prediction and a constructive representation analysis.
cx6FU2U8kh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper clearly separates learned from fixed components, is well motivated as a bridge between classical solvers and neural methods, and shows interesting few-shot cross-resolution fine-tuning results.
cx6FU2U8kh.main_concern: Reviewers say novelty and related work are insufficient, since learned face interpolation inside finite-volume solvers (Bar-Sinai et al., Kochkov et al.) and interface-predicting GNN work already exist, and the experiments do not isolate the benefit of learning interface values versus fluxes.

smdNDdHjnO.one_liner: Decomposes cybersecurity-agent trajectories into atomic verifiable tasks that cheaply predict model rankings on costly agentic benchmarks.
smdNDdHjnO.problem: End-to-end cybersecurity agent benchmarks are costly to run and give only a coarse measure of success with little visibility into the underlying operations.
smdNDdHjnO.method: The framework decomposes agent trajectories into recurring atomic tasks, organizes them into a trajectory-derived capability taxonomy, and converts each into an isolated evaluation with an independently verifiable answer, posed from a fixed trajectory state to avoid error propagation and full rollouts.
smdNDdHjnO.key_idea: Pose each recurring operation as an isolated question from a fixed trajectory state, so model ranking can be predicted without multi-turn rollouts.
smdNDdHjnO.evidence: 13 models evaluated on ExCyTIn and CTI-REALM, comparing atomic-task scores with full agentic performance and with uniformly sampled subsets, plus holdout results across eight model families (per reviews).
smdNDdHjnO.claimed_gains: Atomic-task scores correlate with full agentic performance at Spearman rho of about 0.9, and the prespecified 100-item proxy uses 11.6x fewer evaluation tokens on ExCyTIn and 8.5x fewer on CTI-REALM than uniformly sampled subsets at equal correlation.
smdNDdHjnO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the cost problem is real and that predicting agentic rankings from cheap, verifiable atomic tasks is a useful, complementary direction with positive ranking-recovery evidence.
smdNDdHjnO.main_concern: Reviewers say item quality and reporting are weak spots: a post-freeze audit recommended dropping 182 of 587 ExCyTIn items but was not applied, and exploratory 25-item savings are mixed with prespecified results.

eq5xCQFAxS.one_liner: Fuses heterogeneous VLMs using focal-diversity metrics, genetic-algorithm ensemble pruning, and a verification stage that resolves conflicting outputs.
eq5xCQFAxS.problem: Ensembling diverse vision-language models over both modalities is under-studied, and majority voting fails when there is no consensus or most models are wrong.
eq5xCQFAxS.method: V3Fusion measures complementarity with language-based focal error diversity and a Focal CKA metric on visual embeddings, prunes the VLM pool with a genetic algorithm, then picks the best combination per task and resolves output conflicts to capture epistemic uncertainty.
eq5xCQFAxS.key_idea: Select VLM subsets by focal error diversity plus CKA-based visual diversity, then fuse their outputs and use disagreement as an uncertainty signal to resolve conflicts.
eq5xCQFAxS.evidence: Multiple benchmarks (reviews mention MMMU, MMMU-Pro and OCR tasks, multiple-choice and open-ended) against ensemble baselines such as plurality voting and PairRanker, with ablations.
eq5xCQFAxS.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract (a review cites 56.09% on MMMU versus 54.95% for plurality voting).
eq5xCQFAxS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that VLMs show complementary errors, that the problem is practical, and that fusion results are competitive with ensemble baselines across benchmarks.
eq5xCQFAxS.main_concern: The diversity metrics are not clearly justified (equations do not condition on the focal model and the CKA definition is inconsistent), and the data splits for selection, fusion and evaluation are unclear.

8dYaiUpvvT.one_liner: A coding agent orchestrates a base language model, stitching sampled text spans, to produce responses that evade AI-text detectors.
8dYaiUpvvT.problem: Prior humanization techniques paraphrase AI output over several iterations and invariably cause semantic drift, while post-hoc detectors and soft watermarks target the token patterns of post-trained model generations.
8dYaiUpvvT.method: A coding agent (Claude Opus 5 in a Claude Code harness) is given a local 32B OLMo-2 base language model as a tool and assembles its response from base-model samples, using up to 90% base-model tokens.
8dYaiUpvvT.key_idea: The agent controls sampling from a base model as a tool and splices selected continuations into the response, so most tokens come from the base model.
8dYaiUpvvT.evidence: Benchmarks spanning creative writing, factual grounding, health QA and instruction following, evaluated against Pangram v4 and soft-watermark detection, with comparisons to prior evasion methods (per reviews).
8dYaiUpvvT.claimed_gains: Pangram v4 fraction-AI score drops from 77% to 24% and soft-watermark detection falls to a simulated 10% at low FPR, using up to 90% base LM tokens, while cost per query rises by up to 27x.
8dYaiUpvvT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the attack substantially reduces detection by a strong commercial detector while largely preserving output quality, and that it extends beyond creative writing.
8dYaiUpvvT.main_concern: The attack costs up to 27x more per query, and its incremental contribution over prior base-model and snippet-assembly evasion work is unclear.

K8g604h9hG.one_liner: RL for memory-based search agents that rewards changes in answerability across consecutive memories and assigns credit per search-memory conversation.
K8g604h9hG.problem: In memory-based search agents, useful evidence can be omitted or distorted during memory updates, and outcome-level supervision does not separate each search-memory conversation's contribution to the retained state.
K8g604h9hG.method: MemCredit defines a memory-state reward from changes in answerability across consecutive memories, using gold-answer likelihood under a frozen reader, and feeds it into the search and memory conversations for credit assignment. It keeps outcome-level supervision, needs only final-answer annotations, and adds no inference-time scoring module.
K8g604h9hG.key_idea: Reward each memory update by the change in gold-answer likelihood under a frozen reader across consecutive memories, and credit the search and memory conversations that produced it.
K8g604h9hG.evidence: Seven question-answering benchmarks with Qwen2.5-3B and Qwen2.5-7B against baselines such as MemSearcher, with component ablations.
K8g604h9hG.claimed_gains: Improves Exact Match over the strongest baseline by 1.97% (the abstract is cut off after "and").
K8g604h9hG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies a real failure mode in memory-based search, where retrieval does not guarantee evidence survives memory compression, and that the intermediate reward is intuitive and needs no extra annotations.
K8g604h9hG.main_concern: The gains are modest and statistically unreliable: results use a single training seed and 7B improvements are mostly under one point per benchmark.

GFWcxWhJkD.one_liner: Replaces UCT visit counts with learned pseudo-counts from a Coin-Flipping Network head so related reasoning branches share exploration evidence.
GFWcxWhJkD.problem: Standard UCT gives independent visit counts to textual branches, so different formulations of the same reasoning strategy keep receiving exploration bonuses (count fragmentation), which raises cumulative regret.
GFWcxWhJkD.method: LPC-MCTS changes only the exploration statistic in UCT: a lightweight Coin-Flipping Network head on the policy's hidden representations estimates representation coverage, letting related branches share exploration evidence.
GFWcxWhJkD.key_idea: A Coin-Flipping Network head on policy hidden states estimates representation coverage and replaces per-branch visit counts in UCT's exploration bonus.
GFWcxWhJkD.evidence: A theoretical regret analysis of count fragmentation and experiments on 5 mathematical-reasoning and 7 search benchmarks with Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen3-4B.
GFWcxWhJkD.claimed_gains: Replacing standard MCTS counts at inference improves average mean@16 accuracy on 5 mathematical benchmarks by 3.79 points on Qwen2.5-7B and 2.71 points on Qwen3-4B, and using LPC-MCTS in training and inference gives gains of 4.96 and 4.37 points.
GFWcxWhJkD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree count fragmentation is a real limitation of LLM tree search and that the lightweight, easy-to-integrate fix gives strong gains on mathematical benchmarks.
GFWcxWhJkD.main_concern: There is no cost analysis of token efficiency or latency, no direct comparison with the closely related FETCH and MERCI, and only three older models, with the shared-evidence claim resting on qualitative examples.

ZTW19Z6hby.one_liner: AI writes a hypothesis test for linear models together with a Lean-checked proof of validity against the scientist's assumptions.
ZTW19Z6hby.problem: There is no way to certify that statistical inference produced by AI is valid for the specific null hypothesis, design matrix and assumptions a scientist sets.
ZTW19Z6hby.method: In the protocol, the scientist fixes the null, design matrix and assumption class and withholds the data, and an AI produces a test with a formal proof of validity that Lean checks. They release a Lean formalisation of the finite-sample and asymptotic theory of the model-robust linear model, the statistical paradoxes, and all proofs built through the protocol.
ZTW19Z6hby.key_idea: Per-problem certified validity: the AI writes a new test and Lean-verified proof for the declared assumption class while the data stays withheld, using e-values.
ZTW19Z6hby.evidence: Demonstration on sixteen datasets across science, policy, medicine and AI, three published after AI training cut-offs, with a Lean formalisation of the theory and the protocol's proofs.
ZTW19Z6hby.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find certifying AI-produced statistical inference an interesting problem and see the per-problem Lean-checked proofs, which separate the scientist's judgement from the AI's mathematics, as an original and applicable idea.
ZTW19Z6hby.main_concern: The experiments do not follow the protocol (the AI likely saw the data, the authors knew it, and several proposals had human help), AI ability is not measured, and the scope is limited to regression-coefficient tests.

l44KpjyeZd.one_liner: Repurposes video diffusion as a sparse multi-view generator by resetting the video VAE per view and exchanging camera-aligned features.
l44KpjyeZd.problem: Video VAEs temporally compress frames after the reset frame, so under viewpoint motion neighboring frames add little new angular coverage while carrying larger codec errors, which hurts sparse multi-view reconstruction.
l44KpjyeZd.method: Vid2Orbit passes each requested camera through the VAE's native single-frame path while the diffusion transformer jointly generates the full view set, and adds camera-aligned feature exchange that aggregates intermediate multi-view features in a shared 3D field and reads them back along camera rays. The camera-indexed views feed COLMAP and Gaussian reconstruction.
l44KpjyeZd.key_idea: Reset the frozen video VAE for every view so each camera uses the high-fidelity single-frame path, plus a shared 3D feature field read back along camera rays.
l44KpjyeZd.evidence: A frozen-VAE round-trip test without diffusion sampling, and comparisons of generated views and downstream reconstruction (reviewers note qualitative results on two real inputs and synthetic data).
l44KpjyeZd.claimed_gains: Resetting the frozen VAE for every ground-truth view improves round-trip PSNR by 6.25 dB at 18 degree view spacing.
l44KpjyeZd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the diagnosis of temporal-compression information loss in the video codec clear and useful, with the per-view reset well motivated and generated views showing better reconstructability than baselines.
l44KpjyeZd.main_concern: Direct validation is thin (qualitative comparisons on two real inputs, no quantitative view quality, camera accuracy or geometry accuracy), and the contribution of the 3D feature exchange over RGB adaptation alone is not demonstrated.

Ul3BwycFFs.one_liner: Generates time series with a hyperspherical VAE latent and masked autoregressive modeling with a conditional diffusion head.
Ul3BwycFFs.problem: Two-stage time series generators lose information when discretizing continuous series and accumulate errors during next-token autoregressive generation.
Ul3BwycFFs.method: HALO first uses a hyperspherical VAE that constrains continuous latents to a fixed-radius hyperspherical shell to stabilize their variance and scale. It then uses a masked autoregressive model, with a conditional diffusion module per reviewers, to balance generation efficiency with temporal correlation modeling.
Ul3BwycFFs.key_idea: Continuous latents are constrained to a fixed-radius hyperspherical shell, and a masked autoregressive model generates them in parallel groups instead of next-token over discrete codes.
Ul3BwycFFs.evidence: Per reviewers, 12 datasets, three sequence lengths, three metrics and five seeds against recent generative models; the abstract is cut off before the results.
Ul3BwycFFs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the variance and scale analysis of continuous latents motivates the design clearly and that the evaluation is broad across datasets and sequence lengths with competitive generation performance.
Ul3BwycFFs.main_concern: Novelty is limited because the design overlaps with SphereAR (fixed-radius spherical latents) and MAR (masked autoregression with a diffusion head), and key baselines (SDformer, MSDformer, PolarFormer) and diffusion-head details are missing.

53Ak0jvesg.one_liner: Alternates LLM-driven harness edits from failed trajectories with model fine-tuning on trajectories from the updated harness.
53Ak0jvesg.problem: When the runtime harness (prompts, tools, skills, middleware, memory) stays fixed during agent post-training, model updates change behavior without matching harness adjustments.
53Ak0jvesg.method: An LLM-based HarnessCritic analyzes failed trajectories and proposes local harness edits that are kept after validation. The model is then fine-tuned on quality-filtered trajectories collected under the updated harness, and the resulting model guides the next round of harness search.
53Ak0jvesg.key_idea: Failure-driven harness search and trajectory-based model fine-tuning alternate in rounds so each uses the other's latest version.
53Ak0jvesg.evidence: SWE-bench Verified and SWE-bench Pro for repository-level coding and AIME24, AIME25 and HMMT25 for tool-integrated math, over two joint rounds, plus a separate 200+ hour case study with fixed model weights.
53Ak0jvesg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that treating the harness and the model as one jointly optimized system is timely, and that the paper shows large, consistent improvements and a transparent harness-evolution log.
53Ak0jvesg.main_concern: It is not shown that co-evolution beats separate harness optimization plus fine-tuning (no ablation of model versus harness gains or of alternating updates), and harness search may overlap with the evaluation benchmarks.

iapCnbRtqC.one_liner: Diffusion model predicts a latent physical-parameter field and renders dependent state fields through a differentiable solver.
iapCnbRtqC.problem: Standard diffusion treats coupled physical-field variables as free outputs, so generated parameter-state pairs can be individually plausible yet inconsistent under the governing physics, especially when forcing or boundary conditions shift.
iapCnbRtqC.method: MPDM predicts a compact latent of the independent parameter field, decodes it into a feasible parameter map, and uses a differentiable numerical solver to render the dependent state fields under prescribed conditions. Reconstruction losses propagate through the solver for end-to-end training without a physics-residual objective.
iapCnbRtqC.key_idea: Clean-state predictions are restricted to a solver-rendered manifold by generating only the independent parameter field and computing dependent states with a differentiable solver.
iapCnbRtqC.evidence: Multiple PDE systems under controlled distribution shifts, compared with ambient full-state and residual-based diffusion, with ablations of the components.
iapCnbRtqC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the factorization into independent parameters and solver-rendered states keeps predictions physically consistent without a physics-residual loss and holds under out-of-distribution shifts, with ablations over components.
iapCnbRtqC.main_concern: Novelty is unclear relative to Diffusion with Forward Models and latent generative models with differentiable PDE solvers (LD-DIM, L-DPS, GenPANIS), and evidence for the latent parameterization comes from a favorable setting with known intrinsic dimension.

rC7Vl4Xw1T.one_liner: Encodes a user's pairwise preferences into fast weights via test-time training for personalized reward modeling without inference-time backpropagation.
rC7Vl4Xw1T.problem: In-context-learning personalized reward models fail to capture the preference relations conveyed by a user's contextual comparison pairs.
rC7Vl4Xw1T.method: P-TTT updates user-specific fast weights within a single forward pass using sequence-level update and apply operations that match response-level preference feedback, plus a preference-aligned objective that uses pairwise preference relations to guide the adaptation.
rC7Vl4Xw1T.key_idea: Pairwise chosen and rejected relations drive a closed-form fast-weight update at the response level, replacing in-context conditioning.
rC7Vl4Xw1T.evidence: Experiments on personalized reward modeling with ablations of the two design choices; reviewers note backbones of only 0.5B to 1B parameters.
rC7Vl4Xw1T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the adaptation of test-time training to personalized reward modeling concrete and lightweight, with clear equations, ablations supporting both design choices, and an interesting finding that historical preference pairs help little in ICL.
rC7Vl4Xw1T.main_concern: Evaluation uses only very small models (0.5B to 1B), which undermines the claim that ICL fails, and the theoretical justification does not hold for the evaluated multi-block architecture.

bXitbe80cw.one_liner: Gray-box hallucination detector propagating external semantic embeddings using Top-K local agreement and global anticipatory consistency signals.
bXitbe80cw.problem: Gray-box hallucination detectors that use only API-visible Top-K candidates and probabilities lag white-box detectors, and external embeddings are not aligned with the target LLM's generation dynamics.
bXitbe80cw.method: Prop-K measures local agreement consistency (how Top-K candidates support or conflict with the Top-1 prediction at each step) and global anticipatory consistency (whether early predictive expectations match later generated tokens), and uses both signals to guide semantic propagation across the generated sequence.
bXitbe80cw.key_idea: Top-K candidate agreement and cross-step anticipatory consistency set graph weights that propagate external semantic embeddings along the generated sequence.
bXitbe80cw.evidence: Seven target LLMs and four benchmarks against black-box, gray-box and white-box baselines, with module ablations and a parameter-matched attention control per reviewers.
bXitbe80cw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it makes nontrivial use of gray-box information and beats gray-box baselines across seven LLMs and four benchmarks, with ablations supporting both propagation stages.
bXitbe80cw.main_concern: The interpretation of the consistency measures needs stronger justification (a next-token distribution at an earlier step is read as support for a later token, and similarity is not question-conditioned agreement), and some architectural claims lack controls.

vFndAgYUwc.one_liner: Learned cross-attentive controller selects graph-memory skills at each step for a frozen long-horizon LLM agent.
vFndAgYUwc.problem: Long-horizon LLM agents with graph-structured memory must decide at each step whether memory is needed, which graph-native behavior to invoke, and how returned structures condition later actions, a choice prior work on memory representation, retrieval and management leaves open.
vFndAgYUwc.method: GeMS-SC treats graph-memory invocation as a state-conditioned skill-selection policy: a Cross-Attentive State-Skill Encoder (CASE) contextualizes execution-state fragments with candidate Graph-Native Memory Skills, and a shared scoring head picks one skill or CONTINUE REGULAR EXECUTION. The chosen skill injects an operation protocol while the frozen base agent keeps control of tool calls, and CASE is trained in two stages: weak state-skill alignment, then advantage-weighted trajectory optimization.
vFndAgYUwc.key_idea: Skill-to-state cross-attention decides when and how to invoke graph memory, injecting an operation protocol into a frozen agent.
vFndAgYUwc.evidence: Per reviewers, LoCoMo, LongMemEval, MemoryAgentBench and ALFWorld with same-substrate prompting controls and transfer and diagnostic analyses; the abstract is cut off before the results.
vFndAgYUwc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper isolates an under-addressed question (when and how to invoke an existing graph memory) and that same-substrate prompting controls show the value of learned runtime selection.
vFndAgYUwc.main_concern: Gains are small and mostly inside overlapping standard-deviation bands on three of four benchmarks, with the real gain confined to MemoryAgentBench, and positioning against runtime graph-memory controllers (AriGraph, HAGE, ExpGraph) and the hand-designed seven-skill set are weak points.

xv3yebiu6S.one_liner: Corrects residual rollout-learner mismatch in quantized agentic RL by bounded correction over the state-reaching policy history.
xv3yebiu6S.problem: Quantized rollouts in multi-turn agent RL cause execution mismatch with the learner that accumulates along the policy history, so a current action can look aligned even when its history is mismatched.
xv3yebiu6S.method: InterQ-RL applies bounded execution-prefix correction over the state-reaching policy history and allocates correction strength across action segments by effective support under a fixed displacement budget, with no additional model forward pass.
xv3yebiu6S.key_idea: Correct the rollout-learner mismatch over the whole prefix of policy history rather than the current token, spending a fixed displacement budget by each action segment's effective support.
xv3yebiu6S.evidence: Dense and MoE backbones from 4B to 30B on ALFWorld, WebShop and ScienceWorld, with all quantized arms sharing W8A8-KV8 rollouts.
xv3yebiu6S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practical, the history-based motivation is clear, the correction needs no extra forward pass, and the evaluation covers three environments with dense and MoE backbones and careful alignment studies.
xv3yebiu6S.main_concern: Margins over QAT and other quantized methods are small in several settings and come from single runs without multi-seed variance, cost and budget sensitivity are not reported, and only Qwen3 backbones at W8A8-KV8 are tested.

oH00vTBxVU.one_liner: Clusters unlabeled hyperspectral scenes by disentangling semantic from scene-specific features and admitting target regions progressively in a recurrent loop.
oH00vTBxVU.problem: Existing cross-scene hyperspectral clustering aligns representations wholesale, leaving unclear what structure should be transferred and when target evidence should enter the transfer.
oH00vTBxVU.method: DTRA factorizes each representation into semantic and scene-specific branches, tests whether semantic assignments survive cross-scene variation exchange, summarizes preserved structure by balanced prototypes, and matches them across scenes to initialize the target-oriented state. Target regions are ranked by assignment confidence plus exchange-induced discrepancy and admitted progressively, with the terminal prototype state carried into the next round.
oH00vTBxVU.key_idea: Semantic assignments that survive variation exchange define what to transfer, and confidence plus exchange discrepancy rank target regions for progressive admission in a recurrent loop.
oH00vTBxVU.evidence: Per reviewers, six directional cross-scene tasks against nine recent methods, with component ablation, parameter sensitivity and mechanism visualization; the abstract is cut off before the results.
oH00vTBxVU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the what-to-transfer and when-to-transfer decomposition well motivated and clearly structured, with broad validation across six directional tasks.
oH00vTBxVU.main_concern: Novelty is unclear since disentanglement, consistency regularization, optimal transport and progressive pseudo-labeling are well studied, and gains are only 0.5-1.3 points on several tasks within large standard deviations, with ACC as the only metric.

LDgyEtkayX.one_liner: Distills task and capability experts into one 8B model for individual behavior simulation via multi-teacher on-policy distillation.
LDgyEtkayX.problem: General-purpose LLMs flatten distinct personas when simulating individuals, while task-specific tuning suffers from fragmentation and poor generalization.
LDgyEtkayX.method: They organize simulation into the FONTS taxonomy of five capability dimensions and curate about 10 million training instances across 14 datasets. A three-stage pipeline trains task experts with DAPO, consolidates them into capability experts via off-policy distillation, and unifies them via multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) in probability space, with IndiEval consolidating 29 metrics.
LDgyEtkayX.key_idea: Decouple specialization from integration by training task experts, merging them into per-dimension capability experts, and unifying those with multi-teacher on-policy distillation in probability space.
LDgyEtkayX.evidence: A corpus of about 10 million instances across 14 datasets and the IndiEval suite of 29 metrics, with ablations and out-of-distribution evaluations against Qwen3-8B and frontier models.
LDgyEtkayX.claimed_gains: Socio-Foundation outperforms its Qwen3-8B base by 11.0 points and approaches frontier models such as GLM-5.2.
LDgyEtkayX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study is broad, with extensive evaluation showing an 8B model improving substantially over its base and approaching frontier models, and with design choices supported by ablations.
LDgyEtkayX.main_concern: DeepSeek-V4-Flash serves as training reward model, dialogue counterpart, IndiEval judge and baseline, creating circularity, and most IndiEval benchmarks are in-domain with limited out-of-distribution evidence.

MNok1aJBXI.one_liner: Domain-generalized DiffusionDet detector using spatially calibrated DINOv3 features, region-wise perturbations and prototype-anchored proposal denoising.
MNok1aJBXI.problem: Under unseen domain shifts, detectors struggle to keep reliable spatial and semantic guidance for proposal refinement.
MNok1aJBXI.method: GOLD builds on DiffusionDet with a Spatial Calibration Adapter that adds localization-sensitive structure to frozen DINOv3 features, Spatially Heterogeneous Evidence Perturbing that applies moderate, strong and weak residual perturbations to foreground, localization-critical context and distant background, and Prototype-Anchored Denoising that supervises proposals at each refinement stage with multi-scale class prototypes from clean source images.
MNok1aJBXI.key_idea: Proposal denoising is anchored with class prototypes from clean source images while perturbation strength is set per image region according to its role.
MNok1aJBXI.evidence: Diverse Weather, Cityscapes to BDD100K and Cityscapes to Foggy Cityscapes, with ablations of the three modules per reviewers; the abstract is cut off before the results.
MNok1aJBXI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the framework clearly presented, the heterogeneous perturbation strategy intuitive, and the headline mAP gains large with internally consistent ablations.
MNok1aJBXI.main_concern: No variance, seed count or selection procedure is reported (gains of 0.5-1.0 mAP, target sets evaluated during training), and the link between the modules and diffusion-specific proposal denoising is not established.

tQ08KOSvbz.one_liner: Rarity-scaled shared residual context for prompt learning, dropped at inference, with a fixed-budget long-tailed benchmark.
tQ08KOSvbz.problem: Prompt learning for vision-language models is mostly evaluated under balanced supervision, so the effect of class imbalance on recognition and transfer is poorly understood.
tQ08KOSvbz.method: TailPromptBench varies class imbalance under a fixed annotation budget and evaluates frequency groups, base-to-new transfer and domain shift. RAP adds a shared residual context whose contribution grows with class rarity, is optimized jointly with the prompt parameters, and is discarded at inference.
tQ08KOSvbz.key_idea: A single shared residual context is weighted by class rarity during training so rare classes get stronger corrections, with no class-specific parameters and no inference cost.
tQ08KOSvbz.evidence: Experiments on TailPromptBench with CoOp and CoCoOp learners and ablations; reviewers note only CLIP ViT-B/16 is used and long-tailed distributions are built by random rank assignment.
tQ08KOSvbz.claimed_gains: Stronger tail-class recognition and average base-to-new harmonic-mean gains of up to 2.8 percentage points.
tQ08KOSvbz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the fixed-budget protocol that separates imbalance from training-set size and a simple method that leaves inference unchanged, with consistent gains and reported trade-offs.
tQ08KOSvbz.main_concern: Comparisons are limited to CoOp and CoCoOp, without long-tail methods such as loss reweighting, logit adjustment, Candle or LAMP, so RAP's advantage over imbalance-aware baselines is not established.

JtOp2twYNI.one_liner: Co-evolves antibody cocktails against a simulated virus in a Stackelberg game so combinations steer viral evolution toward weaker variants.
JtOp2twYNI.problem: Combination therapy design is myopic: it optimizes efficacy against present viral strains without anticipating how therapeutic pressure shapes future viral evolution.
JtOp2twYNI.method: Co-ADIOS models antibody cocktails as leaders and the virus as an evolving follower in a Stackelberg evolutionary game, with viral dynamics from a biophysically-grounded lattice simulator of binding energies and evolutionary plausibility. It is evaluated on Influenza H5 for de novo cocktails and for co-designing a partner to an established antibody.
JtOp2twYNI.key_idea: Antibody populations are co-evolved cooperatively as opponent shapers of viral evolution in a lattice binding simulator, optimizing against anticipated escape rather than the current strain.
JtOp2twYNI.evidence: Influenza H5 in a lattice simulator for two scenarios (de novo cocktails and partner co-design), with multiple seeds and held-out evaluation per reviewers.
JtOp2twYNI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation of designing against induced viral escape is compelling and that results show consistent improvements within the simulator across seeds and held-out evaluations.
JtOp2twYNI.main_concern: Results rest on a lattice simulator not calibrated against experimental data, the comparison does not isolate cooperative design from search representation and budget, and the contribution over ADIOS is incremental.

qMZLqWLKS7.one_liner: Single-checkpoint autoregressive transformer unifies piano transcription and rendering with a shared MIDI tokenizer and decoupled audio representations.
qMZLqWLKS7.problem: Unified models for piano transcription and rendering lag task-specific methods because the audio formats suited to each direction differ significantly.
qMZLqWLKS7.method: PianoPoet shares one MIDI tokenizer and a transformer backbone across both directions while using continuous semantic audio frames for transcription and a piano-specific discrete audio tokenizer for rendering. It supports full-band stereo rendering with stereo-position control through acoustic prompts.
qMZLqWLKS7.key_idea: Share the symbolic MIDI tokenizer and backbone but decouple audio representations: continuous semantic frames as input for transcription, discrete piano-codec tokens as output for rendering.
qMZLqWLKS7.evidence: Comparisons with prior unified models, generative transcription methods and specialized rendering methods, with ablations against single-task variants; reviewers cite a 113M causal transformer.
qMZLqWLKS7.claimed_gains: Outperforms prior unified models, achieves the best results among the evaluated generative transcription methods, and outperforms specialized rendering methods in most evaluated metrics, with no numbers stated.
qMZLqWLKS7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the decoupled audio representations are well supported by ablations and the piano-specific stereo codec is valuable, with the unified model staying close to single-task variants.
qMZLqWLKS7.main_concern: Joint training shows no clear benefit over single-task models, rendered-note onset F1 trails specialized systems by a wide margin (70.47 versus 90.84 for P-MUSE), and long-recording handling is underspecified.

lYdjPNeLFn.one_liner: Executes each proposed agent action in an isolated fork, has an LLM review the effects, and commits only approved changes.
lYdjPNeLFn.problem: In long-horizon tasks a tool call can succeed while making a change that violates user instructions or environment rules, and such changes compound and leave the environment hard to recover.
lYdjPNeLFn.method: EVC is a training-free method that runs a state-changing action in an isolated fork and reviews the tool output and state changes against user instructions and policies, using the interaction history. Approved changes are committed without re-execution; rejected ones are discarded with a specific explanation, leaving the live state unchanged.
lYdjPNeLFn.key_idea: Verify the actual post-execution effects of an action in an isolated fork before committing it to the live environment, rolling back with explanatory feedback on rejection.
