lYdjPNeLFn.evidence: Three acting LLMs (Qwen3.8-max, GLM-5.2, Kimi-K3) on three benchmarks with a fixed LLM reviewer and one review per action, plus ablations of execution evidence, rejection feedback and repeated voting.
lYdjPNeLFn.claimed_gains: EVC improves average task success over no-review baselines across the three acting LLMs and three benchmarks, with no numbers stated.
lYdjPNeLFn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it targets a concrete, under-studied failure mode and that isolated execution with commit-or-discard semantics is a practical way to keep rejected actions from altering committed state.
lYdjPNeLFn.main_concern: The reviewer's accuracy is never measured (no rejection or false-rejection rates), the benefit of post-execution over pre-execution verification is not isolated, and irreversible side effects of isolated execution are unaddressed.

sl2JTsvA70.one_liner: An MLLM generates a variable number of object description and object token pairs that form language-addressable object representations.
sl2JTsvA70.problem: Slot-based object-centric methods often fix the number of slots despite varying object counts and give representations without explicit descriptions, making objects hard to identify and select for manipulation.
sl2JTsvA70.method: DeOR has a multimodal LLM sequentially generate an object description and a corresponding object token for each object, with each representation combining the token's semantics with visual features. An external language model selects objects from the descriptions, and editing their representations removes objects or transfers appearance, while recombining representations across images gives compositional generation.
sl2JTsvA70.key_idea: Each object is generated as a description-token pair, where the description specifies which object the token represents, so both object count and identity come from the MLLM.
sl2JTsvA70.evidence: Trained with paired data (the abstract is cut off); reviewers cite COCO FG-ARI, VOC instance mBO, RefCOCO TargetHit@1 and ablations of description initialization, description attention and grounding loss.
sl2JTsvA70.claimed_gains: A reviewer quoting the abstract cites +26.6% FG-ARI on COCO and +44.2% instance mBO on VOC over unsupervised slot methods (the visible abstract is cut off).
sl2JTsvA70.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that generating description-token pairs is a direct way to obtain a variable number of language-addressable representations and that ablations of the description paths and grounding loss show each component matters.
sl2JTsvA70.main_concern: Headline gains compare a mask-supervised model with large pretrained backbones against unsupervised slot methods, and under matched supervision FixedQuery beats it on FG-ARI, with novelty seen as system integration that depends on the MLLM.

xsZZDVfGan.one_liner: Diffusion posterior sampler combining the diffusion prior and a statistical linearization of a simulator likelihood in a Kalman update.
xsZZDVfGan.problem: Scientific measurements come from stochastic simulators with non-Gaussian randomness and unavailable likelihoods and gradients, which diffusion posterior sampling usually requires.
xsZZDVfGan.method: KPS puts the diffusion prior and a statistical linearization of the simulator-defined likelihood into a common Kalman update through their moments, using simulations alone or gradients when the simulator is differentiable. An inner Gibbs loop keeps iterates consistent with the diffusion process so errors do not accumulate across steps.
xsZZDVfGan.key_idea: Moment-matched statistical linearization of the simulator likelihood enters a Kalman update with the diffusion prior's moments, with an inner Gibbs loop preserving consistency with the diffusion process.
xsZZDVfGan.evidence: Latent fluid dynamics and scientific inverse-problem benchmarks (inverse scattering and Navier-Stokes per reviewers) against competing posterior samplers.
xsZZDVfGan.claimed_gains: KPS outperforms the compared samplers in accuracy with as few as 16 particles, delivers close-to-calibrated uncertainty, and captures multimodal posteriors even from black-box simulators.
xsZZDVfGan.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and timely and that using a Kalman update in diffusion posterior sampling is new, clearly derived, and works without a differentiable forward model.
xsZZDVfGan.main_concern: The closest prior work Blade (derivative-free ensemble linearization in a Gibbs-style sampler) is not compared, the Kalman update assumes linear-Gaussian structure that may not hold, and computational cost is not discussed.

m6FJ42JUNf.one_liner: Evolves a complete hypergraph partitioner with an LLM coding agent using behavior-based MAP-Elites and partition fingerprint deduplication.
m6FJ42JUNf.problem: The field lacks an open hypergraph partitioner that is lightweight, strong and fast, since hMETIS is closed-source and KaHyPar spans about 27,000 lines of C++.
m6FJ42JUNf.method: On top of OpenEvolve, they design a harness that evolves a whole solver: programs are placed in a MAP-Elites grid by behavior (running time and relative strength across k) rather than text, deduplicated by partition fingerprinting, and given measured per-instance cut and wall time as prompt feedback. A single 200-iteration run starting from a round-robin program yields EvoPart.
m6FJ42JUNf.key_idea: Evolve a whole solver by indexing programs in MAP-Elites by measured behavior and fingerprinting partitions for deduplication, feeding per-instance cut and time back to the LLM.
m6FJ42JUNf.evidence: ISPD98 and Titan23 benchmarks compared with KaHyPar and hMETIS, plus a held-out set, unseen k values and a three-run ablation of behavioral descriptors per reviewers.
m6FJ42JUNf.claimed_gains: A single 200-iteration run yields a 1,186-line single-threaded C++ partitioner, 22.5x less code than KaHyPar, with cut 5.5% lower than KaHyPar's in 70% of its wall time and 5.1% lower than hMETIS's at equal wall time.
m6FJ42JUNf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the harness-driven approach is interesting and that the compact open-source partitioner convincingly shows LLM code evolution can yield a competitive whole solver, with good evaluation hygiene.
m6FJ42JUNf.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited (OpenEvolve with small changes) and baselines are incomplete (SpecPart, PaToH, Mt-KaHyPar and stronger KaHyPar presets are missing), with results resting on a single evolution run.

y4DLK6y4G0.one_liner: Minimizes an upper average of bootstrap-fitted expected costs to protect decisions from unlucky training samples under parameter uncertainty.
y4DLK6y4G0.problem: When a known distribution family is fitted from limited observations, decisions made on the fitted model are exposed to uncertainty about expected cost caused by an unlucky training sample.
y4DLK6y4G0.method: Parametric APUB refits the model under parametric bootstrap or random likelihood weights (weighted-likelihood bootstrap) without a parameter prior, and minimizes an upper average of the bootstrap-fitted expected costs. An adaptive implementation reuses fitted models.
y4DLK6y4G0.key_idea: Average the upper percentiles of expected costs under bootstrap refits (parametric or weighted-likelihood) as the decision objective, with no parameter prior.
y4DLK6y4G0.evidence: Theory on contraction, decision consistency, selected-decision coverage and finite-ensemble error, plus fixed-population Gaussian and lognormal-mixture newsvendor experiments comparing regret and coverage.
y4DLK6y4G0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the formulation separating parameter uncertainty from outcome randomness is natural and well presented, with technically solid theory and clear exposition of the bootstrap methods.
y4DLK6y4G0.main_concern: The coverage guarantee is conservative (measured coverage about 57.7%, 78.8% and 91.9% at the three tested levels), the literature positioning is thin, and the work is a natural extension of nonparametric APUB from Liu et al. (2026).

mEuRlTuV0J.one_liner: Predicts region-level photographic composition targets by modeling region-region and region-frame relations from source-grounded reference supervision.
mEuRlTuV0J.problem: Photographic composition depends on how people and environmental regions are positioned and scaled relative to each other and the frame, but only whole-image source-reference outcomes exist, so region-level supervision is unavailable.
mEuRlTuV0J.method: They formulate Region-Level Composition Target Prediction, jointly predicting regional geometry, target frame aspect ratio and person framing while preserving source-region identities. Supervision is recovered by transferring reference geometry to source identities through partial correspondence (keeping each reference as a complete alternative arrangement) plus single-image aesthetic annotations, and NextShot conditions regional geometry on predicted frame and person framing.
mEuRlTuV0J.key_idea: Reference geometry is transferred to source-region identities through appearance and semantic correspondence to create region-level targets, which a relational predictor learns jointly with frame and person framing.
mEuRlTuV0J.evidence: Comparisons with lightweight predictors and ablations judged mostly by Qwen and Flash preference rates, plus a five-person user study per reviewers; the abstract is cut off before the results.
mEuRlTuV0J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the region-level formulation is useful because predictions stay tied to observed regions and are inspectable, and the source-reference supervision design fits the task.
mEuRlTuV0J.main_concern: Aesthetic claims rest on model judges that disagree (45.0% versus 72.5% preference for NextShot over NoVLM-AttrAux), with only a five-person user study and no ablation of the geometric representation.

kTZFahYzlK.one_liner: Calibrates monocular depth to single-pixel SPAD histograms and refines it with depth-conditioned recurrent queries into the SPAD evidence.
kTZFahYzlK.problem: Single-pixel SPAD measurements give accurate metric range but have no explicit spatial correspondence with image pixels, making their fusion with dense monocular depth ambiguous.
kTZFahYzlK.method: Hist2Depth uses monocular depth itself to associate unresolved SPAD measurements with pixel-wise depth hypotheses: Global D2 aligns the monocular prediction to the measured depth distribution through order-preserving metric calibration, then MS-GRU performs depth-conditioned recurrent refinement that queries SPAD evidence by the evolving per-pixel depth and merges it with image context.
kTZFahYzlK.key_idea: An order-preserving global calibration to the SPAD depth distribution is followed by recurrent refinement that queries SPAD evidence along the depth axis according to current per-pixel depth.
kTZFahYzlK.evidence: NYU-Depth-v2 with six monocular backbones, zero-shot transfer from synthetic training to captured RGB-SPAD data, photon-thinning tests, and DIODE Outdoor, MatrixCity and STB.
kTZFahYzlK.claimed_gains: On NYU-Depth-v2, Hist2Depth with AdaBins achieves 0.0649 AbsRel and 0.2750 m RMSE, and performance stays nearly unchanged at a 60 s equivalent acquisition using only 7.4% of the full photon count.
kTZFahYzlK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the global-to-local design is well motivated, the bounded calibration preserves depth ordering, and gains hold across six backbones with useful captured-data results.
kTZFahYzlK.main_concern: SPAD guidance is not separated from the extra trained refinement network (no matched RGB-only refinement baseline), and evaluation is narrow (mostly indoor NYU-Depth-v2 at an ideal signal-to-background ratio of 100).

bHQSQoQIKS.one_liner: Dual-LLM computer-use agent that unmasks only accessibility-tree-verified trusted screen regions and passes values through an endorsement channel.
bHQSQoQIKS.problem: Computer-use agents act on screenshots with no boundary between trusted first-party interfaces and attacker-authored content, so indirect prompt injections can cause harm and per-action user confirmation causes fatigue.
bHQSQoQIKS.method: SA-CUA derives conservative deterministic rules from the accessibility tree to unmask only trusted regions of the screenshot shown to the privileged LLM, keeping untrusted content separated. A declassification (endorsement) channel lets values move from the untrusted to the trusted domain after verification through trusted channels, so the user only specifies the task at the start.
bHQSQoQIKS.key_idea: Mask the whole screen by default, unmask only regions that deterministic accessibility-tree rules mark as trusted, and let untrusted values cross only via a verified endorsement channel.
bHQSQoQIKS.evidence: Reviews describe comparisons against the UCM and CaMeL-CUA baselines on benchmarks including OSWorld and UCM-B; the abstract is truncated before its results.
bHQSQoQIKS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the dual-LLM extension to GUI agents well motivated by Biba's integrity model and robust endorsement, with the mask-then-unmask design intuitive and preserving more utility than CaMeL-CUA.
bHQSQoQIKS.main_concern: The system is heavy-weight and task-specific (hand-specified trusted domains, URL-specific rule sets, shortcuts) and shows a steep utility cost, with weak results on OSWorld and UCM-B that put generalization in doubt.

yaROvA7SeF.one_liner: Trains a backbone and post-hoc calibrator jointly via a bilevel Stackelberg objective, using the final classification layer as calibrator.
yaROvA7SeF.problem: Post-hoc calibration needs a separate calibration set, extra calibrator parameters, and separate optimization and model selection.
yaROvA7SeF.method: The calibrator is trained end-to-end with the backbone as the follower in a bilevel Stackelberg game, optimized only with cross-entropy and controlled by one extra hyperparameter, the calibrator learning rate. The best variant uses the final classification layer itself as the calibrator, adding no parameters.
yaROvA7SeF.key_idea: Treat the final classification layer as the calibrator and train it with a different learning rate than the backbone in a bilevel (Stackelberg) objective, replacing the separate post-hoc stage.
yaROvA7SeF.evidence: Reviews report experiments with several calibrator variants, datasets, backbones, OOD detection, multi-attribute classification, and CIFAR-10-C, with multiple seeds, but only on 32x32 datasets trained from scratch.
yaROvA7SeF.claimed_gains: Outperforms SOTA calibrators with minimal added complexity and avoids the multiplicative overhead of separate calibration components in multi-task learning; no numbers stated.
yaROvA7SeF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple to implement (no held-out calibration set, no calibration loss, one hyperparameter) and that the bilevel framing cleanly unifies post-hoc calibration, TS, MS, and TST.
yaROvA7SeF.main_concern: The comparison looks unfair because baselines use a different learning rate and less tuning than COG, the mechanism is unexplained, and scale is limited to small vision datasets with missing single-stage calibration-loss baselines.

jwOwDYFrW8.one_liner: Distills video diffusion teachers into few-step students by modeling trajectory segments as polynomials with a training-only curvature head.
jwOwDYFrW8.problem: Trajectory distillation asks a few-step student to reproduce highly curved teacher transitions at high noise, which exceeds its capacity and degrades fine detail.
jwOwDYFrW8.method: PTD lets the student parameterize teacher trajectory segments as polynomials and learn from teacher guidance along its own predicted path. The curvature head is used only in training, so inference keeps the original backbone architecture.
jwOwDYFrW8.key_idea: Separate each step's endpoint displacement from its interior curvature, parameterized as a polynomial that queries the teacher along the student's own path during training only.
jwOwDYFrW8.evidence: Four-step distillation on Wan2.1-14B against PDD and LoRA-trained distillation on the 33B audio-video MiniMax-H3 against LightX2V Turbo, plus blinded human votes.
jwOwDYFrW8.claimed_gains: Blinded human votes give PTD 55.1% and 63.4% preference shares against PDD and LightX2V Turbo, with improved dynamic quality, naturalness, and diversity.
jwOwDYFrW8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the endpoint/curvature separation is elegant and adds no inference overhead, and that experiments on two large video backbones show practical value.
jwOwDYFrW8.main_concern: Ablations lack a K=0 straight-path baseline and a direct test linking learned curvature to video quality, and comparisons omit Lagrangian-map and MeanFlow-style baselines while relying on PDD.

WngfgqUByS.one_liner: Trains continuous-time neural networks by keeping the forward ODE solve but backpropagating through a one-step gradient approximation.
WngfgqUByS.problem: Gradients through ODE-solver-based state evolution cost substantial compute and memory, making CTNN training a bottleneck.
WngfgqUByS.method: SSBP keeps forward integration unchanged and bypasses backpropagation through the solver's internal steps, using a one-step gradient approximation built from the integration interval's initial state. A theoretical analysis characterizes how its update direction approximates the BPTT gradient.
WngfgqUByS.key_idea: Replace backpropagation through all solver steps with a one-step gradient approximation constructed from the interval's initial state.
WngfgqUByS.evidence: Experiments across several CTNN models, tasks, and solvers against BPTT and adjoint methods, plus numerical experiments on a spin-torque oscillator device.
WngfgqUByS.claimed_gains: Reduces backward-pass compute and memory from O(Ls) to O(1) while reaching performance comparable to BPTT with substantially lower training time and memory.
WngfgqUByS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, applies across CT models and solvers, and delivers measured gains in training time and GPU memory.
WngfgqUByS.main_concern: Novelty over Euler Gradient Approximation is not clearly established, and fairness of the comparison with BPTT is unclear (shared learning rate, best-test-epoch reporting, gains within one standard deviation).

wUdio9L3lL.one_liner: Autoregressive vision-language-action policy that emits reasoning and waypoint tokens for multi-robot pursuit-evasion across unseen maps.
wUdio9L3lL.problem: Graph-based pursuit-evasion methods depend on map-specific representations, and vision-language agents are built for single-agent tasks, so coordinated executable multi-agent actions are hard to generate.
wUdio9L3lL.method: PursuitVLA generates reasoning traces and executable waypoint tokens from top-down observations and multi-agent states, conditioning each pursuer on previously generated teammate actions. It is trained on dynamic-programming demonstrations with strategic reasoning, then reinforcement fine-tuned with Sequential Action Compensation (SeqAC).
wUdio9L3lL.key_idea: Score candidate actions at intermediate states induced by policy-generated teammate prefixes so later agents learn to compensate for deviations in earlier teammates' actions.
wUdio9L3lL.evidence: Eight unseen maps with 100 matched initial conditions per map, local map perturbations, transfer from 2v1 training to simulated 10v1, and outdoor deployment on three quadruped robots, against geometric, graph, MARL, and prompted VLM baselines.
wUdio9L3lL.claimed_gains: Achieves 79.6% capture against DP evaders on eight unseen maps, compared with 63.0% for EPG, the strongest graph-learning baseline.
wUdio9L3lL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unseen-map result is strong under matched comparisons, with broad baselines, several generalization axes, and real-robot deployment without retraining.
wUdio9L3lL.main_concern: Ablations, team-size, and perturbation studies are run on training maps rather than unseen maps, and training and rewards depend on a dynamic-programming solver with evaluation mainly against DP evaders.

4bR5VUQ1G3.one_liner: Builds a 12K multilingual Wikipedia QA benchmark to measure query-language preference under knowledge gaps and conflicts, then mitigates it.
4bR5VUQ1G3.problem: Query-language preference has mostly been studied where equivalent knowledge exists in all languages, leaving its effect under incomplete or inconsistent cross-lingual sources unclear.
4bR5VUQ1G3.method: Waldo is constructed from Wikipedia with 12K QA pairs targeting knowledge gaps (a fact present in one language and absent in another) and knowledge conflicts (language editions giving conflicting versions). Eight models are evaluated across five languages, and mitigation uses targeted attention-head ablation and LoRA training.
4bR5VUQ1G3.key_idea: Hold the context fixed and vary only the query language over real Wikipedia gaps and controlled conflicts to isolate which document a model selects.
4bR5VUQ1G3.evidence: Eight models across five typologically diverse languages on the Waldo benchmark, with attention-head ablation and LoRA/QLoRA mitigation.
4bR5VUQ1G3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is important and well motivated, and that the counterfactual benchmark design with broad model and language coverage is clean and valuable.
4bR5VUQ1G3.main_concern: The benchmark does not define or evaluate the desired behavior under unresolved conflicts (surfacing the disagreement), and mitigation may learn to spot LLM-inserted edits rather than reduce language preference.

qJEQZtLg8Z.one_liner: Predicts counterfactual distributions end-to-end with a graph neural process that restricts message passing across factual and counterfactual worlds.
qJEQZtLg8Z.problem: Counterfactual inference usually requires an estimated causal graph, and errors in that graph propagate into downstream counterfactual predictions.
qJEQZtLg8Z.method: CFGNP is a Counterfactual Graph Neural Process that answers counterfactual queries directly from observational data without estimating a causal graph. It uses GNNs on a dual-graph structure and restricts cross-world message passing to corresponding factual-counterfactual variables.
qJEQZtLg8Z.key_idea: Restrict cross-world message passing in a GNN to matched factual-counterfactual variable pairs, amortizing counterfactual prediction without an explicit causal graph.
qJEQZtLg8Z.evidence: Synthetic structural causal model benchmarks against graph-based baselines (BGM, VACA, CFM), with architecture ablations and one evaluation on real images, per the abstract and reviews.
qJEQZtLg8Z.claimed_gains: When trained on counterfactual pairs from the same structural causal model used for testing, CFGNP achieves 1.6-7x lower MSE than baselines that receive the true (abstract truncated).
qJEQZtLg8Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem formulation crisp and the method principled, with serious experiments and one model handling varying graphs where baselines need a fixed causal graph.
qJEQZtLg8Z.main_concern: The comparison is unfair because CFGNP trains on ground-truth counterfactual pairs that no baseline receives, and the claim that skipping graph estimation avoids error propagation is never tested.

RSjldMHjsr.one_liner: Trains flow-based policies to sample unnormalized Boltzmann densities via self-consistency conditions, without importance sampling or trajectory backpropagation.
RSjldMHjsr.problem: Diffusion and flow policies for online RL are hard to train because the critic gives an unnormalized density without samples, and importance-sampling signals have high variance.
RSjldMHjsr.method: Score-Calibrated Flow (SCF) enforces score-calibrated optimality conditions, first on the terminal density and then on the trainable velocity field, and proves their unique solutions are the target density and the ideal conditional-flow-matching flow. The velocity condition is formulated as a fixed-point equation.
RSjldMHjsr.key_idea: Learn the target flow by enforcing self-consistency from the prescribed target score and flow-matching structure, bypassing estimation of the target posterior mean.
RSjldMHjsr.evidence: Theorems on necessary and sufficient conditions and uniqueness, standalone sampling on a 2D Gaussian mixture, and online RL experiments against other generative policies and Gaussian SAC (per reviews).
RSjldMHjsr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory is clean, with uniqueness results for the target density and velocity field that give a cheap training rule and a principled alternative to SAC actor losses.
RSjldMHjsr.main_concern: Experiments do not show practical reliability (one symmetric 2D mixture, mixed hyperparameters across baselines), and the technical advance over Reverse Flow Matching and Flow Sampling is not clearly delineated.

opsjRlTdTW.one_liner: Adds a contrastive inner objective to test-time training that distinguishes the current representation from historical alternatives for robot memory.
opsjRlTdTW.problem: Common TTT objectives derive self-supervision from the current observation, giving no direct objective for modeling relations across observed history.
opsjRlTdTW.method: TC-TTT augments the reconstruction inner objective with a contrastive term that separates the current representation from historical alternatives conditioned on an earlier observation. The paper also studies how sampling stride and candidate count affect policy performance.
opsjRlTdTW.key_idea: Contrast the current representation against sampled earlier-observation alternatives in the TTT inner loop, which in a simplified model adds a velocity-like term to the reconstruction gradient.
opsjRlTdTW.evidence: Nine RMBench tasks with a 77M-parameter Diffusion Policy, a fixed action-gradient window, and ablations over stride, candidate count, and gradient window.
opsjRlTdTW.claimed_gains: Improves mean success from 31.8% to 51.8% over reconstruction-based TTT under the same 77M-parameter Diffusion Policy and action-gradient window.
opsjRlTdTW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the improvement over the matched reconstruction baseline is substantial and reasonably controlled, with useful analysis of why the update works.
opsjRlTdTW.main_concern: Experiments do not isolate the contribution of contrastive negatives from temporal pairing, and the 51.8% figure is the best of nine configurations chosen on the reported rollouts.

BDngj01uEj.one_liner: Corrects softmax attention bias caused by quantized KV-cache keys, using a training-free per-score correction from quantization step sizes.
BDngj01uEj.problem: Low-bit KV-cache quantization in autoregressive video diffusion degrades quality because quantization noise inflates cached keys' attention (Jensen bias).
BDngj01uEj.method: Due to the convexity of exp in softmax, quantized keys steal attention mass from the unquantized current chunk. The method derives a per-attention-score correction computed on the fly from the cached keys' quantization step sizes and the query norm, using a second-order Taylor approximation.
BDngj01uEj.key_idea: Subtract the expected Jensen-inequality inflation of exp(q.k) caused by key quantization noise, computed from step sizes and query norm, so cached keys no longer steal attention.
BDngj01uEj.evidence: Evaluated on MAGI-1, SkyReels-V2, and HY-WorldPlay at INT2 quantization, complementing upstream quantizers such as QuantVideoGen.
BDngj01uEj.claimed_gains: At INT2 the correction recovers most of the quality lost, reaching near-BF16 video quality, and can match or exceed INT4 quantization while using 50% less memory.
BDngj01uEj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the Jensen-bias observation is insightful and well motivated by the convexity of the exponential, and the correction is simple, training-free, and consistently helpful across three models.
BDngj01uEj.main_concern: Evaluation is limited to 7-10 second videos with overhead only estimated, and the theory shows unbiasedness of expected exponentials rather than of normalized attention weights.

qoFdybfMUk.one_liner: Transformers with egocentric sensory inputs and egocentric movement outputs forecast fly social behavior, evaluated by lesioning representation components.
qoFdybfMUk.problem: How animals attend to, represent, and act on social information (the algorithmic level of behavior) is hard to study, and world-centric multi-agent forecasters do not mirror biological constraints.
qoFdybfMUk.method: Each fly is modeled by a transformer that takes egocentric sensory observations and outputs egocentric movements, so social behavior emerges from agents independently sensing and responding to one another. Lesioning experiments test which representation properties matter, enabled by a new library for animal-centric pose forecasting.
qoFdybfMUk.key_idea: Replace world-centric pose forecasting with per-agent egocentric sensory input and egocentric movement output, so interaction arises from independent agents sensing each other.
qoFdybfMUk.evidence: Comparison with a world-centric representation on MABe 2022-fly, systematic lesioning experiments, and closed-loop social simulation, per the abstract and reviews.
qoFdybfMUk.claimed_gains: Outperforms the world-centric representation and reports SOTA on MABe 2022-fly; no numbers stated.
qoFdybfMUk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the biologically motivated agent-centric formulation addresses an important neuroethology problem, fills a largely vacant niche, and is backed by a systematic evaluation of representation choices.
qoFdybfMUk.main_concern: The agent-centric versus world-centric ablation is confounded (the KEYPOINTS baseline changes inputs, outputs, and targets at once), and the SOTA comparison on MABe 2022-fly may not be directly comparable.

2yVKEAxU5S.one_liner: Propagates Chebyshev polynomials through a trained neural field in one pass, DCT-refitted, to answer region queries in closed form.
2yVKEAxU5S.problem: Region queries on neural fields are handled either by linear surrogates reduced to output bounds or by dedicated architectures and training, neither giving a reusable description of how the field varies within a region.
2yVKEAxU5S.method: A trained neural field is approximated over a region by a closed-form Chebyshev surrogate, and the output of each activation is refitted with a discrete cosine transform to stop the degree from growing across layers. The surrogate then supports locating sub-regions where the field takes a given value and closed-form integrals from its coefficients.
2yVKEAxU5S.key_idea: Refit each activation's output with a discrete cosine transform during Chebyshev propagation so surrogate degree stays fixed and becomes a knob trading computation against accuracy.
2yVKEAxU5S.evidence: Applied to mesh extraction on neural fields (abstract truncated), with two applications shown and degree-selection analysis on mainly one network and shape, per reviews.
2yVKEAxU5S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the Chebyshev surrogate with DCT refitting a clever, clearly written framework that works on existing networks without retraining and supports several region queries.
2yVKEAxU5S.main_concern: The surrogate drops the remainder term so bounds are not certified, and empirical error control is validated mostly on one network and shape, so underestimated errors could discard valid regions.

QzGGstYqbH.one_liner: Distills environment-grounded counterfactual execution labels into a frozen retrospective selector that supplies turn-level advantages for critic-free RL of coding agents.
QzGGstYqbH.problem: Successful coding trajectories contain harmful actions and failed ones contain useful decisions, so trajectory-level rewards give poor credit assignment to individual turns.
QzGGstYqbH.method: State before each action is restored and the observed action plus same-policy alternatives are executed repeatedly; the difference in average correctness-efficiency utility is a gold credit label. These labels guide a parameter-frozen retrospective selector that provides turn-level advantages in a clipped policy objective, without a value critic, GAE, or online counterfactual branching.
QzGGstYqbH.key_idea: Use real-environment counterfactual rollouts from restored states to define gold turn credit, then distill that signal into an offline selector that scores turns for a critic-free policy gradient.
QzGGstYqbH.evidence: Counterfactual supervision from 4B and 9B policies before and after RL, evaluated on four evaluation sets at both actor scales including SWE-bench Pro and LiveCodeBench, with credit-removal and matched-policy probes.
QzGGstYqbH.claimed_gains: Outperforms the trained baselines (including GRPO) in seven of eight comparisons, with SWE-bench Pro gains over PPO of 4.52 and 4.79 percentage points at 4B and 9B, and matches the Base model on LiveCodeBench at 9B.
QzGGstYqbH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that grounding credit labels in real state-restored counterfactual execution is a clear, measurable improvement over heuristic or verbal-critique credit, and that distilling it into an offline selector is practical.
QzGGstYqbH.main_concern: The selector's label quality and cost are uncertain (low evaluator precision with no label-noise control, heavy offline annotation compute), and gains are not isolated from prompt engineering and extra inference compute.

ewzYQinhGA.one_liner: Proves oracle-complexity lower bounds for non-convex SGD under the Blum-Gladyshev (BG-0) variance condition and matches them with anchored, proximal SGD.
ewzYQinhGA.problem: SGD analysis assumes uniformly bounded variance, which often fails, and the oracle complexity of non-convex optimization under the weaker BG-0 quadratic-growth variance condition is underexplored.
ewzYQinhGA.method: The paper proves information-theoretic lower bounds under BG-0 and proposes PASTA (Proximally Anchored STochastic Approximation), a framework whose instantiations combine dynamic batching and gradient estimation with Halpern anchoring and Tikhonov regularization to match the bounds.
ewzYQinhGA.key_idea: Combine dynamic batching, which scales sampling with the iterate-dependent variance, with Halpern anchoring and Tikhonov regularization to control trajectory-dependent noise.
ewzYQinhGA.evidence: Theoretical analysis: information-theoretic lower bounds and matching upper bounds in certain cases (abstract truncated before the algorithmic results).
ewzYQinhGA.claimed_gains: Finding an epsilon-stationary point requires Omega(eps^-6) BG-0 oracle queries for smooth functions and Omega(eps^-4) under mean-square smoothness, versus Omega(eps^-4) and Omega(eps^-3) under bounded variance.
ewzYQinhGA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree BG-0 is a meaningful relaxation of bounded variance and that the lower bounds and matching algorithms clarify the fundamental cost of that relaxation.
ewzYQinhGA.main_concern: The algorithm depends on global constants that are hard to know in advance and may need large batch sizes, and one review finds an incorrect step in the PL proof (Appendix C.7).

lVt1NqKlvi.one_liner: Introduces FEEL, an egocentric vision-touch-pose force-estimation benchmark, and EgoForce, a GRU model with residual experts on a Laplace force head.
lVt1NqKlvi.problem: Embodied models must map visual appearance and hand motion to continuous contact forces despite occlusion and visual-physical mismatch, and this physical intuition is rarely measured quantitatively.
lVt1NqKlvi.method: FEEL is a controlled benchmark of 3,069 vision-touch-pose episodes across ten object and fill-state categories. EgoForce uses a GRU for visual-state aggregation and two softly weighted residual experts that refine a shared Laplace force head, and transformer policies, flow-matching VLAs, generalist multimodal policies, and vision encoders are evaluated on current-force prediction.
lVt1NqKlvi.key_idea: Refine a shared Laplace force head with two softly weighted residual experts on top of a GRU that aggregates visual and hand-state history.
lVt1NqKlvi.evidence: Current-force prediction from RGB and hand state on FEEL across transformer regression policies, flow-matching VLAs, generalist multimodal policies, and vision-foundation encoders, with an out-of-distribution test on empty milk containers.
lVt1NqKlvi.claimed_gains: The 36.18 M-parameter EgoForce achieves test contact MAE of 7.3386 N, contact R^2 of 0.1965, contact Pearson r of 0.3022, and pooled F1 of 0.8395, with OOD contact r of 0.4067 and pooled F1 of 0.8934; baseline numbers are not stated in the abstract.
lVt1NqKlvi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree FEEL is a useful, well-designed controlled resource for continuous fingertip-force estimation, with fragile, deformable, and variable-load cases and concrete hardware and alignment details.
lVt1NqKlvi.main_concern: The physical-intuition framing (pre-contact anticipation, overshoot under deceptive appearance) is not matched by the evaluation, which only scores current contact force from observations that already include post-contact cues.

wJ3eerD0Gz.one_liner: RL-trained planner issues tool calls or abstract intents; a resolver repairs or decomposes them over a 134-tool video library.
wJ3eerD0Gz.problem: Video agents expose few coarse retrieval and inspection tools, and hierarchical agents leave it underspecified how abstract reasoning intents become executable tool calls.
wJ3eerD0Gz.method: The MetaAug-Video Tool Library (MVTL) has 26 base tools for multimodal evidence acquisition and 108 meta tools for operations on intermediate results. In ReTool-Video, a planner emits executable tool calls or abstract intents, a resolver repairs, substitutes, or recursively decomposes intents into validated tool calls, and the planner is optimized with reinforcement learning.
wJ3eerD0Gz.key_idea: Separate planning from tool grounding: a frozen resolver turns the planner's abstract intents into validated tool calls via argument repair, substitution, and recursive decomposition.
wJ3eerD0Gz.evidence: Evaluated on MVBench, MLVU, and Video-MME (without subtitles) with a Qwen3.5-9B backbone, with ablations of Planner-Resolver grounding and planner RL and a second backbone, per the abstract and reviews.
wJ3eerD0Gz.claimed_gains: Achieves 72.9, 81.5, and 76.6 accuracy on MVBench, MLVU, and Video-MME w/o sub., and Planner-Resolver grounding improves MLVU accuracy by 13.1 percentage points under the same Qwen3.5-9B backbone and tool library without planner RL.
wJ3eerD0Gz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the Planner-Resolver design is well motivated, reduces the planner's burden when many tools have different interfaces, and yields competitive results on MVBench, MLVU, and Video-MME.
wJ3eerD0Gz.main_concern: The need for the large tool library is unclear (five tools account for 94.62% of calls), compute overhead of recursive grounding is unreported, and the resolver is not trained.

0j1zyCWT7r.one_liner: Diagnoses looped Transformers on a task ladder separating failures to find operands from failures to compute with them.
0j1zyCWT7r.problem: It is unclear which tasks looped Transformers can generalize to compositionally and why they fail, since syntax inference (locating operands) and syntax execution (computing) are confounded.
0j1zyCWT7r.method: A task ladder from prefix scans to serialized arithmetic trees progressively raises the difficulty of syntax inference, with models trained on small compositions and tested on larger ones. Because the reference DAG is known, true operands can be supplied, for example by restricting a frozen model's attention to the true operand positions.
0j1zyCWT7r.key_idea: Use tasks with a fully known reference computation to supply true operand positions at test time and isolate syntax inference from syntax execution as the cause of failure.
0j1zyCWT7r.evidence: Looped models trained on small compositions and tested on larger ones across the ladder, with larger models, other positional encodings, chain-of-thought, and a pretrained 3.5B looped model, plus attention-restriction interventions.
0j1zyCWT7r.claimed_gains: not stated; diagnostic study finding that looped models extrapolate only when each operand lies at a fixed offset from its operation.
0j1zyCWT7r.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the hypothesis is clearly testable and the task ladder with a known reference DAG is a careful setup that separates syntax inference from execution.
0j1zyCWT7r.main_concern: The causal attribution to syntax inference is broader than the intervention supports (supplying operands raises right-caterpillar accuracy only modestly), and key controls such as training length and a mask-free adaptation baseline are missing.

1v85Pec79o.one_liner: Self-evolving robot agent pairing a VLA loop with a code loop and consolidating physically verified solutions into structured executable memory.
1v85Pec79o.problem: Embodied agents with foundation models and tools tend to approach new problems from scratch, so successful exploration gives little benefit to later interactions.
1v85Pec79o.method: EvoRAM combines a VLA loop for reactive interaction with a code loop for deliberate exploration and reproducible execution. Solutions found in exploration are physically verified and consolidated into structured executable memory (object, task, and plan memory) that is reused, adapted, and refined on later problems.
1v85Pec79o.key_idea: Consolidate physically verified code solutions into executable object, task, and plan memory, while VLA behaviors broaden code exploration and verified code recovers VLA failures.
1v85Pec79o.evidence: Simulation on LIBERO, where memory grows from empty over a single accumulation trajectory, and real-world dual-arm robot tasks such as bimanual bottle unscrewing, cube-stacking recovery, and package grasping.
1v85Pec79o.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract; reviews cite 121 of 130 LIBERO tasks solved (93.1%).
1v85Pec79o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the Object/Task/Plan memory abstraction and bidirectional code-VLA collaboration are concrete and useful, with real-world recalibration and recovery demonstrations.
1v85Pec79o.main_concern: No quantitative baselines or ablations separate the benefit of memory from extra attempts, and the 93.1% LIBERO result is a single accumulation trajectory that does not show repeatability.

ltgypB859e.one_liner: Hierarchical mobile-manipulation policy that lifts one walkthrough video into explicit 3D to guide a VLA in unseen homes.
ltgypB859e.problem: VLA mobile manipulators are brittle in unfamiliar multi-room environments because they fall back to reactive exploration when task-relevant locations move outside familiar layouts.
ltgypB859e.method: The paper studies how a prior walkthrough video should represent spatial context, finds that the Qwen3D recipe that explicitly encodes 3D structure transfers best, and builds a hierarchical policy in which a spatial planner conditioned on a single environment video guides a flat VLA executor.
ltgypB859e.key_idea: Condition a VLA with navigation guidance from a planner that encodes a single walkthrough video as explicit 3D structure, rather than relying on in-distribution spatial prediction accuracy.
ltgypB859e.evidence: Simulated multi-room mobile manipulation with oracle-guidance diagnostics and comparisons of spatial-model recipes as planners, including a second simulator, with 16 tour frames per episode (per reviews).
ltgypB859e.claimed_gains: The strongest policy more than doubles the placement rate of its flat counterpart (24.8% vs. 10.9%) in the hardest setup.
ltgypB859e.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the single-video spatial guidance is intuitive and that the diagnostics show strong in-distribution spatial prediction does not predict transfer, with a clear navigation improvement.
ltgypB859e.main_concern: The benefit of explicit 3D encoding is confounded by extra geometry inputs and different training settings, and the evaluation is narrow (simulation only, task-informed tours that skip decoy rooms).

SXbnBpfnux.one_liner: Graph unlearning that forgets in stages ordered by estimated unlearning difficulty, using a distribution-level NPO objective at each stage.
SXbnBpfnux.problem: Existing graph unlearning methods apply one forgetting operation to the whole forget set and lose substantial utility at large deletion ratios (catastrophic unlearning).
SXbnBpfnux.method: CUNO removes the forget set progressively over multiple stages, ordering samples by estimated unlearning difficulty. At each stage a distribution-level negative preference optimization objective steers the model away from its original behavior on the current forget subset while preserving retained performance.
SXbnBpfnux.key_idea: Order forget samples by estimated unlearning difficulty into curriculum stages and apply NPO per stage so the objective focuses on not-yet-forgotten samples.
SXbnBpfnux.evidence: Experiments across three datasets and three GNN architectures at multiple deletion rates up to 50%, plus theory on stage-wise convergence, overlap-dependent drift, and gradient dispersion.
SXbnBpfnux.claimed_gains: Substantially narrows the utility gap to the retraining reference across all deletion rates evaluated; at 20% deletion it retains 74% of the original (abstract truncated).
SXbnBpfnux.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree mass deletion is an important, underexplored regime and that CUNO gives consistent utility gains across datasets, GNN architectures, and deletion rates.
SXbnBpfnux.main_concern: The curriculum's contribution is not isolated (no shuffled-order control, and NPO accounts for most of the gain), and novelty relative to prior curriculum-based unlearning such as CUFG and CAU is not compared.

NtZ3qeRWiu.one_liner: World-action model conditioned on object-centric relational task specifications that transfer robot and human demonstrations without task-aligned pairs.
NtZ3qeRWiu.problem: In-context robot learning from demonstrations across embodiments needs costly task-aligned demonstration-execution pairs.
NtZ3qeRWiu.method: IntentWAM uses an Object-Centric Relational Task Specification (ORTS) that encodes task roles, endpoint scene graphs, and object dynamics from robot and human demonstrations. With target-scene role bindings it yields intent tokens that guide visual-future prediction and action generation; training uses task-level associations, and deployment keeps parameters fixed.
NtZ3qeRWiu.key_idea: Represent demonstrations as embodiment-agnostic object-centric task intent (roles, endpoint scene graphs, object motion) so one fixed policy can consume robot or human demonstrations.
NtZ3qeRWiu.evidence: Seven held-out RoboTwin tasks with robot and generated human demonstrations, real-world candle lighting with filmed human demonstrations, and a scrambled-egg task excluded from training and adaptation data.
NtZ3qeRWiu.claimed_gains: One checkpoint achieves 47.97-48.26% mean success on seven held-out RoboTwin tasks; candle lighting reaches 47.50% vs 27.50% for the strongest baseline, and scrambled egg 40.0% vs 5.0% for matched raw-video conditioning.
NtZ3qeRWiu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the object-centric task-intent interface is well motivated, embodiment-agnostic, and supported by well-designed simulation experiments.
NtZ3qeRWiu.main_concern: Comparisons confound the interface with different checkpoints, training mixtures, and extra perception models (no matched raw-video or pairing controls), and novelty over Zero-WAM is limited.

Kff8gFq3Ea.one_liner: A 337-case video benchmark with case-specific rubrics that scores whether generated videos realize unstated spatial consequences of an action.
Kff8gFq3Ea.problem: A generated video can depict the requested action while failing to realize its spatial consequences, which instruction-following and visual-quality metrics do not capture.
Kff8gFq3Ea.method: MTS-Bench pairs image-to-video and text-to-video cases across scene, view, and coupled motion, with rubrics for initial-state fidelity, instruction execution, consequence prediction, temporal consistency, and endpoint completion. A VLM scorer audited against blinded human ratings and selectively calibrated by dimension scores nine I2V and eight T2V generators.
Kff8gFq3Ea.key_idea: Score interventions whose spatial consequences are not narrated in the prompt, with case-specific rubrics and a human-audited, dimension-calibrated VLM judge.
Kff8gFq3Ea.evidence: Nine I2V and eight T2V generators on a fixed 150-case subset of the 337 cases, with evaluator analysis against blinded human ratings.
Kff8gFq3Ea.claimed_gains: The highest-scoring generator obtains 80.2 on instruction following and 56.2 on consequence prediction in I2V; the corresponding T2V scores are 77.2 and 62.4 out of 100.
Kff8gFq3Ea.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the action-versus-spatial-outcome distinction is a genuine gap, the case-specific rubrics are more targeted than generic metrics, and the evaluator analysis is transparent and informative.
Kff8gFq3Ea.main_concern: Evaluation reliability is weak: a single human annotator, small audit sets of 40 cases per modality reused for calibration, and low video-level direction accuracy of the proprietary VLM judge (61.0% I2V, 70.2% T2V).

oztuqLyPXV.one_liner: Studies progressive depth growth, inserting layers during training, in MAE and DINOv3 pretraining and its effect on representations.
oztuqLyPXV.problem: How progressive depth growth affects representation quality and computation in self-supervised vision transformers is unclear, despite renewed interest from language-model training.
oztuqLyPXV.method: The paper systematically grows MAE and DINOv3 vision transformers by inserting layers during pretraining, with several growth strategies and schedules, and analyzes downstream global and dense tasks, intermediate-layer performance, and internal attention patterns.
oztuqLyPXV.key_idea: Start from a shallow ViT and insert layers during self-supervised pretraining, then compare to a fixed-depth model with matched steps, data exposure, final architecture, and inference cost.
oztuqLyPXV.evidence: MAE (two model sizes) and DINOv3 pretraining evaluated on global and dense tasks with controls such as a stronger WSD recipe, longer training, and frozen-teacher distillation, per the abstract and reviews.
oztuqLyPXV.claimed_gains: Growing improves downstream performance while reducing training FLOPs by 13.9-24.8%, with ImageNet linear-probe accuracy gains of up to 3.36 percentage points.
oztuqLyPXV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study is systematic and well controlled, with efficiency gains that survive stronger MAE recipes and span global and dense tasks.
oztuqLyPXV.main_concern: Each configuration uses a single pretraining run (reported deviations cover only probe seeds), so small DINOv3 gains are not established, and published growth methods such as LiGO, AutoProg, and EfficientTrain++ are not compared.

n3fdO8qFzG.one_liner: Improves length extrapolation by moving dropout to just before the linear projection (after normalization), plus a variance-preserving affine dropout variant.
n3fdO8qFzG.problem: Length generalization is attributed to positional encoding and attention design, but the training procedure also matters, and standard dropout before layer normalization causes a systematic distributional mismatch.
n3fdO8qFzG.method: The paper shows weight decay can hinder extrapolation, and that placing dropout just before the linear projection removes the mean and variance mismatch caused by dropout before layer normalization. It also proposes Variance-Preserving Affine Dropout (VPAD), which further reduces the pre-activation variance mismatch.
n3fdO8qFzG.key_idea: Apply dropout after normalization, just before the linear projection, so dropout noise does not shift pre-activation statistics between training and longer contexts.
n3fdO8qFzG.evidence: Training from scratch and continual pre-training of a SmolLM3 variant with sliding window attention and of Mamba2, evaluated on Needle-in-a-Haystack, RULER, and HELMET, with theory on pre-activation mismatch.
n3fdO8qFzG.claimed_gains: A modified SmolLM3 with sliding window attention, continually pre-trained with dropout, extrapolates perfectly to 64x on Needle-in-a-Haystack and far beyond the pre-training context on RULER and HELMET.
n3fdO8qFzG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the dropout-placement results are convincing and practical across from-scratch and continual pretraining, benchmarks, and architectures including Mamba2.
n3fdO8qFzG.main_concern: The cause is not established: the theory (Proposition 3 covariance formula) does not cover the per-token implementation, and placement may change which signal is noised or suppress a positional shortcut rather than fix the mismatch.

VNpw2MHzD4.one_liner: One AND/OR energy tree evaluated at two resolutions; learned contraction-error estimates decide which nodes to expand and when to stop.
VNpw2MHzD4.problem: Fast action selection and slow deliberation are usually separate computational modes, rather than adjustable levels of one decision model.
VNpw2MHzD4.method: A dual-resolution recursive energy model puts contracted macro-energies and explicitly composed AND/OR subtrees on a common energy scale. Wake-sleep training distills expanded subtree energies into macro-energies and learns their contraction errors, which guide frontier expansion and stopping when the action-energy margin permits.
VNpw2MHzD4.key_idea: Learn macro-energies that approximate expanded subtrees plus contraction-error estimates, and expand only frontier nodes until the action-energy margin covers the remaining error.
VNpw2MHzD4.evidence: BabyAI, MiniHack, and Overcooked-AI, compared with a Full expansion model and matched-budget controls, with held-out decision-state latency tests and a BossLevel transfer test.
VNpw2MHzD4.claimed_gains: Reduces explicit recursive expansion by 50.88-77.74% while retaining near-Full macro success, and cuts task-averaged P50 action-selection latency by 27.6-60.2% relative to Full while retaining at least 99.2% (abstract truncated).
VNpw2MHzD4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the common-energy interface gives a coherent, interpretable mechanism for per-subtree adaptive computation with a winner-preservation argument and clear presentation.
VNpw2MHzD4.main_concern: The AND/OR structures are generated by LLM agents with manual auditing, and efficiency and stopping reliability under shift are limited (BossLevel falls back to near-full expansion, with some Full-winner disagreement).

lwPX4Nyq8J.one_liner: Replaces one-hot classification heads in neural decoders with text-derived class prototypes, aligning neural features to natural-language class descriptions.
lwPX4Nyq8J.problem: Class-label supervision leaves relationships among classes implicit in brain-computer-interface decoding.
lwPX4Nyq8J.method: Language as Supervision (LaS) aligns neural features with natural-language class descriptions through learned projections and predicts classes using candidate text prototypes. It is evaluated across seven encoder architectures on visual, motor, and speech decoding from scalp and intracranial recordings, with a bidirectional alignment analysis and dual-sided attribution.
lwPX4Nyq8J.key_idea: Classify by matching projected neural features to learned-projected text embeddings of class descriptions, so new candidates can be expressed through their relation to seen classes.
lwPX4Nyq8J.evidence: Seven encoders on motor imagery, SSVEP, and intracranial speech decoding, with session and subject adaptation and zero-shot SSVEP frequency identification, plus theory on bidirectional alignment.
lwPX4Nyq8J.claimed_gains: LaS improves mean speech-decoding accuracy by up to 9.33 percentage points over CLS baselines.
lwPX4Nyq8J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation is broad (several encoders and recording modalities) with consistent gains in all four speech encoders and informative adaptation and zero-shot analyses.
lwPX4Nyq8J.main_concern: Baseline comparisons do not isolate language supervision (different loss, readout, and regularization, and no random or learned prototype control), and novelty over similar text-aligned neural decoders is unclear.

ODnc0BqTZ5.one_liner: JAX suite of 17 differentiable, parallelizable tokamak control environments with 5 physics models, benchmarking RL, evolution strategies, and gradient methods.
ODnc0BqTZ5.problem: Applying RL to tokamak plasma control is held back by the lack of fast, configurable fusion-control environments.
ODnc0BqTZ5.method: Plasmax provides 17 differentiable, parallelizable environments for tokamak kinetic control built on 5 physics models for dynamics simulation. It supports comparisons of RL, evolution strategies, differentiating through the environment, and fixed actuator values, robustness tests under observation corruption such as noise or delays, and transfer between simulators of different fidelity.
ODnc0BqTZ5.key_idea: Implement tokamak simulators in JAX so they can be jit-compiled, run in thousands of parallel GPU instances, and differentiated through for gradient-based control.
ODnc0BqTZ5.evidence: Benchmarks of trajectory and policy optimization methods (RL, ES, backpropagation through the environment, fixed actuators) across tasks, with robustness and cross-simulator transfer tests and speed comparisons with prior work.
ODnc0BqTZ5.claimed_gains: Up to a 1103x speedup over prior work and training an RL agent in 7 minutes on hardware accelerators; untuned open-loop control optimized with CMA-ES performs 30% better than the best untuned RL (abstract truncated).
ODnc0BqTZ5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the environment suite is a fast, broad, useful testbed for fusion-control research, with a unified API, multiple backends, and baselines spanning RL, open-loop optimization, and backpropagation.
ODnc0BqTZ5.main_concern: The headline results are weakly supported (the 1103x speedup compares a single-environment CPU baseline to a 16384-environment GPU run, and the open-loop-beats-RL result rests on untuned, short-horizon RL baselines and survival-dominated rewards).

m1dirAPhnL.one_liner: Fine-tunes a pre-trained model for continual learning by freezing periodic blocks and flattening the gradient singular-value spectrum, mimicking shallow-wide networks.
m1dirAPhnL.problem: Full fine-tuning of pre-trained models causes catastrophic forgetting, while frozen-backbone methods with auxiliary modules limit plasticity and add inference overhead.
m1dirAPhnL.method: SW-Tune modulates the gradient subspace of a deep PTM to emulate shallow-and-wide learning dynamics without architectural changes. Periodic block freezing restricts training to an equidistant sparse subset of blocks, and gradient spectral flattening regularizes the singular-value spectrum of layer-wise gradients so updates span a broader orthogonal subspace.
m1dirAPhnL.key_idea: Train only periodically spaced blocks to reduce effective depth, and flatten the singular-value spectrum of layer-wise gradients to widen the effective update subspace.
m1dirAPhnL.evidence: Three benchmarks, two backbones, and five class orders with standard deviations, component and layer-layout ablations, and a comparison with SLCA/SLCA++ (per reviews).
m1dirAPhnL.claimed_gains: Outperforms existing PTM-based continual learning methods (abstract truncated); no numbers stated.
m1dirAPhnL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, adds no inference overhead, and shows consistent improvements across three benchmarks with comprehensive experiments.
m1dirAPhnL.main_concern: The shallow-wide interpretation is not well justified (blocks are frozen without changing depth), the annealing schedule needs the total task count in advance, and training cost is higher with some strong baselines missing.

zSOWJCx8An.one_liner: Samples video-diffusion noise once in a 3D space over the camera frusta and projects it to per-view 2D noise.
zSOWJCx8An.problem: Camera-controlled video diffusion starts from randomly sampled noise that is agnostic to scene geometry, so different views are generated from unrelated noise.
zSOWJCx8An.method: WorldNoise constructs a 3D noise space over the world region covered by the camera frusta along the trajectory and distributes randomness through it. It projects the world-space randomness into view-specific 2D noise with an EWA-based projection, plus residual and normalization steps to maintain the desired noise statistics.
zSOWJCx8An.key_idea: Sample noise once in a 3D world space and project it into each view with an EWA-based projection, keeping per-view noise statistics.
zSOWJCx8An.evidence: Same-backbone comparisons for camera control and long-horizon experiments, on DL3DV against ScoPE and against a Wan baseline with LoRA rank 32 (per reviews); the abstract is truncated before results.
zSOWJCx8An.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea of geometry-structured noise is natural and principled, simple to follow, and gives convincing same-backbone improvements in camera control for short videos.
zSOWJCx8An.main_concern: The long-horizon claim is not isolated from visual-memory and geometry-update components, and novelty is overstated given prior 3D-structured noise work such as MultiDiff, CFD, and ConsistDreamer.

c3NWMlZw4r.one_liner: Controlled evaluation using byte-identical baseline copies to separate answer coverage from real specialization in generated LLM harnesses.
c3NWMlZw4r.problem: Extra answer coverage can come from repeatedly running the same program, so gains from generated task-specialized harnesses are hard to distinguish from sampling.
c3NWMlZw4r.method: The controlled evaluation separates answer coverage, repeatable task advantages, and gains from pre-execution selection. On MATH-500, eight generated harnesses plus a baseline are compared with nine byte-identical baseline copies, with three executions per member.
c3NWMlZw4r.key_idea: Use identical-code copies of the baseline as a control population to measure how much oracle headroom and score repeatability arise without any specialization.
c3NWMlZw4r.evidence: 386 MATH-500 tasks with eight generated harnesses, nine identical baseline copies, and three executions each, plus known-truth calibration of the diagnostic and BIRD traces.
c3NWMlZw4r.claimed_gains: Identical programs yield 2.16 percentage points of oracle headroom, the frozen selector gains 0.00 percentage points, and both populations reach 98.70% oracle coverage at 27 harness executions, with the generated panel using 4.0 times as many tokens.
c3NWMlZw4r.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the byte-identical clone control is a strong methodological contribution that shows coverage alone cannot establish specialization and that repeatable differences mostly reflect persistent weaknesses.
c3NWMlZw4r.main_concern: The diagnostic is underpowered (0% detection power at three repeats), and the study uses one solver, a small panel, a ceiling-limited 95.85% baseline, and execution-matched rather than token-matched budgets.

UGlFNGIgGF.one_liner: Adapts the l1 regularization strength during mirror-descent training, via top-k or sparsity-gap feedback, to hit a target sparsity.
UGlFNGIgGF.problem: The l1 regularization parameter in mirror-descent sparse training only controls sparsity indirectly, so reaching a target sparsity requires expensive trial-and-error sweeps.
UGlFNGIgGF.method: Two online schemes adapt lambda during training: one based on the magnitude of the largest subgradients (TopK) and one based on the gap between current and target sparsity (SGap). A sparsity schedule extends this to intermediate targets, and a convergence analysis for adaptive lambda in mirror descent is provided.
UGlFNGIgGF.key_idea: Set the regularization strength each step from the (k+1)-th largest accumulated-gradient magnitude or from the current-versus-target sparsity gap, so the target sparsity is reached without sweeping lambda.
UGlFNGIgGF.evidence: CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, and ImageNet-1K with multiple architectures and three seeds, compared with tuned fixed-lambda mirror descent and GraNet.
UGlFNGIgGF.claimed_gains: Both schemes reliably reach the final and scheduled intermediate sparsity targets and outperform a tuned fixed lambda at matched sparsity (abstract truncated); no numbers stated in the abstract.
UGlFNGIgGF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the schemes let users specify the target sparsity within a single run, are simple and well motivated, and work across three datasets and several architectures.
UGlFNGIgGF.main_concern: The convergence analysis does not cover the stochastic, momentum-based algorithms actually used, and some gains come with higher training FLOPs or unmatched sparsity levels, with limited novelty over top-k style methods.

Am6lbNoDTY.one_liner: Characterizes SDS, SDI, and VSD as particle variational inference and proposes PFD, which distills with probability-flow ODE solves.
Am6lbNoDTY.problem: The distributions induced by score distillation methods are not well understood, with SDS collapsing onto modes and SDI contracting the target.
Am6lbNoDTY.method: The paper extends the particle variational inference view of VSD to SDS and SDI, showing SDS collapses onto point masses near target modes and SDI converges to a contracted target. Replacing Tweedie's single Euler step in SDI with a full reverse PF-ODE solve makes the target a fixed point, and dropping a Jacobian from the resulting gradient gives Probability-Flow Distillation (PFD), which needs only the forward PF-ODE.
Am6lbNoDTY.key_idea: Replace the one-step Tweedie posterior mean in SDI with a full probability-flow ODE solve, then drop a Jacobian so only the forward PF-ODE is needed.
Am6lbNoDTY.evidence: Synthetic targets, CelebA with multiple seeds, and text-to-3D generation under the same prior model, representation, and optimizer as VSD.
Am6lbNoDTY.claimed_gains: Experiments are said to support the analysis and show practical effectiveness of PFD; no numbers stated in the abstract (the TLDR says on par with or better than VSD).
Am6lbNoDTY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unified particle variational inference view is useful, explaining mode collapse in SDS and why SDI needs a negative classifier-free guidance scale.
Am6lbNoDTY.main_concern: Gains over VSD are slight (similar quality metrics, worse FID in one table, both slow), and novelty over SDS-Bridge and PF-ODE-based distillation methods such as Consistent Flow Distillation is under-discussed.

nuhWiLJZUL.one_liner: Pairs a compact VLM with a feature matcher for cross-view point correspondence, trained with SFT then GRPO using distance reward.
nuhWiLJZUL.problem: VLMs confuse similar object instances under viewpoint change because fine-grained correspondence is hard to infer from global visual context alone.
nuhWiLJZUL.method: MatchVLM integrates local feature matching with a compact VLM in two stages: Reference-Oriented Spatial Perception Learning supervises reference reliability assessment and answer prediction via SFT, then Distance-Aware Point Refinement applies GRPO with a point-level distance reward and a curriculum emphasizing cases that remain hard after SFT. The paper also introduces CVPC-Bench with 500 annotated point pairs.
nuhWiLJZUL.key_idea: Feed local matcher correspondences to the VLM as reference evidence and refine its point predictions with GRPO using a reward equal to the spatial distance error.
nuhWiLJZUL.evidence: CrossPoint-Bench against evaluated VLMs and the new CVPC-Bench (500 manually annotated pairs, eight outdoor and two indoor scenes) against CroPond-3B and CroPond-7B in zero-shot evaluation.
nuhWiLJZUL.claimed_gains: MatchVLM-3B achieves the highest overall Score on CrossPoint-Bench among the evaluated models (abstract truncated); no numbers stated.
nuhWiLJZUL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining local matching evidence with VLM reasoning is well motivated, with a 3B model outperforming larger VLMs and CroPond-7B at lower inference cost.
nuhWiLJZUL.main_concern: The added value of the VLM and RL is unclear without standalone matcher baselines (e.g., MASt3R, RoMa v2) or SFT with a distance loss, and ablations and robustness tests are limited.

U3tUQMooJO.one_liner: Non-vacuous PAC-Bayes compression bounds for RLVR-tuned billion-parameter LLMs, using Gumbel-max for token sampling and a highly compressible fine-tuning pipeline.
U3tUQMooJO.problem: The generalization of LLMs trained with reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards is poorly understood, and existing bounds are vacuous at billion-parameter scale.
U3tUQMooJO.method: The paper adapts PAC-Bayes compression bounds and handles token-generation stochasticity with the Gumbel-max reparameterization. Progressive RLVR combines RLVR with on-policy distillation, TinyLoRA, and quantization to produce highly compressible weight updates.
U3tUQMooJO.key_idea: Make RLVR updates tiny, quantized, and distilled so their description length is small enough for a PAC-Bayes compression bound to be non-vacuous.
U3tUQMooJO.evidence: Bounds evaluated for a 4B-parameter model in four domains: math, programming, general-knowledge reasoning, and text-to-SQL, with ablations over distillation, adapter choice, and quantization.
U3tUQMooJO.claimed_gains: Progressive RLVR retains 84-97% of standard LoRA performance with weight updates 14,796x more compressible, and the bounds exceed base-model accuracy by 9-51% and lie within 6-11% of fine-tuned accuracy.
U3tUQMooJO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree these are the first non-vacuous, numerically meaningful generalization bounds at billion-parameter LLM post-training scale, reported with penalty decompositions across four domains.
U3tUQMooJO.main_concern: The bound is informative only with very few, low-precision tunable parameters (sacrificing performance), and its validity requires that the checkpoint and quantization level were fixed before inspecting the evaluation subsample.

Epa46495zY.one_liner: Distills a latent 3D generator into one step using a variational objective combining image reconstruction with teacher distribution matching.
Epa46495zY.problem: Distilled few-step latent 3D generators lose quality sharply, especially at a single step, while many-step teachers are too slow for interactive use.
Epa46495zY.method: A variational objective unifies conditioning-image reconstruction with distribution matching against a teacher 3D generator. On top of it, complementary 2D supervision signals are added: feature-distribution matching, semantic consistency, and human preference.
Epa46495zY.key_idea: Supervise the one-step 3D generator with rendered 2D images through a variational objective that pairs conditioning-image reconstruction with a KL-style match to the teacher.
Epa46495zY.evidence: Single-step comparisons against distilled baselines such as MDT-dist, MeanFlow, and DMD on the LiTo backbone, with ablations of each supervision signal and runtime measurements.
Epa46495zY.claimed_gains: Reduces FID by 47% over the strongest baseline while running in 67.5 ms on an NVIDIA B200 GPU and 2.4 seconds on a MacBook Pro with M5 Max.
Epa46495zY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the single-step results show substantial speed and quality gains (novel-view FID and input fidelity), supported by ablations showing image supervision as the main source of improvement.
Epa46495zY.main_concern: The roles of the KL and human-preference terms are unclear (removing either improves reported metrics), the KL-gradient sign differs between Eq. 3 and Eq. 18, and evaluation is only on the LiTo backbone.

zwqKF5ov1l.one_liner: Compares skill representations against measured transfer, finds shared behavioral primitives, and uses them to choose source skills for continual learning.
zwqKF5ov1l.problem: It is unclear which relationships among robotic skills are relevant to transfer and how they should be characterized.
zwqKF5ov1l.method: RoboTaskonomy builds skill relationships from task attributes, fine-grained trajectories, and local motion distributions, and checks each against measured transfer effects. It then discovers behavioral primitives shared across skills, represents skills as their combinations, and uses this structure to guide prior-skill selection in continual learning.
zwqKF5ov1l.key_idea: Represent skills by local motion distributions, validated against measured transfer outcomes, and decompose them into shared primitives to retrieve useful prior skills.
zwqKF5ov1l.evidence: Correspondence analysis against measured transfer effects across directed skill pairs, then continual-learning experiments in simulation and on a real robot (per the abstract and reviews).
zwqKF5ov1l.claimed_gains: Significantly improves new-skill acquisition in both simulation and real-world tasks; no numbers stated in the abstract.
zwqKF5ov1l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework is systematic, grounds skill representations in measured transfer outcomes rather than intuition, and shows local motion distributions align best with transfer.
zwqKF5ov1l.main_concern: The best representation is built from heuristic statistics with modest correlation to transfer, primitives do not clearly beat raw motion distributions, and continual-learning results use fixed task orders with no repeated-run uncertainty.

PUxZ7rfZkh.one_liner: Meta-trains RL algorithms inside learned world models instead of physics simulators, then transfers the discovered algorithm to the real simulator.
PUxZ7rfZkh.problem: Meta-RL algorithm discovery is limited by the high cost of simulating environments for meta-training.
PUxZ7rfZkh.method: Model-Based Meta-Learning (MBML) uses learned world models as an efficient substitute for environment simulation during meta-training. Policies trained in the world models fail to transfer to the simulator, but the algorithms discovered there transfer.
PUxZ7rfZkh.key_idea: Run the inner RL loops of meta-training inside a learned world model, relying on the learned algorithm, not the policy, to transfer to the true simulator.
PUxZ7rfZkh.evidence: Meta-training in a world model of HalfCheetah and meta-testing on unseen continuous control environments such as Walker2d and Hopper, compared with meta-RL using physics simulators.
PUxZ7rfZkh.claimed_gains: Matches the performance of meta-RL with environment physics simulators at a fraction of the time and compute, and a meta-learned algorithm that significantly outperforms prior work on unseen continuous control environments; no numbers stated.
PUxZ7rfZkh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the finding that discovered algorithms transfer even when policies do not is encouraging and valuable, and that the setup separates meta-training, validation, and test cleanly.
PUxZ7rfZkh.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited and the evaluation is narrow (a single world model and few meta-test environments, with dependence on a 24-hour stopping condition), so generality of the result is unclear.

zN8oCFWHrS.one_liner: Rescales per-token router gradients in MoE fine-tuning so each expert's estimated self-region tendency is near zero regardless of its exposure.
zN8oCFWHrS.problem: In MoE fine-tuning, frequently selected experts receive more direct router gradients and have more influence on routing boundaries, causing exposure-induced routing drift from pretrained routing.
zN8oCFWHrS.method: Gradient Rebalancing (GR) targets each expert's self-region tendency, a first-order estimate of the change in its routing-region mass from its own router update. It decomposes this tendency into token-level contributions to region expansion and contraction and selectively attenuates them, without load-balancing constraints or freezing the router.
zN8oCFWHrS.key_idea: Attenuate token-level router-gradient contributions to region expansion and contraction so each expert's first-order routing-region change from its own update is near zero.
zN8oCFWHrS.evidence: Fine-tuning experiments across multiple MoE architectures and task families with ablations on the region-influence estimate (abstract truncated before results).
zN8oCFWHrS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem of separating useful downstream load imbalance from exposure-induced routing drift is meaningful, with an expert-specific, sign-preserving correction supported by experiments.
zN8oCFWHrS.main_concern: The evidence is thin: single runs without uncertainty and modest, non-uniform gains, plus little validation that the batch-level smooth estimate tracks real Top-k routing changes or novelty over routing-preservation methods.

Di6a0orL7v.one_liner: Benchmark and agent for linking events with spatial context in long egocentric videos, using targeted visual checks by parallel verifiers.
Di6a0orL7v.problem: Long video benchmarks do not test connecting events to the spatial contexts where they occurred, and existing memory methods show evidence gaps.
Di6a0orL7v.method: SENRI-Bench has 466 manually annotated multiple-choice questions over 10 self-recorded videos (about 25.3 hours) across six task types in Event-to-Space and Space-to-Event directions; SENRI-Agent uses Target-Guided Visual Check to propose local check tasks for parallel verifiers and integrates their reports into a working memory.
Di6a0orL7v.key_idea: A controller proposes local visual check tasks for a target, parallel verifiers inspect the video, and their reports go into a working memory layered over existing memory systems.
Di6a0orL7v.evidence: Evaluates three paradigms (direct perception, evidence seeking, persistent memory) on SENRI-Bench and adds SENRI-Agent to existing memory baselines.
Di6a0orL7v.claimed_gains: Benchmark of 466 questions over 10 videos with about 25.3 hours of content; SENRI-Agent improves existing baselines without modifying their stored memories, with no numeric gain in the visible abstract.
Di6a0orL7v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the space-event task meaningful and underserved by current benchmarks, and long uncut real-place recordings valuable.
Di6a0orL7v.main_concern: The benchmark is small so per-task margins of error are large, questions were written by the person who filmed each video without agreement or human-accuracy checks, and gains cannot be attributed to spatial modeling.

bI5Ipzccvt.one_liner: Recasts predictive coding networks as hierarchical Gaussian filters with precision-weighted closed-form updates, removing iterative inference.
bI5Ipzccvt.problem: Predictive coding networks are slower than backpropagation and degrade sharply with depth because they fix the precision matrix to the identity, discarding precision-weighted prediction errors.
bI5Ipzccvt.method: They express predictive coding networks as deep hierarchical Gaussian filters, restoring precision-weighted message passing with Hebbian-compatible update rules. Activations, weights, and precisions are learned under one free-energy objective with no global error signal, and inference resolves without iterations or automatic differentiation.
bI5Ipzccvt.key_idea: Replace identity precision with learned per-layer precision in a hierarchical Gaussian filter, so variational inference resolves in closed form without iterative relaxation.
bI5Ipzccvt.evidence: FashionMNIST wall-clock and convergence comparisons with backpropagation, online, data-efficiency, and concept-drift tasks, and convolutional and attentional architectures at various depths.
bI5Ipzccvt.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports near-backprop wall-clock cost per epoch, fewer epochs to converge, and backprop-matching performance on convolutional and attentional architectures, without numbers)
