bI5Ipzccvt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning precision with closed-form inference is a meaningful direction that gets close to backpropagation without iterative relaxation, with encouraging online and continual results.
bI5Ipzccvt.main_concern: The efficiency and architecture-agnostic claims are weakly supported (timing only for small MLPs in the appendix, relatively shallow networks), and single-step inference resembles prior Z-IL.

QsmIQqCdXy.one_liner: Audit showing agent-memory benchmarks credit unverified 'does not exist' answers, plus an evidence-based check of denials against the recording.
QsmIQqCdXy.problem: Memory benchmarks score the answer alone, so denial questions about items the recording never contained are credited without checking the claim about the whole recording, biasing scores.
QsmIQqCdXy.method: The paper adds a fixed completeness note to the reader's memory context to expose score inflation on denial questions, then proposes three mitigation strategies, including a recording check that verifies each credited denial against the recorded lists.
QsmIQqCdXy.key_idea: Scorers ignore whether a denial is grounded in the recording; an exhaustive-list check against the recording separates grounded denials from asserted ones.
QsmIQqCdXy.evidence: Controlled tests on LongMemEval-V2 and LoCoMo, including a fixed answer scored by four judge models, no-memory versus retrieval with and without the note, and the official reader with a 200K-token budget.
QsmIQqCdXy.claimed_gains: Not a method gain: on LongMemEval-V2 a fixed note raises the baseline's denial score from 16% to 72% (73% under the official reader and 200K-token budget) while false denials rise from 1 to 55; checked against the recording, at most 4 of 92 credited denials stand.
QsmIQqCdXy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper exposes a serious, well-controlled flaw in widely used agent-memory benchmarks that persists across many variations.
QsmIQqCdXy.main_concern: The contribution is an analysis of scoring rather than a new benchmark or method, with limited novelty over the known guessing-versus-abstention incentive and a recording check that is only a prototype covering 92 of 128 denial questions.

9SiffnkooL.one_liner: Adaptive quantum measurement framework that certifies fidelity-threshold clusterings through selective overlap tests and reused single-state evidence.
9SiffnkooL.problem: Quantum-kernel clustering estimates fidelities over all sample pairs, which needs measurements on Theta(n^2) pairs, and returns a partition without certifying that the measurements suffice to determine it.
9SiffnkooL.method: Q-Cert establishes within-cluster connectivity through selected overlap tests and reuses single-state measurements to exclude multiple cross-cluster edges. The evidence is integrated into confirmed and possible graphs that determine when the partition can be safely certified.
9SiffnkooL.key_idea: Maintain confirmed and possible edge graphs from connectivity-witness overlap tests and reusable exclusion measurements, and certify only when they pin down a unique partition.
9SiffnkooL.evidence: Theory (error probability bounds, completion of certification, measurement complexity) and simulations on constructed hidden-bridge and bounded-degree state families.
9SiffnkooL.claimed_gains: The probability of incorrectly certifying a partition is at most delta for arbitrary pure-state inputs, and under suitable connectivity-witness and reusable-separation conditions Q-Cert requires only O(n log(n/delta)) measurements.
9SiffnkooL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusing single-state measurements and certifying without recovering the full fidelity graph are interesting ideas, with comprehensive correctness and complexity analysis.
9SiffnkooL.main_concern: The near-linear guarantee needs strong structural conditions shown only on constructed state families, and the problem setup and novelty over prior task-aware measurement methods are questioned.

13FlZnpjSN.one_liner: Uses attention from identified retrieval heads as memory-use traces to guide targeted edits of an agent's persistent memory.
13FlZnpjSN.problem: Agent memory is updated from outcomes, trajectories, and reflections, which give little evidence of how retrieved memory was actually used in decisions, so memory-related error causes are hard to separate.
13FlZnpjSN.method: They identify model-specific retrieval heads and aggregate their attention into a segment-by-decision memory-use trace, validated with intervention experiments. AGMR compares the utilization expected from reflection with the observed trace to propose targeted memory edits.
13FlZnpjSN.key_idea: Aggregated retrieval-head attention over memory segments per decision reveals actual memory use, and mismatch with reflection-expected use drives targeted memory edits.
13FlZnpjSN.evidence: Three interactive benchmarks with two open-weight models (reviewers name Qwen2.5-7B and Llama3.1-8B), intervention experiments, and budget-matched text-only controls.
13FlZnpjSN.claimed_gains: AGMR improves task performance while generally reducing memory length across three interactive benchmarks and two models (the abstract gives no further figures).
13FlZnpjSN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the read-side perspective is a genuine contribution, with the trace validated by interventions and controls and gains over text-only refinement.
13FlZnpjSN.main_concern: The gain evidence is weak: only two small, dated models, three-run means without variance, a text-only control that already captures most of the improvement, and few memory baselines.

FXUofFDv35.one_liner: Tensor-parallel fine-tuning of mixtures of LoRA experts with partial factor replication, low-rank activation synchronization, and grouped matrix multiplication.
FXUofFDv35.problem: MoLE fine-tuning keeps training states for the whole expert pool, and joint expert and router updates need cross-GPU coordination while uneven expert batches hurt sparse computation efficiency.
FXUofFDv35.method: ParaMoLE uses partial factor replication and evaluates each selected expert within the backbone's tensor-parallel group, reuses reduced low-rank activations or activation gradients for expert and router updates, and uses grouped matrix multiplication for variable-sized expert batches without padding. It is shown equivalent to the original MoLE outputs and gradients in exact arithmetic.
FXUofFDv35.key_idea: Reuse reduced low-rank activations or their gradients to compute both expert-factor and router gradients, avoiding separate gradient synchronization of replicated factors.
FXUofFDv35.evidence: Five NLP datasets on 3B and 14B LLMs, measuring memory, training-step time, and communication against full-replication, sharding, and expert-parallel baselines.
FXUofFDv35.claimed_gains: Lower memory, training-step time, and communication on 3B and 14B LLMs across five NLP datasets, with comparable downstream quality.
FXUofFDv35.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the low-rank backward synchronization is well designed, supported by gradient derivations and an exact-equivalence analysis, and that it cuts communication volume.
FXUofFDv35.main_concern: Baselines use per-expert loops while ParaMoLE uses grouped GEMM, so the speedup mixes an existing technique with the proposed synchronization, and novelty beyond S-LoRA-style low-dimensional communication is questioned.

haTAwPC9IP.one_liner: Multi-expert online forecaster that routes on partial feedback and validates matured expert credit against current capability.
haTAwPC9IP.problem: Online time series forecasting must adapt while multi-step supervision arrives progressively: waiting for matured feedback delays adaptation, and historical expert credit becomes stale as experts keep evolving.
haTAwPC9IP.method: PAVE corrects expert routing from partial feedback and trains a neural router with local responsibility supervision. Once all targets mature, it assigns sample-level responsibility from prediction-time expert outputs, validates that ownership against current expert capabilities, and then preserves, rebases, or recovers a capability using responsibility-weighted subspace protection and targeted replay.
haTAwPC9IP.key_idea: Separate timely partial-feedback routing from matured credit assignment, and validate historical expert responsibility against current capability before preserving, rebasing, or recovering it.
haTAwPC9IP.evidence: Four multivariate forecasting benchmarks against online forecasting baselines, with ablation and diagnostic analyses; reviewers also cite feedback-matched controls and 12 settings.
haTAwPC9IP.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms strong online forecasting baselines on four benchmarks; no numeric gains are stated in the abstract.
haTAwPC9IP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the leakage-free progressive-feedback setting is realistic, the distinction between timely partial feedback and stale matured credit is a sound insight, and the experiments are wide.
haTAwPC9IP.main_concern: The method is a complex, hyperparameter-heavy stack, and its representation-alignment capability check is not shown to beat a simpler prediction-loss check.

uh7b7doBNd.one_liner: Treats attack-token position selection as Bayesian inference over optimizer losses, with closed-form Gaussian posteriors that merge across attacks and models.
uh7b7doBNd.problem: Optimization-based jailbreak attacks search over a fixed set of token positions, and methods beyond suffixes choose positions with architecture-dependent heuristics.
uh7b7doBNd.method: SPACE treats intermediate optimizer evaluations that existing attacks discard as observations about which positions are worth attacking, with existing heuristics encoded as priors. Posteriors are Gaussian, so beliefs from separate attacks merge in closed form and compute spent attacking one model becomes a positional prior for another.
uh7b7doBNd.key_idea: Treat discarded optimizer losses as noisy observations of per-position vulnerability and update a Gaussian posterior that allocates insertion positions and transfers across models.
uh7b7doBNd.evidence: Twelve LLMs from 0.6B to 32B parameters with GCG and BEAST optimizers, compared with suffix-based GCG and attention-guided SlotGCG (abstract truncated); reviews mention white-box, black-box, and transferred-prior experiments.
uh7b7doBNd.claimed_gains: Improves mean ASR by 11.1 percentage points over suffix-based GCG and 3.6 points over attention-guided SlotGCG across 12 LLMs.
uh7b7doBNd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning positions from optimization feedback is a coherent alternative to fixed heuristics and that the evaluation covers many models and optimizers.
uh7b7doBNd.main_concern: The gain is not isolated from extra compute and broader positional search (about 33% longer runtime, missing random and fixed-split controls), and the benefit of transferred priors is modest.

7KnDxmvLka.one_liner: LoRA variant that uses its bottleneck representation as a query to attend over differences between current and preceding layer states.
7KnDxmvLka.problem: LoRA performs local low-rank updates using only the current-layer input, without exploiting task-relevant representations in preceding layers, which the authors' analysis shows can influence final predictions.
7KnDxmvLka.method: HiLA constructs differences between the current and preceding layer states and uses the current LoRA bottleneck representation as a query to retrieve relevant historical information through attention, then integrates the retrieved signal into the low-rank update.
7KnDxmvLka.key_idea: Attend, with the LoRA bottleneck as query, over cross-layer state differences to inject preceding-layer information into the low-rank update.
7KnDxmvLka.evidence: Mathematical reasoning, code generation, commonsense reasoning, and open-domain dialogue generation on four backbones, with CKA, activation patching, and linear probing analyses according to reviews.
7KnDxmvLka.claimed_gains: Highest average commonsense reasoning accuracy on all four backbones and best results on five of six dialogue generation metrics among compared methods, and on mathematical reasoning it outperforms all low-rank baselines and surpasses full fine-tuning (abstract truncated).
7KnDxmvLka.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea of retrieving cross-layer information with the current LoRA bottleneck as query is clear and interesting, with extensive experiments across backbones and tasks and supporting mechanistic analyses.
7KnDxmvLka.main_concern: Novelty and overhead are questioned: ResLoRA and MRLA already use related cross-layer connections and queries, gains may come from extra parameters, and inference latency overhead is non-negligible.

ZEQE8bJkZz.one_liner: Shows Muon's reported collapse in RLVR is a step-size effect, so orthogonalization gives a learning-rate rescaling, not robustness.
ZEQE8bJkZz.problem: Muon was reported to suffer reward collapse in RL with verifiable rewards and the spectral filter Pion to fix it, but step size was not separated from update direction.
ZEQE8bJkZz.method: Re-runs the public code in a GRPO setup (Qwen3-0.6B, one seed at 1.7B), compares Muon, Pion and tuned AdamW, and matches optimizers by RMS, input-aligned displacement and one-step policy KL. Proposition 1 shows Pion's filter shrinks its step toward zero.
ZEQE8bJkZz.key_idea: Matching optimizers in per-step policy change (equal one-step KL) rather than parameter RMS shows Muon's direction gives no stability margin beyond a learning-rate rescaling.
ZEQE8bJkZz.evidence: GRPO experiments on Qwen3-0.6B and 1.7B, one-step KL matching over 32 seeds and pre-registered falsification checks per reviews, with failed predictions reported.
ZEQE8bJkZz.claimed_gains: The public code runs Muon at a step 13.5 times AdamW's; Muon tolerates a 1.4-3x larger learning rate, and at equal one-step KL it collapses as AdamW would at a learning rate about 3% higher (-2 to +9%), not 100-200%.
ZEQE8bJkZz.reviewer_consensus: Most reviewers agree the practical question is important and that the matched-magnitude and matched-policy-change controls and the reporting of failed predictions are careful and clarify the limits.
ZEQE8bJkZz.main_concern: Scope and clarity: evidence comes from short runs on small models with unresolved headroom at Qwen3-4B, the input-aligned metric fails across scales and horizons, and one reviewer finds the paper hard to follow with a small contribution.

zLLg0kEfpm.one_liner: Trains causal normalizing flows on incomplete data by maximizing each sample's observed-data marginal likelihood, integrating out only ancestral missing variables.
zLLg0kEfpm.problem: Causal normalizing flows assume fully observed training data, so missing values force row deletion or a separate imputation step.
zLLg0kEfpm.method: MissCNF maximizes the marginal likelihood of each partially observed sample; because the autoregressive factorization encodes the causal structure, only missing variables in the ancestral closure of the observed set are integrated out and the others are dropped. The authors also state conditions for recovering the true joint distribution and introduce causal-family positivity.
zLLg0kEfpm.key_idea: Use the causal DAG's autoregressive factorization to integrate out only missing variables in the ancestral closure of the observed set, training the flow directly on the observed-data likelihood.
zLLg0kEfpm.evidence: Eight standard synthetic causal benchmarks, three missingness mechanisms, and missing rates up to 90%, compared against listwise deletion and impute-then-fit pipelines, plus identification theory based on causal-family positivity.
zLLg0kEfpm.claimed_gains: Lowest KL divergence in 23 of 24 nonlinear MCAR and MAR settings and all nonlinear MNAR settings, lowest counterfactual error in 20 of 24 settings, and top-two rank in 22 of 24 linear-SCM settings.
zLLg0kEfpm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers who list strengths agree the problem is important, the observed-data objective avoids a separate imputation stage, and causal-family positivity clarifies when incomplete data suffice.
zLLg0kEfpm.main_concern: The method requires a known DAG, its theory looks incremental to one reviewer, and the evaluation is limited (few small graphs, a single MICE completion, no recovery accuracy on larger graphs).

JClWDANXnQ.one_liner: Temperature-conditioned intermediate states and transport dynamics align tempering with posterior-induced flow language models.
JClWDANXnQ.problem: Post-hoc temperature scaling changes posterior distributions without matching the denoiser's training states or the flow's transport dynamics.
JClWDANXnQ.method: BCT trains denoisers on tempered intermediate states and applies corresponding tempered endpoint dynamics. The paper also derives training-free variants for conventionally trained checkpoints.
JClWDANXnQ.key_idea: Make temperature explicit in intermediate-state distributions, endpoint distributions, and the conditional dynamics that transport between them.
JClWDANXnQ.evidence: Experiments test hyperspherical flow LMs with two denoiser architectures and a von Mises–Fisher flow LM on GSM8K and Sudoku.
JClWDANXnQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the systematic treatment of posterior tempering and its empirical behavior across temperatures.
JClWDANXnQ.main_concern: Multiple reviewers find the empirical scope too limited to establish broader relevance beyond the tested flow models and constrained tasks.

oPMpYNQ0TJ.one_liner: Target-conditioned queries retrieve covariate information to produce calibrated residual corrections for frozen time-series foundation models.
oPMpYNQ0TJ.problem: Multivariate foundation models do not directly prioritize the subset of covariates relevant to a downstream forecasting target.
oPMpYNQ0TJ.method: ReQuA aggregates auxiliary histories with queries conditioned on target history and forecast horizon. Frozen forecast states attend to this representation for residual corrections scaled by a coefficient calibrated on held-out data.
oPMpYNQ0TJ.key_idea: Use target- and horizon-conditioned queries to aggregate auxiliary histories, then calibrate the resulting residual forecast correction with one scalar.
oPMpYNQ0TJ.evidence: Experiments on eight time-series datasets report improvements across frozen TSFM backbones and examine calibration of harmful corrections.
oPMpYNQ0TJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the lightweight frozen-backbone adapter and its query-based correction design.
oPMpYNQ0TJ.main_concern: Multiple reviewers identify missing empirical comparisons with closely related covariate-adaptation methods.

m1sqB09fSB.one_liner: Position rebinding and intent-weighted value updates reuse visual KV caches across overlapping reasoning crops.
m1sqB09fSB.problem: Repeated crop inspection redundantly encodes images, but direct cache reuse leaves stale positions and misses current reasoning intent.
m1sqB09fSB.method: The framework chooses full re-encoding or regional cache reuse according to crop size and availability. Reused keys receive positional correction, while pre-crop reasoning attention strengthens relevant cached values.
m1sqB09fSB.key_idea: Rebind cached keys to new positions and use pre-crop reasoning attention to amplify relevant values when reusing regional visual tokens.
m1sqB09fSB.evidence: Reviews describe Mini-o3 experiments across five visual reasoning benchmarks and comparisons with full re-encoding and removal of intermediate images.
m1sqB09fSB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value training-free reuse of overlapping visual observations and measured efficiency with preserved reasoning accuracy.
m1sqB09fSB.main_concern: Reviewers find insufficient matched comparisons and controls to distinguish the contributions from prior multimodal cache-reuse methods.

hntCCk1eKG.one_liner: Hidden-state alignment transfers privileged teacher supervision during on-policy self-distillation, using a Fisher metric through the language-model head.
hntCCk1eKG.problem: Token-distribution distillation transfers reasoning supervision only after projection through the language-model head and incurs vocabulary-dependent costs.
hntCCk1eKG.method: A-OPSD matches student and privileged-teacher activations on student rollouts. It studies plain hidden-state matching and objectives based on the Gauss–Newton pullback of the OPSD KL loss.
hntCCk1eKG.key_idea: Pull the token-level KL geometry back through the language-model head to weight teacher–student hidden-state discrepancies.
hntCCk1eKG.evidence: Experiments cover Qwen3 and OLMo-3-7B configurations spanning 1.7B to 8B on MATH-500, AIME24, and HMMT25.
hntCCk1eKG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find activation-space self-distillation well motivated and acknowledge substantial experiments on objective choices and memory.
hntCCk1eKG.main_concern: Multiple reviewers question whether memory savings arise from top-k approximation rather than activation-space distillation and whether they persist at larger k.

TXh7u2qp0z.one_liner: Forward-query Pauli coefficient and relative-phase estimation learns approximately sparse quantum unitaries with diamond-distance guarantees.
TXh7u2qp0z.problem: Learning quantum unitaries in diamond distance remains difficult when Pauli sparsity is approximate and controlled queries are unavailable.
TXh7u2qp0z.method: The algorithm estimates sufficiently large Pauli coefficients up to a shared global phase using non-controlled forward queries. The paper also studies bounded Pauli norm classes and a restricted-input diamond metric.
TXh7u2qp0z.key_idea: Recover large Pauli coefficients and their relative phases using forward queries, then construct an approximation from the estimated sparse spectrum.
TXh7u2qp0z.evidence: Theoretical results provide query-complexity bounds, a relative-phase recovery lemma, and an exponential lower bound for bounded Pauli-norm unitaries.
TXh7u2qp0z.claimed_gains: The abstract gives $\tilde{O}(s^3/\varepsilon^2)$ forward queries, an $\Omega(2^{n/2})$ lower bound for bounded Pauli norm, and $\tilde{O}(L_1^4/\varepsilon^{8})$ queries under restricted diamond distance.
TXh7u2qp0z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate approximate-sparsity learning and recovery of relative phases without controlled unitary access.
TXh7u2qp0z.main_concern: Multiple reviewers note that the extra s factor relative to exact-sparsity learning lacks a matching lower bound.

NLMCTdbzUD.one_liner: A supremum distribution discrepancy trains representations to control worst-case prediction disparity over continuous sensitive attributes.
NLMCTdbzUD.problem: Average fairness measures can conceal discrimination concentrated in low-probability ranges of continuous sensitive attributes.
NLMCTdbzUD.method: supIPM measures the worst conditional-versus-marginal representation discrepancy over sensitive values. supFR trains against this metric, with uniform-convergence analysis linking it to downstream disparity for bounded Hölder prediction heads.
NLMCTdbzUD.key_idea: Replace the average conditional distribution discrepancy with its supremum over sensitive values and optimize representations against that worst-case measure.
NLMCTdbzUD.evidence: Uniform-convergence and downstream-disparity bounds accompany tabular and graph benchmark experiments.
NLMCTdbzUD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize that worst-case fairness addresses violations hidden by averaging and acknowledge promising empirical results.
NLMCTdbzUD.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical relevance of theoretical guarantees requiring strong density and smoothness assumptions, particularly in rare sensitive-attribute regions.

5r4zNWC4od.one_liner: Transition-cost decomposition separates required marginal transport from excess coupling activity in discrete generative sampling.
5r4zNWC4od.problem: Token-revising discrete samplers lack a clear account of unnecessary transitions introduced by choices of finite-step coupling.
5r4zNWC4od.method: Activity Geometry decomposes expected transition cost into a marginal-transport minimum and coupling excess. MAFTC realizes prescribed marginals with minimum activity without retraining or extra model evaluations.
5r4zNWC4od.key_idea: Minimize finite-step coupling cost while preserving prescribed marginals, separating necessary transport from excess token-changing activity.
5r4zNWC4od.evidence: The paper provides finite-step and continuous-time theory, geometric analysis of metric-induced Gibbs paths, and image and text sampling evaluations.
5r4zNWC4od.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the activity decomposition and theoretical analysis of consecutive-step couplings.
5r4zNWC4od.main_concern: Multiple reviewers find the practical case insufficiently established through unclear algorithmic requirements or limited generation evaluations.

5xrP2XqcYt.one_liner: Hierarchical knowledge-graph coverage directs synthetic training-data supplementation and concept-aware sampling for text-to-image generation.
5xrP2XqcYt.problem: Source-organized image-text datasets hide concept coverage gaps that impair generation of rare world-knowledge concepts.
5xrP2XqcYt.method: CGTR maps annotations to a hierarchical knowledge graph, identifies underrepresented concepts, and synthesizes filtered image-text supplements using scene templates and reference images. Concept-aware sampling regulates exposure during fine-tuning.
5xrP2XqcYt.key_idea: Use hierarchical concept coverage to choose supplementation targets and sampling weights, with reference-guided synthesis supplying missing training examples.
5xrP2XqcYt.evidence: The paper audits 370M annotation records, builds KnowGapBench with 3,286 concepts, and fine-tunes UniWorld-V1 on refined Fine-T2I data.
5xrP2XqcYt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value identifying actionable concept gaps and separately evaluating concept identity and compositional compliance.
5xrP2XqcYt.main_concern: Multiple reviewers find the training evidence insufficient to isolate which data-refinement components cause the reported improvements.

mI33kMZRSK.one_liner: Decomposing integrands into a zero-integral neural-field divergence plus a direct predictor learns parametric integrals from integrands.
mI33kMZRSK.problem: Learning neural surrogates for parametric families of integrals conventionally requires expensive numerical integration over many pointwise samples to generate integral supervision.
mI33kMZRSK.method: The method decomposes a parametric integrand into a zero-integral term parameterized as the divergence of a neural field—mapped across parameterized integration domains via change of variables—and a second network component that directly outputs the parametric integral in one differentiable forward pass, trained solely on pointwise integrand evaluations.
mI33kMZRSK.key_idea: Decompose the integrand into a neural-field divergence that integrates to zero under domain change-of-variables plus a direct single-pass integral predictor.
mI33kMZRSK.evidence: Experiments on filtering, rendering, and integral transforms compare approximation error under matched training budgets against Monte Carlo, quasi-Monte Carlo, quadrature, and antiderivative baselines.
mI33kMZRSK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the divergence-based integrand decomposition is clearly explained and produces an efficient, differentiable single-pass integral predictor without precomputed integral targets.
mI33kMZRSK.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical and conceptual advance over prior zero-integral decompositions, neural control variates, and single-sample Monte Carlo regression, while requesting formal function-space and diffeomorphism conditions.

oCU9ruJAG4.one_liner: Primal-dual splitting with annealed score-based denoisers converges to stationary points of nonconvex nonsmooth MAP objectives.
oCU9ruJAG4.problem: Integrating annealed score-based generative denoisers into splitting-based Plug-and-Play inverse solvers complicates theoretical convergence to Maximum a Posteriori objectives and suffers from iterate geometry mismatch.
oCU9ruJAG4.method: The authors formulate MAP estimation with annealed score-based priors via primal-dual splitting (PnP-PDHG), proving convergence of iterates to the stationary set of nonconvex and nonsmooth MAP objectives while quantifying splitting-induced geometry mismatch and deriving closed-form updates for structured nonlinear forward models.
oCU9ruJAG4.key_idea: Formulate Plug-and-Play inverse recovery via primal-dual splitting with annealed score-based denoisers to attain stationary points of nonconvex, nonsmooth MAP objectives.
oCU9ruJAG4.evidence: Convergence proofs and geometry-mismatch bounds are accompanied by experiments on structured nonlinear inverse problems including phase retrieval and sparse-view transmission computed tomography.
oCU9ruJAG4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the convergence theory for annealed primal-dual Plug-and-Play iterations under nonconvex and nonsmooth data-fidelity terms is technically sound.
oCU9ruJAG4.main_concern: Reviewers note extensive prior literature on nonconvex PnP convergence, unclear exposition of the MAP-versus-MMSE proximal denoiser gap, and weak positioning against related work.

wXnuLklgoX.one_liner: Compiling natural-language agent skills into executable tools prevents small LLM executors from derailing on intermediate outputs.
wXnuLklgoX.problem: Natural-language agent skills fail on small open LLM executors both via skill-loading channels and in-context placement because small models derail on messy intermediate outputs they generate mid-procedure.
wXnuLklgoX.method: From each public skill package and a single development instance per task family, an offline producer compiles procedural steps into executable tools that return clean intermediate outputs while leaving tool selection and task completion to the small executor.
wXnuLklgoX.key_idea: Compile natural-language skill packages once per task family into executable tools that return clean intermediate results for small LLM executors.
wXnuLklgoX.evidence: Controlled trajectory, prefix-intervention, pre-registered handoff, and compiled-tool experiments evaluate 4B and 27B executors across two model families on SkillLearnBench.
wXnuLklgoX.claimed_gains: On SkillLearnBench, compiled tools raise a 4B executor from 9 to 53 of 80 held-out instances, outperforming a 27B executor given the skill in context.
wXnuLklgoX.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers praise the empirical diagnosis and controlled handoff and prefix interventions quantifying how small executors fail to invoke skills and derail on noisy intermediates, while one reviewer lists no strengths.
wXnuLklgoX.main_concern: Reviewers argue the comparison is confounded by a strong Claude Opus 5 agent authoring privileged task-specific executable solvers from development instances and failure notes, alongside action-space scalability and unclear terminology.

vjJmN72Swb.one_liner: A learned compiler predicts behavioral outcomes of candidate adaptation programs and selects updates according to downstream priorities.
vjJmN72Swb.problem: Fixed adaptation recipes ignore episode-specific trade-offs, while exhaustive program search must be repeated for each learning episode.
vjJmN72Swb.method: The compiler learns from prior adaptations to predict acquisition, transfer, boundedness, and preservation for candidate programs before adaptation. A utility function selects among those programs under changing priorities without retraining the predictor.
vjJmN72Swb.key_idea: Predict vector-valued adaptation outcomes from pre-adaptation features, then select a program using the desired behavioral utility.
vjJmN72Swb.evidence: Experiments evaluate four LoRA configurations across five learning types on Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-9B, including unseen-family and alternative-utility tests.
vjJmN72Swb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value predicting multiple behavioral outcomes that can be reused under different adaptation priorities.
vjJmN72Swb.main_concern: Reviewers find the small fixed configuration space and weak cross-model or unseen-family results limit practical generality.

dtV3GUe9Ru.one_liner: Optimal intervention decisions under decaying future agency define reward-scale-invariant state criticality relative to a fallback policy.
dtV3GUe9Ru.problem: Identifying consequential states requires accounting for limited intervention opportunities and the fallback policy's behavior.
dtV3GUe9Ru.method: CODA allows an agent to override a fallback policy while each override can reduce future intervention effectiveness. It decomposes the decision problem into coupled optimal stopping problems for tabular and continuous algorithms.
dtV3GUe9Ru.key_idea: Define critical states by optimal overrides when intervention use reduces the probability that future overrides take effect.
dtV3GUe9Ru.evidence: Theory proves existence under suboptimal fallback policies and reward-scale invariance; experiments cover grid worlds and continuous control against State Importance and Lazy-MDPs.
dtV3GUe9Ru.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the principled intervention formulation and its independence from reward-scale tuning.
dtV3GUe9Ru.main_concern: Reviewers find continuous-control and complex-task evaluations too limited to establish practical advantages.

Dny8g9np4M.one_liner: Peak-graph knowledge energy guides diffusion sampling and policy learning toward structurally related spectral band groups.
Dny8g9np4M.problem: Global spectral representations can obscure informative peak-group relationships and encourage reliance on isolated peaks or background patterns.
Dny8g9np4M.method: KERD constructs a Peak Graph, learns consistency-based relation energy, and uses it to guide diffusion sampling. Class-conditional spectral prototypes stabilize policy learning, with optional shared relation graphs for paired cohort variables.
Dny8g9np4M.key_idea: Use learned peak-group relation energy to guide diffusion sampling and relation-derived prototypes to supervise policy learning.
Dny8g9np4M.evidence: The abstract reports multicenter evaluation on more than 70,000 measurements; reviews describe seven datasets, five training seeds, and Raman-specific baselines.
Dny8g9np4M.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize promising experimental results and the interest of incorporating spectral relations into evidence selection.
Dny8g9np4M.main_concern: Reviewers question whether diffusion and reinforcement learning justify their complexity over simpler alternatives.

SwhanFeUvv.one_liner: Simulator-grounded event graphs and controlled interventions test whether video models generate complete physical causal cascades.
SwhanFeUvv.problem: Visual quality and broad physical plausibility metrics do not establish whether generated events follow causal dependencies through a complete process.
SwhanFeUvv.method: CausalCascade combines Blender scenes, structured event graphs, diagnostic VQA, and controlled counterfactual variants. Motion, event, and intervention diagnostics evaluate generated futures under different event-specification levels.
SwhanFeUvv.key_idea: Compare generated physical cascades with simulator event graphs and re-simulated interventions to examine event dependencies and selective responses.
SwhanFeUvv.evidence: The benchmark evaluates nine image-to-video models using 50 Blender scenes, three future-event specification levels, and 2,832 counterfactual variants.
SwhanFeUvv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the inspectable simulator-grounded evaluation of multi-stage physical processes and controlled interventions.
SwhanFeUvv.main_concern: Reviewers find that the diagnostics do not adequately separate basic generation failures from causal-response errors.

G3YUEjH3gd.one_liner: Matched unstated-outcome and explicit-outcome probes test whether language models misinterpret rules as evidence of actual events.
G3YUEjH3gd.problem: Language models may infer that prohibited events did not occur or commanded events occurred without factual evidence.
G3YUEjH3gd.method: Unstated pairs probes with unstated outcomes and explicit-outcome anchors while controlling scenario content. Evaluations examine directional errors, confidence, reweighting, and prompting effects.
G3YUEjH3gd.key_idea: Hold scenarios fixed while varying explicit outcome evidence to measure factual inferences drawn from prohibitions and commands.
G3YUEjH3gd.evidence: Unstated contains 720 instances from 120 scenarios and evaluates 28 open-weight models, ten frontier models, and human performance.
G3YUEjH3gd.claimed_gains: Across 28 open-weight models, median accuracy is 84.5% on explicit-outcome anchors and 6.7% on prohibition probes; most frontier models remain below 75% on prohibition probes.
G3YUEjH3gd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the controlled benchmark and broad evaluation of an apparent factual-inference failure.
G3YUEjH3gd.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the results isolate rule-to-fact projection from likelihood-versus-certainty confusion or other explanations.

ZLsVILQZCN.one_liner: Predicted expert routes, hypergraph placement, and online migration coordinate request locality in distributed mixture-of-experts inference.
ZLsVILQZCN.problem: Distributed MoE inference incurs communication costs determined jointly by expert placement and the device hosting each request.
ZLsVILQZCN.method: MoEAtlas predicts prompt-token expert selections to choose a home GPU, then partitions hyperedges representing co-activated expert sets under load and memory limits. A migration mapping reduces expert-transfer volume while inference continues as workloads change.
ZLsVILQZCN.key_idea: Model each token's complete expert set as a hyperedge and jointly use expert layouts and predicted routes to localize requests.
ZLsVILQZCN.evidence: Experiments on OLMoE, Qwen1.5-MoE, and DeepSeek-V2-Lite assess prefill time, routing prediction, home selection, placement, and workload-dependent migration.
ZLsVILQZCN.claimed_gains: MoEAtlas reduces complete prefill time by 19.33%, 17.00%, and 24.69% on OLMoE, Qwen1.5-MoE, and DeepSeek-V2-Lite, respectively, while Matching reduces OLMoE weight-transfer time by 12.46% relative to Greedy.
ZLsVILQZCN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that complete expert-set hypergraphs match node-level communication semantics better than pairwise statistics alone.
ZLsVILQZCN.main_concern: Restricted baselines and unmatched placement controls do not establish the advantage over complete related serving systems under comparable resources.

MuusqOAmAG.one_liner: Noise-aware input scaling, weight clamping, and error redistribution adapt pretrained LLMs to stochastic analog-memory weight perturbations.
MuusqOAmAG.problem: Digital post-training quantization does not address stochastic analog weight noise, while hardware-aware retraining grows costly for large models.
MuusqOAmAG.method: WARP minimizes expected layer-output distortion decomposed into weight-error and noise-variance terms using per-channel input scaling and exactly solved groupwise clipping thresholds. WARP+ adds GPTQ-style error redistribution using only calibration data.
MuusqOAmAG.key_idea: Choose weight ranges by balancing deterministic clipping distortion against stochastic programming-noise variance.
MuusqOAmAG.evidence: An AIMC simulator with hardware-derived programming noise evaluates Qwen3 models from 0.6B to 32B across benchmarks, noise instances, and component ablations.
MuusqOAmAG.claimed_gains: WARP+ completes the 32B model in <3 hours on 4 A100 GPUs and recovers 40% of Qwen3-14B accuracy loss, more than 2× PTQ recovery, reaching within 3.5% points of noise-free accuracy.
MuusqOAmAG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the noise-aware distortion objective and the practical layerwise alternative to hardware-aware retraining.
MuusqOAmAG.main_concern: Evaluation limited to Qwen3 and PCM noise leaves generalization across model architectures and memory technologies insufficiently established.

CwOZPXu8l4.one_liner: Routed on-policy distillation merges domain-specialist reward models using dense token guidance and domain contribution reweighting.
CwOZPXu8l4.problem: Mixed-domain reward-model reinforcement learning suffers from sparse outcome rewards and interference between heterogeneous capabilities.
CwOZPXu8l4.method: RM-OPD trains specialist teachers with single-domain GRPO, then routes student-generated critiques to those teachers for signed token-level supervision. Domain contribution reweighting balances guidance, and optional criteria context distillation supplies teachers with domain-specific evaluation criteria.
CwOZPXu8l4.key_idea: Distill domain-routed teacher token probabilities on student critiques while reweighting token contributions toward target domain shares.
CwOZPXu8l4.evidence: Reward-model benchmarks compare two 7B initializations with matched Mix-RL baselines and analyze domain-level performance.
CwOZPXu8l4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize consistent gains over backbone-matched Mix-RL and the practical value of consolidating specialist judgments into one model.
CwOZPXu8l4.main_concern: Missing basic multi-teacher distillation controls leave the added contribution of the proposed reward-model adaptations unclear.

cPr98BKtKq.one_liner: Event dependencies and failure-propagation graphs trace distant agent errors to their decisive step, responsible agent, and error category.
cPr98BKtKq.problem: Visible failure symptoms can occur many steps after the decisive error, making agent failure attribution difficult from step content alone.
cPr98BKtKq.method: DeFA constructs an event dependency graph from protocol and semantic relations, identifies possible requirement violations, and traces their causes and effects into a failure-propagation graph. Segmented local analysis uses summaries of other segments to retain global trajectory context.
cPr98BKtKq.key_idea: Trace suspected violations through event dependencies and combine propagation roles with step evidence to localize the decisive error.
cPr98BKtKq.evidence: Who&When and the Who&When Pro text subset support matched-backbone attribution comparisons and graph ablations, with additional image and video trajectory evaluations.
cPr98BKtKq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize consistent exact-step attribution gains across backbones and supporting component ablations.
cPr98BKtKq.main_concern: Missing variance estimates, confidence intervals, or paired tests leave the reliability of gains in a multi-stage prompting pipeline uncertain.

jpRV8KXEBy.one_liner: Trains layer-wise hash retrieval networks end-to-end via closed-loop language modeling gradient feedback and pairs them with an LRU working KV cache.
jpRV8KXEBy.problem: Learning discrete token selection for sparse long-context attention directly from the language modeling objective is difficult and typically restricted to layer-wise imitation of dense attention.
jpRV8KXEBy.method: RouteCache initializes hash-based retrieval from an oracle and applies closed-loop gradient feedback during training, where gated hash scores modulate attention and receive gradients from the final language modeling loss while the LLM backbone remains frozen. At inference, the gates are removed for sparse hash retrieval and paired with an LRU working cache, fused kernels, and asynchronous CUDA execution.
jpRV8KXEBy.key_idea: Use gated hash scores during dense training so language modeling loss gradients jointly optimize discrete hash retrieval across layers, then deploy with an LRU working cache.
jpRV8KXEBy.evidence: Evaluated across Qwen3 models from 4B to 30B parameters (including MoE and reasoning variants) on perplexity, LongBench V2, RULER, and 256K-context latency benchmarks.
jpRV8KXEBy.claimed_gains: Achieves up to 4.9-7x latency speedups over StaticCache at 256K context while maintaining quality close to dense attention.
jpRV8KXEBy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear writing, thorough operator-level efficiency analysis, and the closed-loop gradient feedback mechanism for training hash-based sparse attention.
jpRV8KXEBy.main_concern: Reviewers note that combining learned hash indexing (similar to Spotlight) with an LRU cache feels incremental, evaluation is limited to the Qwen3 family, and full-model end-to-end latency comparisons across batch sizes are incomplete.

KhK1dt2Gzc.one_liner: Propagates a dense quantile grid deterministically under a diagonal Monge-Ampere approximation of the probability flow for time-series forecasting.
KhK1dt2Gzc.problem: Deterministic linear-time diffusion forecasters do not directly output predictive distributions, while Monte Carlo sampling adds computational cost and sampling error.
KhK1dt2Gzc.method: QFLOW relates probability density to local stretching of a vector quantile map via the Monge-Ampere equation and applies a diagonal Jacobian approximation to derive a one-step recursion that transports a quantile curve along the probability-flow field. At inference, it advances a dense quantile grid, centers it on a separately estimated conditional mean head, and computes probabilistic metrics directly from the transported quantiles.
KhK1dt2Gzc.key_idea: Apply a diagonal Monge-Ampere approximation to transport an ordered quantile grid deterministically along the probability-flow ODE without Monte Carlo sampling.
KhK1dt2Gzc.evidence: Evaluated on synthetic probability flows with known marginals (against 10^4-sample Monte Carlo) and across nine long-horizon time-series forecasting datasets (including ETTm1, ETTm2, ILI, Solar, and Traffic).
KhK1dt2Gzc.claimed_gains: Recovers bimodal, skewed, and heavy-tailed marginals more accurately than 10^4-sample Monte Carlo on synthetic flows and ranks among the top three recent diffusion forecasters across nine long-horizon datasets.
KhK1dt2Gzc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers admire the concise mathematical derivation of the diagonal Monge-Ampere quantile recursion that guarantees ordered quantiles in O(H) deterministic inference.
KhK1dt2Gzc.main_concern: Reviewers highlight that in the paper's own ablations, direct linear quantile regression beats QFLOW on all nine datasets and fixed validation residuals beat the quantile transport on five of nine datasets, showing gains come primarily from the separate linear location head.

ZzJWMU6dUI.one_liner: Estimates diffusion training-data influence via Kronecker-preconditioned local score discrepancy and distills the rankings into cached internal activation embeddings.
ZzJWMU6dUI.problem: Diffusion training data attribution methods rely on proxy losses rather than generative score changes and require expensive per-sample gradients or query-specific optimization.
ZzJWMU6dUI.method: Formulates Training-data Influence via score Discrepancy (TID) as a preconditioned gradient similarity using Kronecker-factored curvature to estimate local generative score changes without retraining or random projections. Then distills TID online into TIDE, a forward-only student that predicts influence rankings from cached internal diffusion model activations.
ZzJWMU6dUI.key_idea: Estimate leave-one-out diffusion score discrepancy via Kronecker-factored preconditioned gradients and distill the resulting teacher rankings into a forward-only activation embedding student.
ZzJWMU6dUI.evidence: Counterfactual retraining evaluation on CIFAR-10, ArtBench-10, and MS-COCO across DDPM, EDM, and flow-matching variants.
ZzJWMU6dUI.claimed_gains: TIDE retains most of TID's attribution accuracy at four to five orders of magnitude lower per-query cost, attributing generated samples in milliseconds.
ZzJWMU6dUI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value distilling gradient-based influence rankings into cached diffusion activations for fast forward-only query attribution and appreciate the counterfactual retraining experiments.
ZzJWMU6dUI.main_concern: Reviewers point out that TID still relies on multiple unvalidated linearization and curvature approximations of true leave-one-out score discrepancy, and the counterfactual deletion test removes the union of selected images across queries rather than testing query-specific attribution accuracy.

un6ZVyHnXF.one_liner: Synthesizes rule-guided executable adversarial computer-use tasks and validated safe trajectories across desktop applications for safety fine-tuning.
un6ZVyHnXF.problem: Chat-style text safety alignment fails to transfer reliably to computer-use agents, which often execute harmful intents when instantiated as concrete GUI tasks.
un6ZVyHnXF.method: SAFEST uses a hierarchical rule-guided pipeline to ground 43 abstract risk categories into 2,724 concrete executable adversarial tasks (1,299 direct and 1,425 indirect) across 8 desktop applications, paired with validated safe-execution trajectories for supervised safety fine-tuning.
un6ZVyHnXF.key_idea: Hierarchically ground abstract safety risks into executable desktop-application tasks (both direct and indirect) and collect verified safe GUI trajectories for agent fine-tuning.
un6ZVyHnXF.evidence: Fine-tunes two open-source computer-use agent backbones (Qwen3-VL-8B and EvoCUA-8B) on the 2,724-task SAFEST dataset and evaluates across four CUA safety benchmarks.
un6ZVyHnXF.claimed_gains: Increases the average safe rate across four CUA benchmarks from roughly 41% to 87.8-90.1% on Qwen3-VL-8B and EvoCUA-8B.
un6ZVyHnXF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that executable safety training data covering direct and indirect environmental risks across desktop applications is a valuable resource that yields large safety gains across benchmarks.
un6ZVyHnXF.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about selection bias from reusing the 36-task OSWorld-Small split for both checkpoint/hyperparameter selection and final utility evaluation, as well as insufficient ablations isolating executable trajectories from text-only safety data.

0QXPPsbddF.one_liner: Combines instruction-citation checks with a counterfactual log-probability drop test that provably bounds missed malicious tool calls under indirect prompt injection.
0QXPPsbddF.problem: Language-model agents acting on untrusted external content are vulnerable to indirect prompt injections that redirect tool calls toward attacker goals.
0QXPPsbddF.method: ATTRACK pairs early instruction-citation checks that flag untrusted instruction sources with an action-influence test that deletes untrusted content and re-scores the proposed tool call's log-probability under the agent's weights, blocking calls whose log-probability drops beyond a threshold and providing a formal upper bound on missed malicious actions.
0QXPPsbddF.key_idea: Re-score each proposed tool call after deleting untrusted context and block calls whose log-probability drop exceeds a threshold, bounding undetected attack probability.
0QXPPsbddF.evidence: Theoretical probability-ratio bound and empirical evaluation across AgentDojo's four suites and three open-weight models (Mistral, Qwen, Gemma) under standard and adaptive attacks against CausalArmor, AttriGuard, CaMeL, and taint isolation.
0QXPPsbddF.claimed_gains: Achieves 0% standard attack success on AgentDojo, 2/104 adaptive attack successes on Mistral (vs. 23 for CausalArmor and 19 for AttriGuard) and 0 on Qwen/Gemma, while retaining 75-89% benign task utility (vs. 43-52% for CaMeL and taint isolation).
0QXPPsbddF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate decoupling the formal probability-ratio guarantee from the auxiliary citation detector so the bound holds even when citation checks are fooled.
0QXPPsbddF.main_concern: Reviewers note that the formal bound assumes temperature-1 sampling over a single exact serialized string whereas evaluation uses greedy decoding, and at the deployed threshold (tau=100 nats) the bound becomes vacuous on 20-51% of attacks, leaving protection dependent on the uncertified citation check.

0hjJwDnuyI.one_liner: Transfers item and user knowledge across autonomous recommender systems without shared IDs by grounding shared semantic concepts in local interaction behavior.
0hjJwDnuyI.problem: Autonomous recommender systems operate in incompatible item and representation spaces without shared user or item IDs, while generic LLM semantics miss locally learned behavioral meaning.
0hjJwDnuyI.method: Federated Semantic Grounding (FedSG) anchors cross-system knowledge exchange at two levels: at the item level, it uses shared semantic descriptors to complement low-support item representations across platforms; at the user level, it re-expresses local preferences in another system's item context using behaviorally grounded semantic mappings.
0hjJwDnuyI.key_idea: Use shared semantic concepts as anchors to exchange behavior-grounded item embeddings and cross-context user preference mappings across unaligned recommender systems.
0hjJwDnuyI.evidence: Evaluated across multiple cross-platform collaboration scenarios and recommender backbones (including C2DSR) with differing architectures against independent and federated baselines.
0hjJwDnuyI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that enabling federated knowledge transfer across autonomous recommenders without shared user or item IDs via behavior-grounded semantic anchors is practical and well-supported by controlled ablations.
0hjJwDnuyI.main_concern: Reviewers note that averaging descriptor embeddings and combining preference mappings across independently trained systems lacks theoretical parameter-space compatibility guarantees, and key semantic preprocessing details (such as the specific LLM used and train/test leakage checks) are omitted.

2nS75GAxmD.one_liner: Learns compact visual-transition tokens from video data and couples a transition dynamics expert with an action expert via a Mixture-of-Transformers.
2nS75GAxmD.problem: Vision-language-action models struggle to extract compact latent representations of future observations that retain the scene-change information needed for robot control.
2nS75GAxmD.method: MoAct learns compact visual-transition tokens conditioned on preceding observation features from large-scale robot and egocentric human videos, using spatial gating and feature modulation. It connects the visual-transition dynamics expert with an action expert through a dual-stream Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture to guide policy learning.
2nS75GAxmD.key_idea: Encode scene changes relative to preceding visual features into compact transition tokens and couple the transition predictor with an action policy via a dual-stream Mixture-of-Transformers.
2nS75GAxmD.evidence: Evaluated in SimplerEnv simulation across two robot embodiments and on real-world physical manipulation tasks, including few-shot learning and zero-robot-demo scene adaptation using egocentric human videos.
2nS75GAxmD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate conditioning transition tokens on preceding visual features, the inference efficiency of dropping the DINO predictor at test time, and the practical benefit of adapting to new scenes using egocentric human videos.
2nS75GAxmD.main_concern: Reviewers note limited conceptual novelty over recent latent-transition and MoT-based VLA models (such as FLARE, LAPA, World Guidance, and DUST) and point out that ablations remove entire training stages rather than isolating spatial gating, modulation, or the MoT interface.

xUfOKMx2hz.one_liner: Benchmarks interleaved edge-cloud collaboration strategies in long-horizon LLM agent execution across task completion, resource cost, and privacy exposure.
xUfOKMx2hz.problem: In long-horizon agent execution, cloud assistance is interleaved across trajectory steps rather than one-shot per query, creating poorly understood trade-offs among task success, compute cost, and sensitive data exposure.
xUfOKMx2hz.method: Introduces EC^2-Bench, a benchmark of executable digital-workspace agent tasks annotated with sensitive information units and paired with a unified evaluation framework measuring task performance, cloud resource usage, and trajectory-level privacy exposure across edge-cloud collaboration strategies (such as Per-step Routing, Delegation, and Advisory).
xUfOKMx2hz.key_idea: Evaluate interleaved edge-cloud agent collaboration strategies jointly on task completion, resource cost, and unit-level sensitive data leakage across multi-step digital workspace trajectories.
xUfOKMx2hz.evidence: Empirical study across executable digital-workspace tasks in EC^2-Bench comparing edge-only, cloud-only, and multiple edge-cloud collaboration strategies across Qwen edge models of varying sizes and frontier cloud models.
xUfOKMx2hz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly measuring task completion, resource usage, and unit-level privacy exposure in long-horizon edge-cloud agent execution is a timely and well-validated benchmark setup.
xUfOKMx2hz.main_concern: Reviewers point out that collaboration strategies are not compared under matched cloud-call budgets, edge models are restricted to a single model family (Qwen), and aggregated scores lack confidence intervals and end-to-end latency measurements.

GNBNfrOQXy.one_liner: Derives sharp partial-identification bounds showing aggregate audio-visual accuracies fail to identify cross-modal conversion changes and resolves them via paired overlap evaluation.
GNBNfrOQXy.problem: Standard aggregate audio-only, video-only, and joint accuracy reports after Audio-Visual LLM fine-tuning conceal whether gains come from cross-modal fusion or single-modality shortcuts and can reverse the sign of functional change.
GNBNfrOQXy.method: Defines isolated-path coverage (fraction of questions solved by audio-only or video-only) and conversion (joint accuracy minus coverage), then derives sharp partial-identification bounds for conversion change from aggregate before-and-after accuracies and shows how measuring paired prediction overlap resolves the ambiguity.
GNBNfrOQXy.key_idea: Decompose joint audio-visual accuracy into single-modality union coverage plus cross-modal conversion, deriving sharp bounds from marginals and exact identification from paired instance overlap.
GNBNfrOQXy.evidence: Theoretical identification bounds and an empirical audit across 56 checkpoint-dataset evaluations and 40 before-and-after fine-tuning comparisons on Qwen2.5-Omni, Qwen3-Omni, MiniCPM-o, and VITA.
GNBNfrOQXy.claimed_gains: Aggregate reports identify 0 of 40 conversion-change signs across 56 checkpoint-dataset evaluations, while the conventional joint-minus-video gap points in the opposite direction in 17 of 40 comparisons.
GNBNfrOQXy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies a widespread evaluation flaw in multimodal fine-tuning and demonstrates through a 40-comparison audit that a simple paired-overlap statistic resolves sign reversals hidden by marginal accuracies.
GNBNfrOQXy.main_concern: Reviewers note that the theoretical bounds follow directly from classical Fréchet/Boole probability inequalities on error overlap and do not provide an actionable training or inference algorithm to improve cross-modal fusion.

NBRxyZGt6o.one_liner: Compiles LLM agent execution trajectories into a provenance-and-effect safety graph (VEGAS) for runtime verification and witness-guided task recovery (GraphGuard).
NBRxyZGt6o.problem: Safety evidence in LLM agent execution is scattered across long trajectories, making rule-based verification and continuation of benign tasks after an intervention difficult.
NBRxyZGt6o.method: Formalizes agent safety as source and effect conditions over VEGAS (Verifiable Graph for Agent Safety), which structures trajectory provenance, user authorizations, and action effects into a unified graph. Implements GraphGuard for runtime graph compilation, property verification, and witness-guided recovery so agents can continue benign tasks after blocking unsafe actions.
NBRxyZGt6o.key_idea: Compile trajectory provenance, authorizations, and action effects into an evolving graph to verify safety properties at runtime and guide post-block recovery.
NBRxyZGt6o.evidence: Evaluated on AgentDojo and MT-AgentRisk across agent backbones including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, GLM, and Kimi.
NBRxyZGt6o.claimed_gains: Reduces the attack success rate (ASR) of DeepSeek-V4-Pro from 45.3% to 0.0% on AgentDojo while maintaining high benign-task performance.
NBRxyZGt6o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate structuring provenance, authorization, and outcome constraints into an explicit graph that supports witness-guided recovery and achieves strong ASR reductions across benchmarks.
NBRxyZGt6o.main_concern: Reviewers point out that constructing the graph's influence, violation, and authorization edges still relies on prompting a compiler LLM and trusting the agent's self-reported reasoning text, rather than purely deterministic verification.

a65cHiP8y3.one_liner: Transforms recent vision foundation model features into the temporal Fourier domain to predict feature-space deltas for long-horizon visual world modeling.
a65cHiP8y3.problem: Autoregressive visual world models that predict future vision foundation model (VFM) features suffer from accumulating feature errors over long rollouts.
a65cHiP8y3.method: Fourier-World applies a temporal discrete Fourier transform to the four most recent VFM context features and uses a query initialized from the latest feature to read the resulting frequency coefficients, predicting feature-space deltas that are accumulated onto the latest feature for future rollouts.
a65cHiP8y3.key_idea: Apply a temporal Fourier transform over recent VFM feature frames and query the frequency coefficients to predict residual feature deltas for autoregressive rollouts.
a65cHiP8y3.evidence: Pretrained on Kinetics-700 and evaluated on downstream segmentation, depth estimation, action anticipation, and causal future-point forecasting across Cityscapes, VSPW, KITTI, EK100, and TAP-Vid-RGB-Stacking.
a65cHiP8y3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the clean separation between the latest feature state and frequency-domain temporal dynamics, as well as the broad downstream evaluation across five benchmarks.
a65cHiP8y3.main_concern: Reviewers note that because a four-frame DFT is an invertible linear basis change, the paper lacks retrained end-to-end ablations (comparing against raw frames, DCT, or Haar under identical architecture and training) to prove the gains come specifically from the Fourier basis.

UxQxf53ZOn.one_liner: Optimizes temporally coordinated video style transformations with source-based content restoration to evade input safety guards while preserving harmful events.
UxQxf53ZOn.problem: Attacking a guarded VideoLLM pipeline requires bypassing an upstream input content guard without erasing the underlying harmful event that triggers downstream harmful generation.
UxQxf53ZOn.method: Constrained Temporal Adversarial Style Optimization (CTASO) searches a continuous space of temporally coordinated video style edits combined with source-based content restoration, using feasibility-first optimization guided solely by input-guard feedback without querying the downstream VideoLLM.
UxQxf53ZOn.key_idea: Combine temporally coordinated video style transfer with source-based salient content restoration under feasibility-first black-box optimization against the input safety guard.
UxQxf53ZOn.evidence: Evaluated across three input content guards (including LlavaGuard) and four downstream VideoLLMs against five baselines and five adapted prior attacks, with human auditing for harmful event preservation.
UxQxf53ZOn.claimed_gains: Achieves a human-audited Guard Evasion Rate of 0.61 versus 0.22 for budget-matched random style search on LlavaGuard.
UxQxf53ZOn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing input-guard evasion from downstream VideoLLM jailbreaking while verifying harmful-event preservation via human audit addresses a realistic multimodal security threat.
UxQxf53ZOn.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the evaluated guards rely on frame-level or general VLM prompts rather than dedicated temporal video guardrails, optimization requires continuous guard confidence scores, and the heavy wall-clock computational cost of diffusion-based video editing per query is not reported.

hctrVEKkGJ.one_liner: Evaluates how faithfully autonomous AI research agents reconstruct human research decisions and artifacts across scientific workflow stages on ICLR oral papers.
hctrVEKkGJ.problem: End-to-end task completion metrics for autonomous research agents do not measure whether their intermediate research decisions and artifacts align with those of human experts.
hctrVEKkGJ.method: AutoResearcher-Human Research Similarity (AutoHRS) provides a stage-wise reconstruction benchmark built from 152 ICLR oral papers, generating 456 research trajectories across workflow stages (such as gap identification, idea generation, and solution design) to measure alignment between auto-researcher outputs and ground-truth human research decisions.
hctrVEKkGJ.key_idea: Decompose published ICLR oral papers into stage-wise research contexts and measure how closely autonomous research agents reconstruct the subsequent human research decisions and artifacts.
hctrVEKkGJ.evidence: Evaluated across 456 generated research trajectories derived from 152 ICLR oral papers.
hctrVEKkGJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the stage-wise reconstruction formulation for auditing autonomous research agents beyond final task completion timely and well-structured.
hctrVEKkGJ.main_concern: Reviewers note that similarity to a published paper's specific decisions does not measure scientific validity or originality (penalizing valid alternative ideas), and experiments only test a single agent setup (ClaudeCode / Sonnet 4.5).

GhCb2ZuoHN.one_liner: Guides LLM program evolution for multi-agent policies under sparse rewards using parent-child execution trace comparisons for mutation, selection, and scheduling.
GhCb2ZuoHN.problem: Under sparse task-completion feedback, unsuccessful synthesized multi-agent program policies receive identical zero fitness scores, creating plateaus where fitness alone cannot guide selection or revision.
GhCb2ZuoHN.method: BehEvolve retains parent-child code diffs and paired execution traces, using a feedback LLM to generate behavioral diagnoses for program mutation, pairwise behavioral preferences for parent selection, and progress signals for idea-level branch scheduling without hand-designed process rewards.
GhCb2ZuoHN.key_idea: Compare paired parent-child execution traces with an LLM judge to produce behavioral mutation diagnoses, relative parent-selection rankings, and strategy-branch scheduling under zero-fitness plateaus.
GhCb2ZuoHN.evidence: Evaluated across eight VMAS multi-agent tasks and five Overcooked layouts against general evolution (AdaEvolve) and domain-specific (KnowPC) baselines, including token-matched controls.
GhCb2ZuoHN.claimed_gains: Achieves an average success rate of 81.5% on VMAS and 12.6 soups on Overcooked, outperforming AdaEvolve by 29.0% and KnowPC by 18.9%.
GhCb2ZuoHN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that leveraging parent-child execution trace comparisons effectively breaks zero-fitness ties in multi-agent program evolution and is well-supported by controlled ablations.
GhCb2ZuoHN.main_concern: Reviewers note that the feedback LLM is given continuous success predicates that could trivially define a distance-to-threshold shaped reward without an LLM judge, and biases or noise in pairwise LLM behavioral judgments are not thoroughly analyzed.

T3lOPR4HCP.one_liner: Reuses learned cross-view reference samples and relation weights to jointly recover missing view representations and directly estimate soft cluster assignments.
T3lOPR4HCP.problem: In incomplete multi-view clustering, missing-view representation imputation and cluster-assignment estimation typically use different sample relations, failing to align recovered features with target-view cluster memberships.
T3lOPR4HCP.method: ReSA learns cross-view relation representations via instance-level contrastive learning and neighborhood distribution consistency. For a sample missing a target view, it retrieves top related reference samples observed in both views and reuses the exact same reference samples and relation weights both to aggregate target-view latent representations and to directly estimate target-view soft cluster assignments.
T3lOPR4HCP.key_idea: Retrieve cross-view reference samples via contrastive relation embeddings and reuse identical reference weights for both missing latent representation recovery and direct soft cluster-assignment aggregation.
T3lOPR4HCP.evidence: Evaluated across multiple incomplete multi-view clustering datasets (including ALOI-100, HandWritten, and Hdigit) and missing-view rates with controlled Hellinger discrepancy comparisons.
T3lOPR4HCP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the pipeline clear and technically sound, noting that sharing reference samples and weights between feature imputation and soft-assignment estimation provides a consistent design with strong clustering performance.
T3lOPR4HCP.main_concern: Reviewers view reusing the same neighbor weights for both imputation and soft assignment as a narrow incremental refinement with small accuracy margins (<0.7 percentage points) over standard two-step assignment on recovered features.

7mUMwemV8u.one_liner: Characterizes the geometric separation exponent and primal-dual certificates needed for observation records to justify replacing a baseline controller with a frozen learned controller.
7mUMwemV8u.problem: A finite calibration record can be consistent with multiple system models that imply opposite decisions on whether replacing a baseline controller with a frozen learned controller is safe and beneficial.
7mUMwemV8u.method: Paired Hybrid Policy Improvement (PHPI) characterizes the separation exponent—the rate at which the minimum observation gap between conflicting models vanishes as performance/safety margins shrink—and derives exact primal-dual certificates for a restricted positive-monomial class, alongside recurrent-control timing constructions.
7mUMwemV8u.key_idea: Characterize the observation-gap separation exponent between feasible models with conflicting deployment verdicts and construct primal-dual certificates to rule out unsafe controller replacements without full system identification.
7mUMwemV8u.evidence: Analytical recurrent-control and ReLU closed-loop constructions plus numerical and real-time simulation studies on a DC microgrid with a frozen 89-parameter GRU controller across 16,384 histories.
7mUMwemV8u.claimed_gains: A frozen 89-parameter GRU reproduces all complete-execution labels across 16,384 histories in the DC microgrid study, with joint readouts resolving single-port collisions.
7mUMwemV8u.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the formalization of when finite experimental evidence suffices to certify replacing a baseline controller with a learned controller without full plant identification.
7mUMwemV8u.main_concern: Reviewers find the theoretical assumptions (such as externally supplied chart catalogues and positive-monomial restrictions) restrictive and hard to apply to general nonlinear systems, while heavy undefined terminology makes the paper difficult to follow.

1mANJJuebs.one_liner: Analyzes how input variance degrades long-term memory retention in Mamba S6 recurrences and introduces a Gumbel-Softmax-based initialization to preserve near-unit state transitions.
1mANJJuebs.problem: In selective state space models (Mamba S6), high input variability degrades long-range information retention, and standard initialization shifts discretized state transitions toward zero rather than one as state size grows.
1mANJJuebs.method: Analyzes expected log-retention and local sensitivity in the S6 recurrence under input variance, proving that standard Mamba initialization fails to increase the proportion of discretized state matrix entries near 1 as state dimension grows. Proposes a Gumbel-Softmax-inspired bias initialization that places discretized state transition values close to 1 without altering the model architecture.
1mANJJuebs.key_idea: Modify the selective SSM step-size bias initialization using a Gumbel-Softmax distribution so discretized state transition eigenvalues concentrate near 1 to preserve long-term memory under input variance.
1mANJJuebs.evidence: Theoretical log-retention and sensitivity proofs plus empirical evaluations on synthetic copying tasks and Long Range Arena (LRA) benchmarks.
1mANJJuebs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the observation that standard Mamba initialization bounds the count of near-1 state transitions independently of state size N and appreciate the simple, zero-overhead initialization fix that improves LRA results.
1mANJJuebs.main_concern: Reviewers question whether input variability is the true driver of the gains—noting Theorem 1 relies simply on Jensen's inequality without modeling input-dependent state writes, and strong gains appear even on constant-token copying tasks with zero input variance.

5pn56kXIZb.one_liner: Proves that requiring point predictors to compose exactly across time incurs excess squared-error risk whenever conditional means do not compose, whereas composing distributions avoids it.
5pn56kXIZb.problem: Enforcing multi-step compositional consistency on point predictors conflicts with squared-error optimality in stochastic nonlinear dynamics because conditional expectations generally do not obey the Chapman-Kolmogorov composition law.
5pn56kXIZb.method: Derives lower bounds on the excess risk of any exactly composing point predictor proportional to the squared mean-composition defect with sharp rates in smoothness and noise, gives a drift-and-noise criterion characterizing when diffusion conditional means compose, and shows that composing Markov transition laws (via closed-form transformed linear diffusions or sample rollout) eliminates the defect.
5pn56kXIZb.key_idea: Lower-bound the excess L2 risk of any compositionally consistent point predictor by the squared Chapman-Kolmogorov mean-composition defect and eliminate the penalty by composing predictive distributions instead of conditional means.
5pn56kXIZb.evidence: Theoretical risk lower bounds, small-noise asymptotics, drift-noise characterization propositions, and controlled fixed-model propagation experiments on synthetic chains and dynamical systems (such as Lorenz).
5pn56kXIZb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clear theoretical distinction between composing conditional means and composing transition distributions, along with the sharp smoothness and small-noise risk bounds.
5pn56kXIZb.main_concern: Reviewers note that the distinction between iterative mean rollout and distributional ensemble propagation is classical, Theorem 1 follows from a triangle inequality with potentially large coverage constants, and experiments do not evaluate modern flow-map or consistency-model benchmarks.

lUusjOJd13.one_liner: Maps arbitrary relational databases and prediction tasks into a fixed universal schema so standard relational deep learning models can pretrain and transfer across databases.
lUusjOJd13.problem: Relational deep learning models are normally tied to a single database schema, and existing relational foundation models handle schema variation by designing specialized model architectures.
lUusjOJd13.method: Defines an information-preserving data transformation that re-encodes any relational database's tables, typed attributes, foreign-key links, timestamps, and task specifications into a fixed universal schema, enabling standard off-the-shelf relational GNNs (such as GraphSAGE) to be trained across heterogeneous databases and transferred zero-shot or fine-tuned on unseen databases.
lUusjOJd13.key_idea: Move cross-database schema agnosticism from model architecture to data representation by mapping arbitrary relational schemas and tasks into a fixed meta-relational schema.
lUusjOJd13.evidence: Evaluated on RelBench classification and regression tasks using a standard GraphSAGE backbone under the leave-one-database-out Relational Transformer protocol.
lUusjOJd13.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find decoupling schema agnosticism from model architecture via a universal database representation clean, intuitive, and architectural-overhead-free.
lUusjOJd13.main_concern: Reviewers point out that ablations show zero-shot transfer gains on RelBench are driven almost entirely by historical target self-labels and task description text rather than relational schema structure, and checkpoint/hyperparameter selection used target validation data.

OSZl2MvK6k.one_liner: Constructs a 229K-hour multilingual speech corpus with multi-view utterance, long-form monologue, and multi-speaker dialogue annotations plus style instructions and vocalization tags.
OSZl2MvK6k.problem: Open speech generation corpora mostly consist of short utterances under tens of seconds and benchmarks cover at most two speakers, limiting controllable long-form and multi-speaker speech synthesis.
OSZl2MvK6k.method: Continuo processes 229K hours of in-the-wild multilingual audio into linked short utterances, single-speaker long-form passages, and multi-speaker turn-taking dialogues (preserving pauses and transitions), augmented with 4.77M natural-language style instructions, 933K nonverbal-vocalization tags, and a 23-hour bilingual benchmark (Continuo-testset) with up to 30-minute, 4-speaker recordings. The authors also train 0.6B autoregressive and non-autoregressive TTS baselines on the dataset.
OSZl2MvK6k.key_idea: Preserve continuous multi-scale views (utterances, long monologues, and multi-speaker dialogues with natural pauses) from in-the-wild recordings paired with text instructions and nonverbal vocalization tags.
OSZl2MvK6k.evidence: Trains 0.6B autoregressive (AR) and non-autoregressive (NAR) models on Continuo and evaluates on TTSD-Eval, Continuo-testset, Long-TTS-Eval, and InstructTTSEval against MOSS-TTSD (8B) and Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-VD.
OSZl2MvK6k.claimed_gains: Dataset spans 229K hours (50.0% of monologue hours and 66.8% of dialogue hours >5 min; 4.77M instruction and 933K nonverbal examples); 0.6B Continuo-NAR achieves 5.27% Chinese CER and 9.93% English WER on TTSD-Eval, and Continuo-AR reaches 76.2/78.3 (zh/en) on InstructTTSEval.
OSZl2MvK6k.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that Continuo is a large, well-structured dataset contribution that preserves long-form temporal structure, pauses, multi-speaker turns, and expressive annotations missing from short-clip corpora.
OSZl2MvK6k.main_concern: Reviewers note that the paper does not train a controlled baseline model on a mixture of existing open datasets to isolate the data gain of Continuo, and automated annotation errors (such as emotion tagging and >30s captioning) and overlap filtering are insufficiently audited.

59TfLUgu4l.one_liner: Measures full-reference signal degradation across modalities via the symmetric KL divergence between diagonal Fisher information profiles of a single frozen SIREN network.
59TfLUgu4l.problem: Conventional full-reference signal degradation metrics are hand-crafted for specific modalities and often saturate or lose monotonicity under severe distortions.
59TfLUgu4l.method: SymKL fits an implicit neural representation (SIREN) once to the pristine reference signal, freezes its weights, and derives a closed-form expression for its diagonal Fisher information. Evaluating the diagonal Fisher profile on both the pristine reference and the degraded observation yields two normalized parameter-sensitivity distributions whose symmetric KL divergence defines the degradation score.
