59TfLUgu4l.key_idea: Fit and freeze a single SIREN on the pristine reference signal, then compute the symmetric KL divergence between its closed-form diagonal Fisher sensitivity profiles on the reference and degraded signals.
59TfLUgu4l.evidence: Analytical closed-form diagonal Fisher derivation for SIREN and empirical degradation-tracking experiments across image, speech/audio, and volumetric 3D occupancy benchmarks.
59TfLUgu4l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate evaluating both reference and degraded signals on a single frozen reference INR to avoid parameter misalignment and achieve a modality-agnostic degradation measure across images, audio, and 3D data.
59TfLUgu4l.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the quantitative evaluation relies primarily on relative sensitivity/elasticity—which can be artificially inflated by applying any monotonic nonlinear power transform to an existing metric without improving ranking discrimination—and omits citation/comparison to closely related INRIQ.

LQcCkc4OIN.one_liner: Decomposes VLM responses into atomic visual claims verified by multi-agent visual questioning and regulated for informativeness to provide label-free RL rewards.
LQcCkc4OIN.problem: Mitigating hallucinations in vision-language models typically requires human annotations or external ground-truth supervision, limiting scalability on unlabeled image corpora.
LQcCkc4OIN.method: MARVEL decomposes generated VLM responses into atomic claims, reformulates them into visual verification questions answered against the image to compute consistency scores, and applies a Visual Claim Regulation (VCR) mechanism that penalizes trivial or redundant claims to form reinforcement learning rewards without ground-truth labels.
LQcCkc4OIN.key_idea: Turn unlabeled VLM responses into self-supervised RL rewards by decomposing outputs into atomic visual claims, cross-examining them via visual question answering, and regularizing against trivial claims.
LQcCkc4OIN.evidence: Evaluated across 12 benchmarks covering hallucination evaluation, real-world VQA, and general multimodal understanding across multiple VLM scales.
LQcCkc4OIN.claimed_gains: Achieves average improvements of +3.30 on hallucination evaluation benchmarks, +1.74 on real-world VQA, and +4.07 on general multimodal understanding benchmarks across 12 benchmarks.
LQcCkc4OIN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the label-free multi-agent claim verification pipeline paired with Visual Claim Regulation to prevent reward hacking from generic claims is intuitive and well-motivated.
LQcCkc4OIN.main_concern: Reviewers point out a mismatch between the broad claim-verification framing and the actual claim extraction prompt in Appendix A.1, which restricts extracted description claims solely to color, five coarse image positions, and explicit numeric quantities while omitting object existence, actions, and text.

amyi0tJd3V.one_liner: Audits how efficiency-oriented training shortcuts across vision and language models increase adversarial, privacy, and forgetting vulnerabilities via sharper loss geometry.
amyi0tJd3V.problem: Efficiency-oriented training strategies reduce compute and data overhead, but their impact on model robustness, privacy leakage, and alignment stability remains underexamined.
amyi0tJd3V.method: Conducts a cross-domain empirical and geometric study comparing efficient training strategies—including selective data sampling, efficient pre-training, and simplified 'zero RL' alignment—against standard training baselines under matched clean utility, analyzing adversarial robustness, membership inference privacy attacks, catastrophic forgetting, loss landscape sharpness, and representation structure.
amyi0tJd3V.key_idea: Benchmark efficiency-trained vision and language models against accuracy-matched standard counterparts across adversarial, privacy, and forgetting evaluations while probing loss-landscape sharpness and representational geometry.
amyi0tJd3V.evidence: Evaluated across vision models (ResNet-18, Swin-Tiny on subsets of CIFAR-10, TinyImageNet, PubFig83) and language model checkpoints under adversarial attacks, membership inference, and simplified RL alignment.
amyi0tJd3V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that investigating the hidden security, privacy, and robustness costs of training-efficiency shortcuts alongside internal loss geometry is an important and timely research direction.
amyi0tJd3V.main_concern: Reviewers note that the experimental scale (small vision models with 36-48% test accuracy on dataset subsets and only three uncontrolled pre-existing LLM checkpoints) does not match the foundation-model framing, and the disparate efficiency settings prevent drawing a unified causal conclusion.

ZAimy2M5Ug.one_liner: Selects zoom-in crops for GUI grounding directly from coordinate-decoding attention heads refined by low-rank residual adapters trained with a containment-ranking loss.
ZAimy2M5Ug.problem: Two-stage zoom-in inference for high-resolution GUI grounding requires decoding a coarse coordinate in a preliminary forward pass before cropping, roughly doubling inference latency.
ZAimy2M5Ug.method: ZoomSD extracts coarse target localization directly from a small subset of attention heads involved in coordinate decoding to select a zoom crop without preliminary coordinate generation. It refines these attention maps using Isolated Localization-Head Residuals (ILR)—lightweight low-rank corrections trained with a containment-ranking objective whose gradients are isolated from the OPSD-trained backbone.
ZAimy2M5Ug.key_idea: Read zoom-in crop regions directly from coordinate-decoding attention heads enhanced by isolated low-rank residual adapters trained to maximize target box containment, bypassing first-pass coordinate generation.
ZAimy2M5Ug.evidence: Evaluated across multiple GUI grounding benchmarks and two model sizes against GUI-SD and two-stage coordinate-decoding zoom baselines.
ZAimy2M5Ug.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the observation that native attention heads encode coarse target locations, enabling lower-latency zoom-in GUI grounding without first decoding text coordinates.
ZAimy2M5Ug.main_concern: Reviewers note that almost all accuracy gains over the base model come simply from zooming in with native attention maps, while the proposed ILR module and joint OPSD training add only marginal improvements (0.1-3.1 points) over post-hoc or uncalibrated attention cropping.

ZjON93Afaq.one_liner: Accelerates GRPO training for autonomous machine learning engineering agents by repurposing execution traces into an evolving task buffer sampled by reward-variance learnability.
ZjON93Afaq.problem: Applying reinforcement learning to long-horizon autonomous machine learning engineering (MLE) suffers from prohibitive code-execution latency and inefficient uniform task sampling.
ZjON93Afaq.method: AceGRPO combines an Evolving Data Buffer that continuously converts intermediate execution traces (both partial successes and failures) into reusable training starting states with an Adaptive Sampling curriculum guided by a Learnability Potential function based on group reward dispersion to prioritize tasks at the agent's learning frontier.
ZjON93Afaq.key_idea: Recycle intermediate MLE execution traces into a dynamic starting-state buffer and prioritize training tasks with high group reward variance to focus RL updates on the learnability frontier.
ZjON93Afaq.evidence: Trains Ace-35B (and Ace-30B for ablations) with AceGRPO and evaluates on MLE-Bench-Lite against base models and vanilla GRPO.
ZjON93Afaq.claimed_gains: Ace-35B achieves a 100% valid submission rate on MLE-Bench-Lite and substantially outperforms its base model.
ZjON93Afaq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that recycling intermediate execution states into an evolving training buffer is a practical and effective way to mitigate long-horizon execution costs in MLE agent RL.
ZjON93Afaq.main_concern: Reviewers point out that using unnormalized reward variance as a proxy for gradient magnitude is mathematically flawed under GRPO's standard deviation advantage normalization, and comparisons against existing dynamic-sampling RL methods like DAPO are missing.

sNRqeY8bT1.one_liner: Benchmarks whether long-horizon agents proactively query and store future-critical environment state before task-required transitions make that information permanently unobservable.
sNRqeY8bT1.problem: Existing long-horizon agent benchmarks test memory of already-observed information but do not causally isolate whether agents proactively acquire currently queryable state before an irreversible transition removes access to it.
sNRqeY8bT1.method: ForesightBench formalizes prospective information acquisition under irreversible observability loss and provides 90 executable, outcome-verified tasks across eight operational domains (50 Standard and 40 Frontier tasks). Each Frontier task is paired with a matched Persistent Control that keeps the query interface accessible after the transition to causally isolate failures due to missed pre-transition acquisition.
sNRqeY8bT1.key_idea: Pair executable long-horizon tasks where a required action permanently closes an information window with matched persistent-access controls to causally measure prospective state acquisition.
sNRqeY8bT1.evidence: Evaluated six agent systems under a common scaffold across 90 tasks and 200 completed matched Frontier-Control pairs across five systems with Holm-corrected statistical tests.
sNRqeY8bT1.claimed_gains: Six agent systems achieve 21.1-41.1% overall success (30.0-62.0% on Standard, 2.5-20.0% on Frontier), while preserving state access in matched controls increases success by 47.5-97.5 percentage points (p_adj <= 1.4e-4).
sNRqeY8bT1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clear problem formulation isolating prospective information acquisition from retrospective memory and the causal Challenge-vs-Persistent-Control experimental design.
sNRqeY8bT1.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the constructed tasks reflect realistic operational workflows where observability loss is predictable from environment documentation, and note the absence of simple prompting baselines that instruct the agent to dump state before transitions.

K97WYPrbKO.one_liner: Audits internal hallucination probes across observability, readoutability, support identifiability, and causal interventions to test whether predictive directions justify mechanistic claims.
K97WYPrbKO.problem: Studies on internal hallucination scores often conflate predictive accuracy of a probe with identifying a reproducible causal mechanism or actionable repair direction inside the model.
K97WYPrbKO.method: Introduces an executable measurement-to-claim audit structured around risk observability, conditional quantitative readoutability, and support identifiability, followed by controlled activation-intervention tests (including output-token remapping and fixed-question evidence contrasts) on Gemma-2-2B-IT across 110 source groups and 192 frozen sources.
K97WYPrbKO.key_idea: Separate predictive probe accuracy from causal mechanistic claims via a staged audit testing support reproducibility, output-label remapping invariance, and targeted activation interventions.
K97WYPrbKO.evidence: Evaluated on synthetic nonlinear control models and natural LLM targets (primarily Gemma-2-2B-IT across 110 source groups and 192 frozen sources, plus Qwen checks).
K97WYPrbKO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the methodological rigor of separating error prediction from causal mechanistic claims and highlight the output-mapping manipulation as an effective diagnostic against overclaiming in probing studies.
K97WYPrbKO.main_concern: Reviewers note that the natural-LLM experiments lack a positive control where an intervention succeeds on a known causal mechanism, making null intervention results on small candidate-answer tasks difficult to interpret.

pUbowhIYJM.one_liner: Uses an embedding's local angular neighborhood density as a label-free measure of input typicality to predict downstream accuracy and cross-model representation agreement.
pUbowhIYJM.problem: Assessing whether an individual input is reliably represented by a self-supervised model normally requires ground-truth labels, class structure, or downstream task evaluation.
pUbowhIYJM.method: Defines an embedding's angular density (average cosine similarity to its local nearest neighbors in an unlabeled reference set) as a label-free proxy for input typicality and evaluates its correlation with classification accuracy, QA correctness, and cross-model representation similarity across vision, vision-language, and language encoders.
pUbowhIYJM.key_idea: Measure the local angular density of an embedding among unlabeled neighbors on the unit hypersphere as a label-free indicator of input typicality and representation reliability.
pUbowhIYJM.evidence: Empirical correlation study across 21 models spanning three paradigms (7 self-supervised vision models trained across checkpoints, 5 vision-language models, and 9 language models) comparing angular density against embedding norm, global centroid distance, and supervised Mahalanobis distance.
pUbowhIYJM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the broad, systematic empirical evaluation across 21 vision, vision-language, and language models showing that local angular density consistently outperforms global centroid distance as a label-free reliability proxy.
pUbowhIYJM.main_concern: Reviewers note that the evidence is purely correlational without comparison to standard output-confidence baselines (such as predictive entropy or logit margin) and that k-NN density in embedding space is nearly identical to existing unsupervised OOD detection metrics (Sun et al., 2022).

saxgnlIEvu.one_liner: Organizes long-term agent memory as a state-evolving graph with temporal event trajectories and retrieves evidence via intent-guided multi-round query expansion.
saxgnlIEvu.problem: Static agent memory representations and single-round retrieval fail to track how facts evolve or conflict across long-term interaction histories.
saxgnlIEvu.method: EMIR^2 constructs a State-Evolving Memory Graph (SEMG) that links semantic knowledge states to temporal event trajectories with explicit update and conflict relations. An intent-guided multi-round retrieval controller iteratively identifies missing evidence from accumulated context and expands graph retrieval across rounds.
saxgnlIEvu.key_idea: Track factual updates and conflicts in a state-evolving memory graph with supersede/contradict links and pair it with an iterative intent-guided multi-round retrieval loop.
saxgnlIEvu.evidence: Evaluated on the LoCoMo and MemConflict benchmarks covering long-term memory utilization, dynamic and static conflict handling, and multi-hop retrieval.
saxgnlIEvu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explicitly modeling temporal fact evolution and contradictions in a structured memory graph paired with multi-round retrieval addresses a realistic limitation of long-horizon LLM agents.
saxgnlIEvu.main_concern: Reviewers point out that ablations conflate graph state versioning with multi-round retrieval and summaries, performance on conditional conflicts drops below baselines, and LoCoMo evaluations omit a simple full-context window baseline (~16-18K tokens).

zJAORUCoh5.one_liner: Narrows the accuracy gap between parallel and sequential LLM post-training quantization by regularizing each layer's weights against upstream activation noise in parallel.
zJAORUCoh5.problem: Parallel layer-wise post-training quantization is fast but suffers from compounding residual-stream errors across depth, whereas sequential re-calibration corrects upstream errors at the cost of a serial bottleneck.
zJAORUCoh5.method: Models upstream quantization error as isotropic activation noise and applies a general linear preprocessing transformation (activation denoising) followed by metric-weighted rounding independently at every layer in parallel. This induces a depth-compounding smoothness penalty that dampens error amplification and composes with orthogonal weight rotations.
zJAORUCoh5.key_idea: Pre-multiply layer weights by a regularized linear activation-denoising transform before parallel metric-weighted rounding so each layer dampens upstream quantization noise without sequential calibration.
zJAORUCoh5.evidence: Evaluated on Llama-2 and Llama-3.2 models across parallel and sequential PTQ baselines (including GPTQ and QuIP#).
zJAORUCoh5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the robustness perspective on parallel vs. sequential quantization clearly written, mathematically unifying, and compatible with existing rounding and rotation methods.
zJAORUCoh5.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical necessity of saving offline sequential calibration time (e.g., 306 minutes on one GPU vs. 41 minutes on eight GPUs for a one-time 13B model quantization) when sequential or end-to-end optimized PTQ (like SpinQuant) achieves higher final model quality.

n1Zr81aHsx.one_liner: A shared transformer compares masked, predictive-embedding, and autoregressive pretraining against tuned scratch baselines for intracortical sequence decoding.
n1Zr81aHsx.problem: It is unclear whether self-supervised pretraining consistently improves neural decoding at currently limited and fragmented intracortical data scales.
n1Zr81aHsx.method: The study standardizes multi-subject, multi-behavior, cross-species recordings and compares MAE, JEPA, autoregressive pretraining, and scratch training with a common BIT transformer. Matched fine-tuning search budgets help isolate pretraining-objective effects.
n1Zr81aHsx.key_idea: Hold the transformer backbone and tuning budget fixed while varying pretraining objective and corpus composition.
n1Zr81aHsx.evidence: Up to 345 recording hours combine 208 hours from 6 humans and 137 hours from 19 non-human primates, with speech, handwriting, and typing decoding evaluations.
n1Zr81aHsx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the standardized recording collection and controlled comparison against carefully tuned scratch baselines.
n1Zr81aHsx.main_concern: The absence of few-shot or low-data transfer analysis leaves a key regime for pretraining benefits untested.

6rih2tIbm5.one_liner: HEAR separates text-aligned and text-deviating audiovisual evidence, reasons hierarchically, and injects incremental pseudo-tokens into a frozen language model.
6rih2tIbm5.problem: Global multimodal fusion can obscure subtle sentiment cues and informative disagreement between text, audio, and vision.
6rih2tIbm5.method: HEAR extracts temporal and spectral audiovisual evidence, conditions it on text, and preserves aligned and deviating branches. Local-to-global reasoning produces hierarchical evidence that is incrementally projected into pseudo-tokens for sentiment prediction with a frozen LLM.
6rih2tIbm5.key_idea: Preserve text-conditioned agreement and discrepancy in separate evidence branches, then incrementally project hierarchical evidence into LLM pseudo-tokens.
6rih2tIbm5.evidence: Reviews describe four English and Chinese benchmarks including CMU-MOSEI, three frozen LLM backbones, matched MSE-Adapter comparisons, ablations, and five seeds.
6rih2tIbm5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the coherent evidence-processing pipeline and broad controlled evaluation across datasets and frozen LLM backbones.
6rih2tIbm5.main_concern: Addition and subtraction with text-conditioned representations do not establish that the branches capture meaningful semantic agreement and discrepancy.

2fjVHePiD3.one_liner: Meta-reinforcement learning trains agents to explore tools, extract reusable operational skills, and apply them to subsequent tasks.
2fjVHePiD3.problem: Tool descriptions often omit implicit operational rules needed to succeed in unfamiliar environments.
2fjVHePiD3.method: MetaSkill trains exploration, skill extraction, and exploitation over a distribution of tool-using environments. Success on a distinct query task rewards knowledge extracted from limited support-task interactions.
2fjVHePiD3.key_idea: Train exploration and skill extraction using success on a distinct query task so extracted operational knowledge transfers within an environment.
2fjVHePiD3.evidence: Experiments cover multiple model sizes, in-distribution and out-of-distribution environments, cross-benchmark transfer, and stage-wise ablations.
2fjVHePiD3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the meta-learning formulation that trains agents to acquire and reuse environment-specific operational knowledge.
2fjVHePiD3.main_concern: The evaluation does not clearly establish how well the learned adaptation generalizes to genuinely unseen operational rules.

uU2YSF1vU5.one_liner: Tumor-conditioned diffusion residuals and trajectory selection guide longitudinal MRI forecasts toward future lesion fidelity.
uU2YSF1vU5.problem: Longitudinal MRI generators can preserve anatomy while missing tumor changes, and stronger tumor supervision can impair image quality.
uU2YSF1vU5.method: TUG conditions generative residuals on tumor structure, follow-up interval, and treatment while supervising clean-image lesion estimates and intermediate diffusion features. At inference, tumor-aware scorers prune trajectories and weight completed predictions using terminal tumor evidence.
uU2YSF1vU5.key_idea: Inject tumor and treatment information into diffusion residuals, then prune and weight forecast trajectories according to predicted tumor evidence.
uU2YSF1vU5.evidence: Experiments across three longitudinal glioma MRI cohorts compare image and lesion fidelity with existing forecasting methods and include component ablations.
uU2YSF1vU5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that whole-volume image metrics can hide lesion errors and that tumor-focused longitudinal forecasting addresses a meaningful gap.
uU2YSF1vU5.main_concern: The same segmenter guides training, trajectory selection, and evaluation, so tumor Dice gains may reflect fitting the evaluator rather than better tumor evolution.

qSF6LxtL76.one_liner: Coordinated poisoned skills separate a fabricated execution rationale from an intact downstream malicious operation.
qSF6LxtL76.problem: Skill-poisoning evaluations do not explicitly separate the contextual justification for execution from the operation an agent performs.
qSF6LxtL76.method: CoordPoison places an intact operation in a downstream Steering Skill while an upstream Grounding Skill alters persistent artifacts to create its pretext. An automated workflow uses execution dependencies and runtime feedback to construct coordinated attacks.
qSF6LxtL76.key_idea: Alter persistent artifacts through one skill so a separate downstream skill's intact malicious operation appears justified by the task context.
qSF6LxtL76.evidence: Reviews describe runtime-feedback experiments, transfer to MiniMax-M3, and within-session and cross-session attack evaluations.
qSF6LxtL76.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the usefulness of studying coordinated skill poisoning and the empirical attack results.
qSF6LxtL76.main_concern: Conditional or optimization-stage success rates and missing uncertainty estimates make headline attack efficacy difficult to interpret.

OTvChsVpc4.one_liner: Lipschitz extension reconstructs future costs from landmark predictions for online decisions in metrical task systems.
OTvChsVpc4.problem: Predicting future values for every state can require more information than an online metrical task system needs.
OTvChsVpc4.method: The method predicts canonical dual values only at fixed landmark states and reconstructs full-state values with a Lipschitz extension. A value-greedy policy acts on these values, with error controlled by landmark coverage and shift-invariant prediction error.
OTvChsVpc4.key_idea: Reconstruct full-state future values from fixed landmark predictions using a Lipschitz extension, then choose actions with a value-greedy policy.
OTvChsVpc4.evidence: The paper proves an excess-cost upper bound, a matching lower bound for sparse finite lines, and learning guarantees from independent training episodes.
OTvChsVpc4.claimed_gains: Additive excess cost is bounded by O(T r(L) + sum_{t<T} delta_t), with matching covering-radius dependence on sparse unit-spaced finite lines.
OTvChsVpc4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value studying prediction granularity in metrical task systems and the lower bound supporting the compression tradeoff.
OTvChsVpc4.main_concern: Underdefined terms and difficult exposition obscure the technical contributions, particularly the lower-bound argument.

sBeL4xbNkQ.one_liner: Hierarchical suffix refinements turn frozen marginal forecasts into weighted trajectories with exact shared-prefix merging.
sBeL4xbNkQ.problem: Marginal time-step forecasts do not capture joint temporal dependence or quantities defined over entire trajectories.
sBeL4xbNkQ.method: CPSS converts TimesFM-2.5 marginals into 64 weighted trajectories by refining broad alternatives with suffix-supported variations. Truncation merges identical prefixes and sums their probabilities.
sBeL4xbNkQ.key_idea: Build weighted trajectories through nested suffix refinements that preserve shared prefixes and aggregate identical prefixes exactly under truncation.
sBeL4xbNkQ.evidence: Experiments span eight datasets and a separate 12-domain, 128-step benchmark, with a matched 64-trajectory baseline and nested-sharing controls.
sBeL4xbNkQ.claimed_gains: On the 12-domain, 128-step benchmark, CPSS reduces complete-trajectory error by 6.80% and path-dependent quantity error by 16.80%.
sBeL4xbNkQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that joint trajectory forecasting addresses a practical limitation of marginal forecasts and appreciate the structured branching representation.
sBeL4xbNkQ.main_concern: The consistency claim applies to truncating one forecast and does not establish consistency across separately trained forecast horizons.

hnoPpdzS4U.one_liner: Neuron suppression identifies MLP parameters to fine-tune toward uniform demographic-group probabilities with completions held fixed.
hnoPpdzS4U.problem: Reducing a pairwise bias gap can leave a language model's preferences across other demographic groups unequal.
hnoPpdzS4U.method: Multigroup-StereoSet varies dispersed demographic groups while holding stereotype and anti-stereotype completions fixed. DAID identifies MLP neurons whose suppression makes group probabilities more uniform, then fine-tunes only their parameters.
hnoPpdzS4U.key_idea: Select neurons by how their suppression shifts fixed-completion group probabilities toward uniformity, then restrict fine-tuning to those neurons.
hnoPpdzS4U.evidence: Experiments evaluate four models on English text using Multigroup-StereoSet, StereoSet ICAT, MMLU, and editing or activation-intervention baselines.
hnoPpdzS4U.claimed_gains: Median max/min group-probability ratios fall from 23-35 to 1.3-2.3 for nationality and from 97-138 to below 1.5 for occupation, while ICAT rises 6-16 points at a cost of 1-5.4 MMLU points.
hnoPpdzS4U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value multigroup evaluation as a way to expose demographic disparities that pairwise bias metrics miss.
hnoPpdzS4U.main_concern: Limited model coverage and reuse of training contexts in evaluation leave generalization to new models and contexts uncertain.

s6VjdGUHX7.one_liner: Task-specific KL constraints adapt protection strengths during continual LoRA training using stored output distributions.
s6VjdGUHX7.problem: Parameter-space separation and aggregate drift penalties can miss severe forgetting on individual previous tasks.
s6VjdGUHX7.method: DualKL stores representative examples and output distributions after each task, then constrains each previous task's predictive KL drift separately. Primal–dual updates increase protection when a task exceeds its budget and relax it when stable.
s6VjdGUHX7.key_idea: Assign each previous task a separate predictive-KL constraint and adaptive dual variable measured on stored examples.
s6VjdGUHX7.evidence: Evaluation includes Standard CL, the complete 15-task Long Sequence benchmark, Llama, Qwen, and T5-large models, plus runtime, memory, and sensitivity analyses.
s6VjdGUHX7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize that task-wise predictive-distribution constraints address forgetting that aggregate or parameter-space measures can conceal.
s6VjdGUHX7.main_concern: Average KL control on a small stored anchor set does not guarantee preservation of individual anchors or the full previous-task distribution.

O5d5gVEBLs.one_liner: Sinkhorn-normalized prior interactions combine heterogeneous denoisers within an inertial deep equilibrium solver.
O5d5gVEBLs.problem: Combining expressive heterogeneous priors in deep equilibrium models can undermine convergence stability.
O5d5gVEBLs.method: MHC-DEM maps a query distribution through a learned doubly stochastic interaction matrix to produce convex prior-fusion weights. An inertial second-order solver operates in an augmented state space using the fused priors.
O5d5gVEBLs.key_idea: Use Sinkhorn normalization to constrain prior interactions to the Birkhoff polytope before computing convex fusion weights for inertial equilibrium updates.
O5d5gVEBLs.evidence: Inverse-problem reconstruction experiments include fusion-strategy, refinement-depth, and momentum ablations alongside convergence analysis.
O5d5gVEBLs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find combining complementary priors in equilibrium reconstruction well motivated and empirically effective.
O5d5gVEBLs.main_concern: Doubly stochastic interactions do not by themselves justify the claimed prevention of concentrated or collapsed fusion weights.

brzge06SlD.one_liner: A local branch-posterior correction supplements soft-embedding distillation with supervision for alternative reasoning branches.
brzge06SlD.problem: Discrete rollouts supervise only one reasoning continuation, while naive soft trajectories can erase branch-specific information.
brzge06SlD.method: BASED decomposes hard-branch KL into mixture and branch-posterior terms to identify supervision missing from soft distillation. It combines soft KL with a local branch-posterior correction at selected positions.
brzge06SlD.key_idea: Add local branch-posterior KL supervision to soft-trajectory KL so mixture matching retains information distinguishing alternative reasoning branches.
brzge06SlD.evidence: The abstract reports nine mathematics, science, and code-generation benchmarks at two student scales, with gradient and trajectory analyses.
brzge06SlD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the mixture-versus-branch-posterior decomposition a useful explanation of what soft-embedding distillation omits.
brzge06SlD.main_concern: The experiments insufficiently isolate whether the branch-posterior correction recovers the missing supervision and drives the observed gains.

gJvWSNcUtw.one_liner: Closed-loop reinforcement learning selects reasoning questions per driving frame using episode outcomes and dense step rewards.
gJvWSNcUtw.problem: Fixed reasoning chains can distract driving policies, while local answer objectives miss a question's effect on later driving outcomes.
gJvWSNcUtw.method: DynaChain treats question selection and action commitment as a closed-loop Markov decision process. A hybrid advantage combines episode driving outcomes with per-step rewards derived from benchmark scoring.
gJvWSNcUtw.key_idea: Train per-frame question selection and action commitment with a hybrid advantage combining trajectory outcomes and benchmark-derived step rewards.
gJvWSNcUtw.evidence: Bench2Drive-VL experiments compare fixed chains and two adaptive-reasoning methods, with question-selection ablations on the ten-route dev10 set.
gJvWSNcUtw.claimed_gains: Driving Score rises from 58.93 to 79.15 while the policy asks 2.52 questions per decision instead of seven.
gJvWSNcUtw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers support treating adaptive reasoning-question selection as a driving decision linked to subsequent outcomes.
gJvWSNcUtw.main_concern: A small dev10 evaluation, also used for model selection, provides insufficient independent evidence of stable generalization.

8Oe0tnlNgO.one_liner: Cycle-and-lead residual lookup plus a linear remainder predictor correct frozen time-series forecasts.
8Oe0tnlNgO.problem: Forecast errors contain recurring cycle- and horizon-dependent structure that existing post-hoc correctors leave partly unresolved.
8Oe0tnlNgO.method: LIRA pools historical residuals by target cycle position and forecast lead, then trains a channel-shared linear head on the remaining error. Online updates modify lookup statistics without further backbone calls or gradient optimization.
8Oe0tnlNgO.key_idea: Estimate recurring residuals with a cycle-position and forecast-lead lookup, then predict the remaining error with an input-conditioned linear head.
8Oe0tnlNgO.evidence: Experiments cover five task-specific backbones and four foundation models, with phase-shift controls, remainder-target ablations, and longer-lookback evaluations.
8Oe0tnlNgO.claimed_gains: With a 96-step lookback, online LIRA reduces average MSE by 8.77% on task-specific backbones and 24.43% on foundation models.
8Oe0tnlNgO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the simple frozen-model correction interface, consistent improvements, and gradient-free online updates.
8Oe0tnlNgO.main_concern: The comparisons do not fully separate the benefit of staged residual decomposition from extra calendar information or correction-model capacity.

CuyhJQQt6E.one_liner: Splits parameter-efficient adaptation into global and selective pathways to prevent feature collapse in multi-domain forensics.
CuyhJQQt6E.problem: Jointly training a single fake image detector across multiple forensic domains triggers asymmetric cross-domain gradient conflicts and collapses the learned artifact feature space.
CuyhJQQt6E.method: After analyzing cross-domain update interactions across forensic domains, the authors introduce Role-Specialized Global-Selective Adaptation (RGSA) with two parallel adaptation pathways. A global pathway learns representations shared across all four domains while a selective pathway captures partially shared and domain-specific forgery artifacts.
CuyhJQQt6E.key_idea: Partition multi-domain adaptation capacity into a global all-domain pathway and a selective pathway tailored to partially shared and domain-specific artifacts.
CuyhJQQt6E.evidence: Evaluated under the four-domain unified protocol of OpenMMSec across four backbones against 23 baseline methods, accompanied by cross-domain gradient harm and LoRA-rank analyses.
CuyhJQQt6E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper provides a thorough empirical analysis of asymmetric cross-domain optimization conflicts and broad benchmark comparisons across backbones.
CuyhJQQt6E.main_concern: The mechanistic link between expert routing and true forgery traces versus domain distributions is unproven, gradient-conflict analysis overlaps with prior work, and specialist ensembles are not compared.

1mK4kKsUp1.one_liner: Transfers low-dimensional internal activation signatures across domains via cross-fitted predictor weighting for LLM reliability detection.
1mK4kKsUp1.problem: Internal-representation detectors for LLM hallucinations and reasoning errors require large domain-specific labeled datasets, limiting deployment in label-scarce target domains.
1mK4kKsUp1.method: AdaST extracts low-dimensional PCA-based representational signatures from internal activations in each source and target domain, then applies question-level cross-fitting to estimate convex combination weights over domain-specific predictors. The learned representational directions can also be applied for activation steering.
1mK4kKsUp1.key_idea: Extract low-dimensional domain activation signatures and combine source and target reliability predictors using cross-fitted aggregation weights adapted to target relevance.
1mK4kKsUp1.evidence: Supported by theoretical proofs of aggregation consistency and optimal weights, plus experiments across multiple hallucination and reasoning datasets on open-weight LLMs.
1mK4kKsUp1.claimed_gains: With 25 labeled questions in a new domain, adaptive transfer improves hallucination-detection AUROC by 7.8% and reasoning-step prediction AUROC by 7.7%.
1mK4kKsUp1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework addresses a practical few-label transfer problem for LLM reliability detection and transfers effectively across models and datasets.
1mK4kKsUp1.main_concern: Methodological novelty over established stacking and multi-source transfer is limited, and key design choices and simpler aggregation baselines are insufficiently ablated.

Ak7FXazIev.one_liner: Fine-tunes a vision-language model on hierarchical phase-step-action annotations for adaptive proactive procedural video assistance.
Ak7FXazIev.problem: Step-only supervision in proactive procedural assistance fails to capture fine-grained action completion cues, higher-level phase goals, and user-adjustable guidance granularity.
Ak7FXazIev.method: The authors construct ProactiveCoach-Instruct and ProactiveCoachBench with verbal guidance structured into phases, steps, and actions, and train ProactiveCoach—a single vision-language model that jointly predicts timing and guidance across all three hierarchy levels with adaptive granularity.
Ak7FXazIev.key_idea: Jointly supervise a vision-language model across hierarchical phase, step, and action levels to track procedural progress and adapt guidance granularity.
Ak7FXazIev.evidence: Evaluated on ProactiveCoachBench spanning 7.2K videos (1,452 hours across eight procedural sources including cooking, DIY, and household tasks) against step-only baselines.
Ak7FXazIev.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that structuring procedural assistance into a phase-step-action hierarchy is well motivated and supported by a substantial multi-domain video dataset and benchmark.
Ak7FXazIev.main_concern: Anchor-based evaluation confounds hierarchical learning gains by giving the multi-level model ground-truth action history unavailable to step-only baselines, without end-to-end streaming latency tests.

xNpP2u99zY.one_liner: Feeds forward-operator and physics residuals back into a shared conditional diffusion denoiser during inverse-problem sampling.
xNpP2u99zY.problem: Standard conditional diffusion models do not verify forward-operator measurement consistency, whereas plug-and-play posterior samplers require costly test-time differentiation through operators and denoisers.
xNpP2u99zY.method: At each sampling step, the denoiser predicts a clean estimate, evaluates the forward measurement residual and optional governing-equation physics residual, and passes those residuals back into the same denoiser on a second pass. The network is trained with the standard denoising objective without backpropagating through the forward operator or sampling chain.
xNpP2u99zY.key_idea: Condition a two-pass diffusion denoiser on forward-operator and PDE residuals computed from its own clean prediction without differentiating through the operator.
xNpP2u99zY.evidence: Evaluated on six underdetermined inverse problems: three radiograph-conditioned compressible-flow benchmarks, compressed-sensing MRI, sparse-view CT, and inverse scattering, matched by network function evaluations.
xNpP2u99zY.claimed_gains: Against the same conditional model at an equal number of network evaluations, residual feedback reduces reconstruction error by 6–50%.
xNpP2u99zY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the gradient-free two-pass residual conditioning is simple and yields consistent NFE-matched error reductions across six diverse inverse problems.
xNpP2u99zY.main_concern: Iterative residual conditioning is incremental relative to recurrent inference machines and prior residual-conditioned diffusion methods, and supervised training requires retraining for new measurement operators.

RBnIugC2ZF.one_liner: Ranks variational quantum circuit parameters via SPSA estimates and applies parameter-shift evaluations to top coordinates.
RBnIugC2ZF.problem: Training variational quantum circuits faces a measurement bottleneck between exact parameter-shift rules with linear dimension cost and low-cost SPSA estimators with high variance.
RBnIugC2ZF.method: The authors formalize gradient-energy sparsity from causal-cone, commutation, and response-decay properties of quantum circuits. SGIQ averages initial SPSA estimates to rank parameter coordinates, computes exact parameter-shift rule gradients only for the selected top-k coordinates, and retains SPSA estimates for the remaining parameters.
RBnIugC2ZF.key_idea: Rank circuit parameters using averaged SPSA probes and selectively replace only the highest-magnitude coordinate estimates with exact parameter-shift rule gradients.
RBnIugC2ZF.evidence: Supported by theoretical conditions for gradient-energy sparsity and simulation experiments reported on circuit sizes up to 60 qubits across regression and classification tasks.
RBnIugC2ZF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that dynamically allocating exact parameter-shift evaluations to high-energy gradient coordinates based on SPSA screening is a clear and reasonable cost-accuracy trade-off.
RBnIugC2ZF.main_concern: Empirical validation relies heavily on small synthetic circuits where sparsity holds by construction, relies on restrictive local-observable and noise-independence assumptions, and requires manual hyperparameter selection.

d718wOnVjU.one_liner: Fine-tunes embodied vision-language models using prompts with confusable distractors and compact single-letter option targets.
d718wOnVjU.problem: Prior comparisons of multiple-choice versus open-ended fine-tuning for embodied vision-language models conflate input candidate information with output target formatting.
d718wOnVjU.method: Embodied Choice Tuning (ECT) curates 10,000 examples across eight embodied capabilities and 102 question types, placing confusable distractor options in the input while supervising only a compact option letter. Using identical visual inputs and answers, the authors construct four controlled supervision formats to isolate candidate presence, distractor semantics, and target form.
d718wOnVjU.key_idea: Include semantically confusable candidate distractors in the fine-tuning prompt while supervising a compact option-letter target to improve task transfer.
d718wOnVjU.evidence: Evaluated across three VLM families on nine native-format benchmarks in Embodied Arena using four controlled supervision variants trained on 10,000 examples.
d718wOnVjU.claimed_gains: On Qwen3.5-4B, ECT achieves an aggregate gain of 3.89 points over the base model and 2.27 points over open-ended supervision.
d718wOnVjU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the four-variant experimental setup cleanly isolates candidate input availability, distractor semantics, and target format across diverse embodied benchmarks.
d718wOnVjU.main_concern: Methodological novelty over standard multiple-choice tuning with hard distractors is limited, and gains from letter targets are not disentangled from sequence-length and token-weighting effects.

EEkOYuwcxU.one_liner: Disentangles WiFi CSI signal patterns from noise using asymmetric key-value cross-attention and Kronecker spatial priors.
EEkOYuwcxU.problem: Hardware impairments and environmental noise in raw WiFi Channel State Information cause deep networks to learn spurious features that fail to transfer across domains.
EEkOYuwcxU.method: KronDPBL uses distribution-guided and asymmetric attention that keeps noise representations in the keys for contrastive similarity while suppressing them in the values to synthesize clean pattern embeddings. It combines Kronecker-sum spatial encoding, a low-rank reconstruction loss, and dual contrastive objectives under fold-wise self-supervised pretraining.
EEkOYuwcxU.key_idea: Retain noise features in attention keys while suppressing them in values, regularized by Kronecker-sum spatial encoding and dual pattern-noise contrastive losses.
EEkOYuwcxU.evidence: Evaluated with frozen encoders under a fold-wise pretraining protocol across six WiFi CSI datasets and four downstream sensing task types.
EEkOYuwcxU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the asymmetric key-value architecture with Kronecker spatial structure is well motivated for noisy WiFi CSI and thoroughly evaluated under leak-free fold-wise pretraining.
EEkOYuwcxU.main_concern: The dual contrastive objective does not guarantee true semantic disentanglement of physical signal and noise, since aligning corrupted views of the same segment preserves segment-specific signal.

3i4lkzke7g.one_liner: Pretrains motor EEG encoders without labels by conditioning future egocentric video prediction on EEG latents.
3i4lkzke7g.problem: Motor EEG decoding methods rely on costly cue-based trials with coarse discrete labels or self-supervised objectives disconnected from continuous movement dynamics.
3i4lkzke7g.method: Mind World Model (MWM) encodes EEG up to the current timestep with a Lateralization-Aware Transformer (LAT) that uses soft-gated frame averaging across hemispheres, then treats the EEG embedding as a latent action in a world model to predict future egocentric video representations.
3i4lkzke7g.key_idea: Treat causal EEG embeddings from a hemisphere-averaging Transformer as latent actions that condition a world model to predict future egocentric visual representations.
3i4lkzke7g.evidence: Pretrained on naturalistic paired EEG and egocentric video without action annotations and evaluated across 9 motor classification and 7 regression tasks.
3i4lkzke7g.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using causal EEG windows to predict future egocentric visual features is a compelling annotation-free pretraining formulation evaluated across diverse motor-decoding benchmarks.
3i4lkzke7g.main_concern: LAT's soft-gated mirror operation is not a true involution so its claimed symmetry guarantees fail, and ablations show future-frame prediction adds much less than standard alignment and masking losses.

XqmsnQeWa0.one_liner: Public-threshold and index-private mechanisms characterize sample-privacy-utility tradeoffs for learned prophet inequalities.
XqmsnQeWa0.problem: Learning prophet inequalities from samples needs decision rules that protect individual training samples under differing release models.
XqmsnQeWa0.method: The paper studies public threshold mechanisms and index-private mechanisms that release only the selected element, deriving essentially tight sample-privacy-utility tradeoffs for both.
XqmsnQeWa0.key_idea: Derive matching sample, privacy, and utility bounds for public thresholds and for mechanisms releasing only the selected index.
XqmsnQeWa0.evidence: The support consists of theoretical upper and lower bounds for both privacy notions, with no experiments reported in the abstract or reviews.
XqmsnQeWa0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper gives clear, comprehensive theory with tight bounds for a new differential-privacy setting.
XqmsnQeWa0.main_concern: The main concern is limited algorithmic novelty and practical motivation despite the tight theoretical bounds.

pAdrEGpv2g.one_liner: A parameter-derived spectral basis orders features so nested prefixes retain information under compression.
pAdrEGpv2g.problem: Matryoshka Representation Learning lacks an explicit constraint ensuring that leading embedding prefixes form suitable compact encodings.
pAdrEGpv2g.method: SpecMRL reorganizes the feature space with a parameter-derived spectral basis ordered by feature importance, retaining standard MRL training but reading prefixes in spectral space.
pAdrEGpv2g.key_idea: Perform MRL prefix readout in a learned spectral basis ordered by feature importance.
pAdrEGpv2g.evidence: MTEB experiments compare reduced-dimensional SpecMRL with MRL, with reviews also noting multiple Qwen and Llama backbones and readout controls.
pAdrEGpv2g.claimed_gains: SpecMRL outperforms MRL at all evaluated reduced dimensions and surpasses full-dimensional MRL with only half the embedding dimensions.
pAdrEGpv2g.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the simple drop-in spectral reorganization improves compressed embeddings and that readout controls support its motivation.
pAdrEGpv2g.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite limited reliability and scope, including single-seed runs, small models, and unevaluated memory overhead.

SI6gzRExOb.one_liner: Kronecker-fitted Fisher curvature turns sub-1-bit NanoQuant updates into Sylvester-equation solves.
SI6gzRExOb.problem: NanoQuant's diagonal reconstruction geometry omits dense curvature information for sub-1-bit post-training quantization.
SI6gzRExOb.method: ShamAN-Q fits a Kronecker product to a calibration set's empirical Fisher by KL minimization, forms a Mahalanobis reconstruction loss, refreshes layer-local statistics, and redistributes rank across layers.
SI6gzRExOb.key_idea: Replace NanoQuant's diagonal reconstruction metric with a layer-local Kronecker approximation to empirical Fisher curvature.
SI6gzRExOb.evidence: Qwen3-Base models at 0.6B, 1.7B, and 4B are evaluated on WikiText-2 perplexity and Eleuther LM Evaluation Harness zero-shot reasoning.
SI6gzRExOb.claimed_gains: At ≈1 bpw, WikiText-2 perplexity falls from 27.56 to 22.96 (0.6B), 19.21 to 16.72 (1.7B), and 14.29 to 13.80 (4B); at ≈0.8 bpw, 0.6B matches NanoQuant at ≈1.0 bpw.
SI6gzRExOb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the curvature adaptation is technically well motivated and produces meaningful perplexity improvements at matched storage budgets.
SI6gzRExOb.main_concern: Reviewers most often say the ablations do not isolate dense curvature from rank allocation, refresh schedules, and tempering.

AGNtnbZFlM.one_liner: Collection-matched task updates and imagined value gradients coordinate online multi-task reinforcement learning.
AGNtnbZFlM.problem: Updating every task at a fixed frequency inflates task-wise update-to-data ratios as online multi-task training adds tasks.
AGNtnbZFlM.method: WAM-MTRL-VE shares a task-conditioned representation between an actor and ensemble world model, backpropagates short imagined reward gradients to the actor, and samples replay-ready tasks using collection weights.
AGNtnbZFlM.key_idea: Sample each replay-ready task for optimization with its data-collection probability while training the actor through short imagined rollouts.
AGNtnbZFlM.evidence: From-scratch online experiments on Meta-World MT10 and MT50 include controlled ablations of collection-matched updates and actor-side value expansion.
AGNtnbZFlM.claimed_gains: WAM-MTRL-VE achieves 96.2%±1.6% success on MT10 and 86.6%±2.0% on MT50 after 1M and 15M total environment interactions per run, respectively.
AGNtnbZFlM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the update-to-data mismatch is clearly identified and that targeted schedule comparisons support the optimization strategy.
AGNtnbZFlM.main_concern: All reviewers question the single MT50 training run and evaluation-only variance, which leave training robustness unresolved.

T3VAseIUpu.one_liner: Exogenous-variable conditioning, consistency regularization, and counterfactual imagination deconfound world-model dynamics.
T3VAseIUpu.problem: Observational world models can conflate actions with unobserved physical factors that remain fixed within episodes but vary across them.
T3VAseIUpu.method: CausalDream infers exogenous variables from a short probe using a label-supervised estimator, reconstructs their estimates from latent trajectories, and intervenes on the first imagined action while holding estimates fixed.
T3VAseIUpu.key_idea: Hold inferred exogenous physical factors fixed while intervening on imagined actions and regularizing latent trajectories to retain those estimates.
T3VAseIUpu.evidence: Eight DeepMind Control tasks compare learning AUC against an architecture-matched context baseline, with action-intervention prediction assessed on four tasks.
T3VAseIUpu.claimed_gains: CausalDream achieves the highest aggregate learning AUC among compared methods, 12.9% above an architecture-matched baseline using the same estimates without causal components.
T3VAseIUpu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the architecture-matched ContextDream comparison usefully tests the additions beyond context conditioning across several tasks.
T3VAseIUpu.main_concern: Reviewers most often question reliance on simulator-provided physical labels and whether the results demonstrate deconfounding rather than context conditioning.

Fz31P9pi9Q.one_liner: Concrete-score Gibbs correctors accelerate uniform-rate discrete diffusion without extra training.
Fz31P9pi9Q.problem: Uniform-rate discrete diffusion often needs many sampling steps, while accelerators require extra training or mix slowly.
Fz31P9pi9Q.method: GADD constructs Gibbs posterior likelihoods directly from concrete scores and adds corrector steps without training beyond standard score estimation.
Fz31P9pi9Q.key_idea: Convert concrete scores into Gibbs posterior likelihoods for corrector steps without learning additional quantities.
Fz31P9pi9Q.evidence: Theory establishes sampling-complexity bounds, while experiments cover synthetic data, zero-shot text sampling, and zero-shot conditional music generation against Euler and CTMC correctors.
Fz31P9pi9Q.claimed_gains: GADD achieves an overall sampling complexity of O(polylog(ε⁻¹)) and consistently improves sample quality and wall-clock efficiency over standard baselines.
Fz31P9pi9Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that score-derived correction without extra training is useful and supported by convergence analysis and experiments.
Fz31P9pi9Q.main_concern: Reviewers most often question the unquantified spectral-gap assumption underlying the polylogarithmic guarantee and its relevance to the evaluated domains.

yDXuMhMb0J.one_liner: Dynamic swap maintenance preserves constant-factor (k,z)-clustering as metric distances decrease.
yDXuMhMb0J.problem: Local-search clustering repeatedly pays a high cost to find improving swaps when metric distances change.
yDXuMhMb0J.method: A deterministic data structure maintains the best improving swap in O(n log n) per distance decrease and supports a constant-factor approximation with Õ(kn²) total update time.
yDXuMhMb0J.key_idea: Maintain the best improving center swap incrementally under distance decreases instead of rebuilding the swap table.
yDXuMhMb0J.evidence: Theoretical runtime and approximation guarantees are tested on metric spaces from two evolving graphs with up to 55,000 vertices.
yDXuMhMb0J.claimed_gains: The algorithm handles 1,000 edge insertions in about 10 s versus roughly 5,100 s for warm start, matching full-recomputation quality within 0.25 percent.
yDXuMhMb0J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the deterministic total-time bound is a clean theoretical result matching static local search up to lower-order terms.
yDXuMhMb0J.main_concern: Reviewers most often question practical scope because only distance decreases are supported and dynamic all-pairs shortest-path costs are excluded.

NIg25rWhip.one_liner: Condition-dependent factorized Koopman transitions distill multistep diffusion control into one forward pass.
NIg25rWhip.problem: Iterative diffusion-policy denoising introduces latency that constrains real-time closed-loop robot control.
NIg25rWhip.method: DNK lifts noisy trajectories into a latent space where a Factorized Dynamic Koopman layer applies a condition-dependent linear transition for one-step generation from observations and noise.
NIg25rWhip.key_idea: Parameterize a context-dependent latent linear operator whose factorized eigenvalues map noisy trajectories to denoised actions in one pass.
NIg25rWhip.evidence: Benchmarks span locomotion, state-based and image-based manipulation, long-horizon tasks, and a physical Kinova hardware experiment.
NIg25rWhip.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that DNK offers a strong performance-efficiency tradeoff and that intuitive context-dependent transitions receive useful ablation support.
NIg25rWhip.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite missing matched one-step comparisons and ablations, leaving the specific benefit of Koopman parameterization unclear.

FqFI5YnTqO.one_liner: Dual co-state dynamics enforce nonlinear generation constraints without per-step projections or optimization subproblems.
FqFI5YnTqO.problem: Flow-matching applications need nonlinear inference-time constraints, but projection and optimization alternatives can be expensive.
FqFI5YnTqO.method: Lagrangian Dual Flows evolve a dual co-state alongside generated samples, connecting constrained flow matching with primal-dual optimization while avoiding denoising-time projections and pseudoinverses.
FqFI5YnTqO.key_idea: Augment the flow ODE with Lagrangian dual dynamics that drive generated samples toward nonlinear constraint satisfaction.
FqFI5YnTqO.evidence: Convergence analyses for equality and inequality constraints accompany experiments on synthetic data, MNIST inpainting, and robotic trajectory tasks.
FqFI5YnTqO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the primal-dual connection is clear, avoids costly per-step solves, and shows promising runtime and constraint results.
FqFI5YnTqO.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite limited scalability evidence and evaluation focused on constraint violation rather than sample-distribution quality.

pO8K4TsVIv.one_liner: Nested time and note decoders autoregressively model symbolic music with harmonic-plan guidance.
pO8K4TsVIv.problem: Flattened autoregressive music models lose explicit two-dimensional structure, while fixed-grid non-autoregressive models limit variable-length generation.
pO8K4TsVIv.method: DID's time decoder maintains running musical history and its note decoder generates events from that memory, with harmonic Plan tokens acting as soft constraints on following notes.
pO8K4TsVIv.key_idea: Factor generation into a time decoder maintaining musical history and a note decoder conditioned on that memory.
pO8K4TsVIv.evidence: Multiple public datasets evaluate harmonic and rhythmic coherence, variable-length continuation, chord-conditioned piano generation, and accompaniment generation.
pO8K4TsVIv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the nested architecture captures musical dependencies at multiple scales and that harmonic planning provides useful guidance.
pO8K4TsVIv.main_concern: Reviewers most often question its distinction from hierarchical 1D autoregressive models and whether modest ablation gains justify the architecture.

RVyU6VMNEF.one_liner: Implements exact translation of binary-classification hard-attention transformers and input-specific sufficient reasons into Linear Temporal Logic.
RVyU6VMNEF.problem: Theoretical encodings of hard-attention transformers (HATs) into Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) for formal verification have not been practically implemented.
RVyU6VMNEF.method: The authors formulate an exact encoding of single-head hard-attention transformers (without masking or positional encodings) into LTL with past operators, alongside an encoding of input-specific sufficient-reason formulas, and implement both.
RVyU6VMNEF.key_idea: Translates trained hard-attention transformers and per-input sufficient-reason certificates into exact Linear Temporal Logic formulas with past operators.
RVyU6VMNEF.evidence: Implemented and tested on synthetic sequence classification tasks and the balanced parenthesis problem.
RVyU6VMNEF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that implementing exact LTL formula extraction from transformers for the first time is interesting and mathematically rigorous.
RVyU6VMNEF.main_concern: Reviewers highlight severe formula blowup (10^10 to 10^11 symbols even on small models), a very restrictive HAT architecture, and limited theoretical novelty over Yang et al. (2024).

ghGpYhzy61.one_liner: Aligns multi-view latent displacements across synchronized viewpoints before learning action-conditioned residual dynamics for robot manipulation.
ghGpYhzy61.problem: Multi-view world models that only align static state representations fail to guarantee consistent finite-horizon action displacements across viewpoints.
ghGpYhzy61.method: TAM-WM trains a shared visual coordinate in Stage A by aligning action-induced displacements across synchronized views, freezes it in Stage B to learn state- and action-conditioned residual dynamics, and uses an online correction teacher to score and selectively adjust nominal policy actions.
ghGpYhzy61.key_idea: Decouples representation learning into cross-view transition-displacement alignment followed by frozen-coordinate residual dynamics for candidate action scoring.
ghGpYhzy61.evidence: Evaluated on eight simulated robot manipulation tasks and Can PH with fixed-capacity transition-alignment ablations.
ghGpYhzy61.claimed_gains: Achieves 75.8% average success across eight simulated manipulation tasks (per TL;DR).
ghGpYhzy61.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing transition alignment from static state alignment is meaningful and supported by controlled ablations on demonstrated-action ranking.
ghGpYhzy61.main_concern: Reviewers note that closed-loop gains are intertwined with an elaborate downstream correction pipeline, physical-ranking metrics and tie-handling need clarification, and Delta Match directly reflects the Stage A training loss.

v1ghWLv5IN.one_liner: Enforces constraints in frozen flow-matching models via closed-form adjoint trajectory perturbations at adaptively chosen intervention times.
v1ghWLv5IN.problem: Constrained sampling methods for flow-matching models often displace generated samples far from the pretrained data distribution.
v1ghWLv5IN.method: MintFlow computes a closed-form minimal perturbation of an intermediate flow state via an adjoint formulation so subsequent evolution under the frozen flow field satisfies the constraint, while adaptively selecting the intervention time to balance perturbation size and flow amplification.
v1ghWLv5IN.key_idea: Uses a closed-form adjoint minimum-norm state perturbation at an adaptively selected flow time to satisfy constraints while staying close to the pretrained trajectory.
v1ghWLv5IN.evidence: Evaluated across multiple pretrained models, generative vision tasks, and physical system modeling with linear and nonlinear constraints.
v1ghWLv5IN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that MintFlow's adjoint minimal-intervention formulation is mathematically clear, training-free, and broadly evaluated across vision and physics tasks.
v1ghWLv5IN.main_concern: Reviewers flag inconsistencies between reported W2^2 and FID values, note that the Wasserstein bound does not guarantee exact conditional sampling, and question the reliance on rectified/one-step extrapolation.

6d5I2eeSHo.one_liner: Derives the Interval Denoiser target for Pixel MeanFlow from the flow-matching ODE and trains it with residual clipping and an interval curriculum.
6d5I2eeSHo.problem: The exact target and stop-gradient behavior of Pixel MeanFlow (pMF) and its instability on wide time intervals are not theoretically characterized.
6d5I2eeSHo.method: The authors derive the Interval Denoiser from the flow-matching ODE, showing it averages instantaneous denoising estimates and recovers Consistency Trajectory Models; for pixel Interval Denoiser (pID), they analyze stop-gradient placement and introduce residual clipping plus a wide-interval time-sampling curriculum.
6d5I2eeSHo.key_idea: Identifies the Interval Denoiser as the ODE-derived target of Pixel MeanFlow and stabilizes wide-interval training via residual clipping and a two-phase time-sampling curriculum.
6d5I2eeSHo.evidence: Evaluated on ImageNet 256x256 in pixel space using B/16 (160 and 320 epochs) and L/16 models without perceptual losses.
6d5I2eeSHo.claimed_gains: On ImageNet 256x256 (160 epochs, B/16), the interval curriculum lowers 1-step FID from 9.34 to 7.06 for pMF and 9.25 to 7.55 for pID; pID-L/16 achieves 1-step FID 4.55 and 2-step FID 3.98.
6d5I2eeSHo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that deriving the Interval Denoiser clarifies the theoretical link between Pixel MeanFlow, stop-gradient placement, and Consistency Trajectory Models.
6d5I2eeSHo.main_concern: All three reviewers note that pID and pMF perform nearly identically under a matched static sampler (9.25 vs 9.34 FID) and that pMF is not evaluated under the same curriculum/clipping recipe at 320 epochs.

m4Y8MgYnjy.one_liner: Removes immediate zero-lag sharpness feedback from momentum-based SAM to isolate historical momentum-routed sharpness corrections.
m4Y8MgYnjy.problem: In momentum-based Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM), sharpness corrections act both immediately and through momentum, leaving unclear whether immediate action is necessary.
m4Y8MgYnjy.method: Temporal Feedback SAM (TF-SAM) removes the zero-lag sharpness correction from the current parameter update while retaining its generation and delayed propagation through the momentum buffer.
m4Y8MgYnjy.key_idea: Suppresses zero-lag sharpness feedback while keeping sharpness corrections in momentum to test whether immediate application is needed.
m4Y8MgYnjy.evidence: Derives exact iterate identities, first-order alignment criteria, and local stability polynomials, and evaluates across image and text classification and corruption benchmarks.
m4Y8MgYnjy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling sharpness correction generation from immediate vs. delayed application is a clean, testable perspective with sound local analysis.
m4Y8MgYnjy.main_concern: TF-SAM performs similarly to M-SAM without consistent gains or global convergence guarantees, and summary robustness tables appear inconsistent with detailed tables.

ZFM5ol21aL.one_liner: Composes embodiment, interaction, and scene edits on robot demonstrations and egocentric videos while maintaining observation-action consistency.
ZFM5ol21aL.problem: Imitation learning suffers from costly demonstration collection and limited diversity, while composing multiple data augmentations risks breaking task-relevant contact and action consistency.
ZFM5ol21aL.method: WorldZoo coordinates embodiment retargeting, visual editing, and trajectory adaptation across robot demonstrations and human egocentric videos, using UniAug to compose edits along embodiment, interaction, and scene dimensions within each sample.
ZFM5ol21aL.key_idea: Applies feasibility-checked embodiment retargeting, object contact adaptation, and visual editing jointly so augmented observations remain aligned with adapted action trajectories.
ZFM5ol21aL.evidence: Evaluated on extended robotic simulation benchmarks and real-robot experiments across policies including pi 0.5 and LingBot-VLA.
ZFM5ol21aL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate that WorldZoo preserves observation-action alignment across diverse data sources and provides insightful perturbation analyses.
ZFM5ol21aL.main_concern: Reviewers point out limited technical novelty from integrating existing models, missing compute-cost analysis, weak baselines, and unequal-budget controls for UniAug.

gZ2q4NB4rw.one_liner: Whitens shared LoRA right factors by private left-factor Gram matrices and aggregates them via truncated server SVD.
gZ2q4NB4rw.problem: Averaging shared LoRA right factors in personalized federated learning fails to recover the average update because client left factors induce arbitrary factorizations.
gZ2q4NB4rw.method: In PERSIA, each client whitens its shared right factor using the Gram matrix of its private left factor before uploading, and the server recovers a shared rank-r right subspace via truncated SVD.
gZ2q4NB4rw.key_idea: Pre-whitens client right factors with private left-factor Gram matrices so server-side truncated SVD minimizes reconstruction error invariantly to equivalent LoRA factorizations.
gZ2q4NB4rw.evidence: Proven theoretically via reconstruction optimality and factor-stationarity bounds, and evaluated on GLUE with RoBERTa-Large.
gZ2q4NB4rw.claimed_gains: On GLUE with RoBERTa-Large after a 1280-step local phase, PERSIA reaches 91.1% accuracy versus 90.8% local, while factor averaging loses 4.1 points and two-factor FedAvg loses 11.3 points, at half the upload cost of two-factor sharing.
gZ2q4NB4rw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper identifies a genuine coordinate-misalignment issue in one-sided federated LoRA and provides a principled, theoretically grounded aggregation rule.
gZ2q4NB4rw.main_concern: Reviewers note that post-aggregation accuracy gains largely vanish after subsequent training rounds, leaving final accuracy similar to baselines and local training.

Hd0xBKO3Nq.one_liner: Weights on-policy distillation by teacher visual sensitivity and filters rollouts where the student already beats the teacher.
Hd0xBKO3Nq.problem: Standard on-policy distillation for medical VLMs overlooks student visual misallocation and overwrites student rollouts that already outperform the teacher.
Hd0xBKO3Nq.method: VITAL combines Visual Advantage Policy optimization (VAP), which scales token-level distillation weights using teacher probability shifts under image perturbations, with Task Advantage Distillation (TAD), which rejects rollouts lacking positive teacher task advantage.
Hd0xBKO3Nq.key_idea: Scales token distillation by teacher sensitivity to image perturbations while filtering out student rollouts without positive teacher task advantage.
Hd0xBKO3Nq.evidence: Experiments across four adult and neonatal medical diagnosis datasets using Qwen3-VL-8B as teacher and Qwen3-VL-2B as student.
Hd0xBKO3Nq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the clean diagnosis of visual and task deficits in medical VLM distillation and the structured decomposition.
Hd0xBKO3Nq.main_concern: Reviewers raise limited novelty over prior visual-advantage OPD (Med-OPD), missing Med-OPD + TAD ablations, single teacher-student pair evaluation, and potential conflict between VAP and TAD.

j5AZJxZQp1.one_liner: Introduces StructVista, a 419-figure benchmark evaluating MLLMs and tool agents on local, explicit, and implicit molecular assembly reconstruction.
j5AZJxZQp1.problem: Existing chemical structure benchmarks test isolated crops rather than reconstructing full multi-compound figures requiring implicit visual assembly reasoning.
j5AZJxZQp1.method: StructVista curates 419 expert-verified figures and 3,412 identifier-structure pairs from scientific articles across three levels: local recognition (L1), explicit global instantiation (L2), and implicit assembly relations (L3). They formalize structural roles, replacement scopes, attachment correspondences, and shared interfaces, evaluating direct MLLMs and tool-using agents.
j5AZJxZQp1.key_idea: Stratifies full-figure molecular reconstruction into local recognition, explicit instantiation, and implicit context-dependent assembly reasoning across 419 expert-verified figures.
j5AZJxZQp1.evidence: Evaluated seven direct MLLMs and two tool-equipped agent frameworks (including Codex) on the 419 figures and 3,412 targets.
j5AZJxZQp1.claimed_gains: Direct GPT-6 Sol scores 50.8 F1 (26.5% exact figure recovery) versus 89.2 F1 (74.9%) in Codex, drops from 55.53 (L1) to 34.35 F1 (L3) on shared targets, and chemistry tools add 4.8 F1 overall.
j5AZJxZQp1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the expert-verified curation of full scientific figures and the underexplored L3 context-dependent assembly formulation.
j5AZJxZQp1.main_concern: Reviewers note the paper offers no new reconstruction method, lacks L3 relation-type breakdowns or human baselines, and shrinks the L3 gap to ~4% after target-count standardization.

r6TrdHnMIZ.one_liner: Selects active permutation elements, fits a Merge-kernel GP surrogate, and reconstructs full permutations via structure-aware fill-in.
r6TrdHnMIZ.problem: Claims that vanilla Bayesian optimization suffices in high dimensions overlook discrete combinatorial permutation spaces under tight evaluation budgets.
r6TrdHnMIZ.method: VaPBO performs variable selection over permutation elements, fits a Merge-kernel Gaussian process on active sub-permutations, and reconstructs full permutations using structure-aware fill-in and greedy local search.
r6TrdHnMIZ.key_idea: Combines permutation variable selection, a Merge-kernel GP surrogate on active sub-permutations, and structure-aware fill-in reconstruction.
r6TrdHnMIZ.evidence: Experiments on classical combinatorial problems, chip placement, and biodiversity history reconstruction with and without GP guidance.
r6TrdHnMIZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find high-dimensional Bayesian optimization over permutation spaces well-motivated and appreciate the honest ablation splitting GP-guided and GP-free variants.
r6TrdHnMIZ.main_concern: Reviewers challenge the distance-concentration argument in Figure 1, note only the Merge kernel is tested, and flag a potential bug in the released code instantiating fill-in outside the seed loop.

VS4QRFrhyt.one_liner: Adds a Thinker role and iteration-dependent reward mixing to Questioner-Solver self-evolution for long-horizon LLM training.
VS4QRFrhyt.problem: Zero-data LLM self-evolution frameworks stagnate and degrade after a few iterations as majority-vote reward accuracy declines.
VS4QRFrhyt.method: Zero-L initializes Questioner, Solver, and Thinker roles from one base LLM, where the Thinker scores Solver reasoning traces by embedding similarity and an iteration-dependent policy mixes Solver and Thinker rewards.
VS4QRFrhyt.key_idea: Introduces a third Thinker role that scores reasoning-trace representations and mixes its process reward with Solver rewards over iterations.
VS4QRFrhyt.evidence: 12-round self-evolution experiments on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B across mathematical and general reasoning benchmarks over three seeds.
VS4QRFrhyt.claimed_gains: At 12 iterations on Qwen3-4B/8B, mathematical averages exceed R-Zero by 2.94 and 2.98 percentage points (from review).
VS4QRFrhyt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that preventing stagnation in multi-round zero-data self-evolution without external verifiers is an important problem.
VS4QRFrhyt.main_concern: Reviewers note that the Thinker reward reduces to centroid proximity calibrated on majority votes, freezes early, lacks ablation removing it, and compares only against R-Zero.

N06RTPfhCQ.one_liner: Quantizes 2-bit LLMs using a finite 16-dimensional Barnes-Wall lattice codec and residual-preserving QAT initialization.
N06RTPfhCQ.problem: Most 2-bit quantization-aware training (QAT) methods focus on optimization recipes while overlooking the choice of underlying discrete weight representation.
N06RTPfhCQ.method: BW-QAT encodes every 16 weights into a fixed 32-bit payload using a finite Barnes-Wall (BW16) lattice with a dynamic-programming codec, calibrated gain alphabet, and compensated pre-quantization proxy initialization.
N06RTPfhCQ.key_idea: Represent 16-weight blocks on a finite 2-bit-per-weight Barnes-Wall lattice with an exact dynamic-programming codec and decision-preserving proxy initialization.
N06RTPfhCQ.evidence: Experiments compare BW-QAT against matched lattice, scalar-QAT, and vector-QAT baselines on Qwen and Llama models in low-data regimes.
N06RTPfhCQ.claimed_gains: On Qwen3-1.7B, BW-QAT improves six-task average accuracy from 52.17% to 58.30% over matched LC-QAT and reduces WikiText-2 perplexity from 18.90 to 14.02 across three seeds.
N06RTPfhCQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the finite BW16 dynamic-programming codec that avoids materializing a huge codebook and the strong low-data accuracy gains.
N06RTPfhCQ.main_concern: Reviewers point out ~14.5x higher training-time overhead than LC-QAT, missing inference-time decoding latency benchmarks, and incomplete isolation from initialization differences.

er5xZ7etzv.one_liner: Converts a frozen VLM into a unified understanding-and-generation model via hierarchical feature fusion and block-wise Mixture-of-Transformers.
er5xZ7etzv.problem: Unifying visual understanding and generation in one model often degrades understanding because the two tasks favor different visual representations.
er5xZ7etzv.method: Integral aggregates hierarchical features from a frozen VLM vision encoder via Abstraction Fusion to form shared visual tokens and adds a 0.89B generative stream interacting at block boundaries via Block-wise MoT.
er5xZ7etzv.key_idea: Fuse multi-layer features from a frozen VLM encoder into a shared visual space and attach a lightweight generative stream coupled at transformer block boundaries.
er5xZ7etzv.evidence: Evaluations span visual understanding, compositional and knowledge-intensive image generation, image editing, and FLUX.1-VAE latent controls.
er5xZ7etzv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate that Integral adds image generation with only 0.89B parameters while preserving nearly all of the frozen VLM's understanding performance.
er5xZ7etzv.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited novelty over prior multi-layer encoder fusion methods (e.g., RAEv2, DualToken) and missing comparisons against recent unified multimodal models.

MvYWN3jQrz.one_liner: Learns an RL context-selection policy for long-horizon agents driven by the executing LLM's internal attention signals.
MvYWN3jQrz.problem: Appending all observations in long-horizon agents causes context bloat and distractor-induced accuracy drops, while external relevance scorers ignore the executing LLM's internal signals.
MvYWN3jQrz.method: CURATE extracts internal attention-head and activation relevance signals from the frozen executing LLM and trains a lightweight context-selection policy via outcome-grounded reinforcement learning to decide which context passages to forward.
MvYWN3jQrz.key_idea: Trains an outcome-grounded RL context-curation policy using internal attention-head relevance features from the frozen executing LLM.
MvYWN3jQrz.evidence: Evaluated across four datasets (including LoCoMo and HotpotQA) and two model families against context-compression baselines.
MvYWN3jQrz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using internal LLM attention signals with RL for distractor-resistant context selection is well motivated and achieves strong accuracy-compression results.
MvYWN3jQrz.main_concern: Reviewers raise a critical concern about whether evaluation/probe questions are leaked during inference-time memory selection and note missing ablations isolating RL from attention heuristics.

A8VXqBzs74.one_liner: Repurposes pretrained tabular foundation models with architecture-aware readouts and contrastive post-training for dataset embeddings.
A8VXqBzs74.problem: Existing dataset representation methods rely on hand-crafted meta-features or task-specific encoders rather than leveraging pretrained tabular foundation models.
A8VXqBzs74.method: TabMF attaches an architecture-aware dataset-level readout to pretrained tabular foundation models (TabICLv2, TabPFN-2.5) and adapts them end-to-end via contrastive learning on stochastic views of synthetic datasets.
A8VXqBzs74.key_idea: Adapts pretrained tabular foundation models into dataset encoders using backbone-specific readouts and contrastive post-training over synthetic dataset views.
A8VXqBzs74.evidence: Evaluated across six dataset-level tasks (including retrieval, benchmark construction, and shift assessment) on unseen real datasets against meta-features, dedicated encoders, and frozen TFMs.
A8VXqBzs74.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea of repurposing tabular foundation models for dataset representations interesting and note strong empirical results.
